sent_emails.subject: RE: AgriProve - Key Commercial Terms Agreement Griffin CP1&2 (Wowan)
sent_emails.body: Hi Melanie, I am responding on behalf of Dylan. Thankyou for providing the proposed amendments. To clarify, while we do accept addendums in some cases, this is only where the amendments have no material impact on the commercial and compliance obligations for both parties under the agreement, such as a landholder/property specific biosecurity plan as an example. As such there are fundamental issues with the proposed addendum that we cannot accept. 1. AgriProve Fee: This is not negotiable. 1. Clause 14: This is not negotiable. Noting that Cl. 14 is specific to the circumstance where the Operator elects to terminate the agreement and the project, resulting in a requirement to relinquish any ACCUs issued. In this instance AgriProve as proponent must hand back 100% of ACCUs due to a decision to terminate made by the Operator, and therefore AgriProve does not bear the cost of re-sourcing the AgriProve fee ACCUs (25%) 1. Clause 20.1: This is not negotiable. 1. Clause 6: As proponent we are required to gain all required consents, and the projects will not be able to generate ACCUs until this is done, and therefore it is in the best interests of both parties to work collaboratively to ensure these consents are gained. AgriProve is happy to lead the engagement and administrative requirements as per Cl. 6.2 but may require input and introductions from the Landholder/Operator where appropriate. With this in mind, some further context as to why these amendments are sought would be appreciated. 1. Project Areas: The project areas are clearly defined in the Key Commercial Terms and the project area maps supplied. The agreements only pertain to the project areas shown, and not the entirety of the relevant titles. Once registered this can be verified against the ERF register. Regarding the GreenCollar projects, it is important to note that it is not possible to stack the Greencollar method type with soil carbon (they cannot be registered on the same area), and we have spent considerable time completing a detailed mapping process taking into account their proposed project areas to ensure the projects can co-exist. We will only register the areas agreed as per these maps. I note that this should also be a requirement for Greencollar, as if their applications are not restricted to their project areas (eg. whole land titles), this will render the area ineligible for soil carbon unless area variations are completed which will delay the projects commencing. We have made every attempt to ensure this is not the case to date. I would welcome the opportunity to further discuss any of the points raised above. sent_emails.subject: RE: AgriProve, Next Steps
sent_emails.body: Hi Finola, 1. The fundamental undertaking is that the land remain in an agricultural system for the term of the agreement. The specific restricted and activities not permitted are specified by the legislated method and were provided as attachments to the agreements provided previously but re-attached here. In terms of achieving outcomes, part of onboarding is a commitment that at least one of the eligible carbon building activities are implemented on farm. Looking at your records I understand that this is proposed to be a combination of altering stocking rates and pasture reestablishment/rejuvenation. For project registration we need to clearly establish that the intended management actions are new or materially different to what has been done in the 5 years prior to registration. For best outcomes it is important that the frequency, intensity, or duration of these activities is changed relative to the baseline management. Refer to s5-8 of our Master Terms and Conditions as relevant clauses. 2. This is not entirely accurate and depends on the scenario. BSR can discontinue at any point up until the point that ACCUs are issued to the project. A key decision point here is likely to be year 5. If no ACCUs have been issued by year 5, we are required to report to the regulator and incur sampling and audit costs for no return, so there may be no incentive for either party to continue at this point. If ACCUs have been issued to the project and BSR choose to terminate the agreement early for convenience and we need to revoke the project, AgriProve as project proponent will be required to return all ACCUs issued to the project to that point in time to the Clean Energy Regulator (CER). In this circumstance we require the operator (BSR) to return any ACCUs (or equivalent dollar value) to AgriProve so we can relinquish these to the CER. Refer to s10, 14, and 15 of the Master Terms and Conditions as relevant clauses. 3. Our model uses results obtained from our portfolio to date with factors applied for rainfall and enterprise type. It provides us with an indication of the project potential but is indicative only. As the method relies on physical measurement of soil organic carbon stocks, if the project achieves greater sequestration rates through successful management implementation, then this benefit is realised. 4. sent_emails.body: Hi Finola, Yes, I am the best person to handle enquiries from at this stage. I have attached some of our background information here which outlines the process. Regarding potential, our internal estimates indicate that the potential yield of the project would be 1.5 ACCUs/ha/year. Current ACCU pricing can be found here: https://coremarkets.co/resources/market-prices. This yield estimate factors in the climate and intended activity implementation on the project. I note that this is an estimate only, and actual sequestration rates will vary. To generate the ACCUs we need to re-sample within 5 years, and it is the measured increase in the soil organic carbon stocks relative to the baseline that allows us to apply for ACCUs. sent_emails.body: Hi Elliot, Good to catch up last week. Apologies for the delay in getting this back to you, I am still catching up after my disrupted week last week with illness in the household. To summarise our conversation, I believe there were three key clauses that remained a concern: 1. Market Adjustment Fee. In this instance your concern stems from the interpretation that this clause may allow us to raise our service fee (for example from 25% to 30%) and pass this on to all existing contracts. As discussed on the call, this was not the intent of the clause, which was designed to not disadvantage early adopters if we ended up reducing our service fee (for example from 25% to 20%). I note that Cl. 21.2 of the master Ts and Cs notes that amendments can only be passed on if they have a materially adverse effect on the landholder/operator. Notwithstanding, I am happy to provide clarification that this market adjustment fee will only occur in your favour (ie. a reduction in our service fee), as this is the original intent of the clause. 2. Risk of ACCU Relinquishment. As discussed, this is not a clause we can amend as it is a function of the regulation that we are working under. This clause arises due to the requirement that if the operator elects to terminate the agreement early and ACCUs have been issued to the project and we are then required to revoke the project with the CER, the CER in all likelihood will request that all ACCUs issued to the project are returned by the project proponent (AgriProve). In this instance where the termination is initiated by the operator AgriProve will request that these are sourced (or the equivalent value thereof) by the landholder/operator, as it is their breach of terms that has led to the relinquishment requirement in this instance. The key undertaking on the landholder/operator here is that the land remain in agricultural system for the 25 year project period to mitigate this risk. 3. Liability. Regarding the disclaimer of liability in Cl. 20.6, this is specific to instances where further decisions based on information we provide (such as decisions regarding whether to sell or hold ACCUs) are made by the landholder/operator, the outcomes of which we have no control over, such as a reduction in ACCU price. We would always recommend that independent advice is sought on such decisions. In terms of 20.6 (2), similarly, we cannot be liable for actions taken by a New Project Proponent (not AgriProve) where they are nominated by the operator as per Cl. 10, as we have no control over the actions of an independent entity in this scenario. This is not removing our liability for negligence or non-performance which is covered by Cl. 10 (the ability to remove AgriProve as proponent/agent if we are not performing), and more specifically Cl. 20.1 under which we are liable for the greater of $50k or an equivalent value to AgriProve’s 25% fee over the preceding 12-month period if we are found to be negligent etc. As above, I am unable to amend these clauses, but I believe the liability clauses provide adequate protection for both parties to this agreement, with the intent to ensure that both parties have an interest in ensuring the success of the project by virtue of the overall structure. sent_emails.body: Hi Deane, Some comments below: 1. We will amend and restate (ie replace) the current agreements between Corporate Carbon and the farmers and Corporate Carbon and RAF (“New Agreements”) - Agreed; new agreements also to replace Corporate Carbon with AgriProve. 2. The New Agreements will limit the application of the Projects to the contracted based-line trial areas (~10% of the total farm areas) - Agreed; new agreements will only relate to the registered project areas. All cases have now had area variations lodged and approved by the CER to limit the registered projects to the baselined area. 3. Similarly Corporate Carbon will remove any wording relating to ownership or rights over the Farmer’s soil carbon as currently appearing in the Participation Deed - Agreed; any reference to claim on ownership on landholders soil carbon will be removed. 4. The Farmers and RAF shall receive their respective proportion of verified ACCUs (following completion of the audit process) for T0-T1 (first 5 years) into their own ANREU accounts, to sell on the secondary market, hold as carbon offsets or otherwise, based on initial splits assuming ~$12/ACCU: a. 66.5% Farmers Agreed; 66.5% of ACCUs to landholder. Landholders are individually responsible for establishing ANREU accounts. b. 25% RAF c. 8.5% Agriprove (for them to deal with as they see fit) - Points b and c pertaining to the remaining 33.5% to be agreed between RAF and AgriProve based on work completed to date (refer to the attached spreadsheet) and CAC servicing obligations. 5. ACCUs generated and verified for T1-T2 (next 5 years of which we are already 2-3 years into) will be received by farmers into their own ANREU accounts in a proportion of 72.5-75%. The balance will be split between Agriprove and RAF which shall be determined following a clear and agreed definition of the respective roles and responsibilities of Agriprove and RAF for T1 -T2; this will occur during May. Farmers will deal solely with RAF (as the ‘Agent’) but some services may be provided by Agriprove to RAF. The details of the service and % allocation will be shared with farmers - Agreed in principle; please see attached breakdown of tasks and responsibilities for further discussion between RAF/AgriProve. 6. All audit costs for ACCU verification shall be borne by the individual farmers - Agreed; the audit process will be managed by AgriProve and audit quotes provided to RAF for approval with landholders before progressing. 7. Following the conclusion of T2 and for T3 and beyond (at completion of 10 year ERF contract period plus), Agriprove will exit the Projects and the farmers will become their own project Proponents under regulation and RAF shall be appointed as Project Agents. At this time, the splits may be renegotiated between Farmers and RAF - Agreed; AgriProve to be removed as Proponent at year 10 and replaced with landholder, RAF to be registered as Agent. AgriProve have no further involvement in the projects after the proponent has been varied. 8. Upon acceptance of the ’New Agreements’ by all parties, the following steps will be undertaken prior to ACCU creation: a. The Novation of Project Proponent transferring from Corporate Carbon Australia to AgriProve; Agreed; AgriProve to manage proponency variation process once agreements are signed and AgriProve has legal right to do so. Note the assessment period can be a minimum of 3 months at the CER and we cannot initiate audit until this variation is approved. b. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. Can you please confirm that you are happy for us to come and resample your project areas within the period of May 5th – June 5th? Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. The attached factsheet has information regarding resampling process but if you have any other questions, please let me know. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. engagements.body: Hi Aude, I have just uploaded the data from the sampling to the Digify dataroom as below. Please let me know if there are any issues with access. [cid:image002.png@01DB1F2E.D9595A70] As an explainer, the 'McLachlan_Unique_S123' files are the raw field data as downloaded from Survey 123. The 'Sample_Exported_Data' files are the raw laboratory data (split across three reports). The 'McLachlan_Unique_Compiled file is a compilation of the field and lab data, linked by the sample barcodes. I have also included a 'Scenario' column here to indicate the 10 randomisation scenarios and the repeat of T0 and T1. This is split into individual tabs for the L1 and L2 data. Hopefully this is all relatively self-explanatory, but please don't hesitate to reach out if there are questions or if there is additional information we can provide. I am more than happy to jump on a call and walk this through if needed. @Aude CARRO could you please confirm details with regard to issuing an invoice for the work completed as agreed. This is not new or surprising. The mistake made is the conclusion that it is rainfall that is causing the increase in soil carbon sequestration. This confuses ‘necessary conditions’ with ‘causal actions’ * the paper uses a ‘normalised difference vegetation index’ model for their analysis which we believe over simplifies the rainfall-SOC nexus * the paper uses a sample size of n=1 (actually not even the entire project so n=0.05) to conclude that SOC levels reduce once rainfall reduces which is not conclusive * our portfolio includes multiple projects that have measured SOC declines in dry baseline and wet subsequent sampling rounds, and sequestered SOC in wet baseline and dry subsequent sampling rounds which is add odds with the central premise of this paper * suggested methodological changes are very academic and lack any real world ability to be implemented * importantly the paper also ignores the impact of management on ‘effective rainfall’ which is the amount of rainfall on a property, less the amount lost in runoff. (Note that we are developing a rating tool as part of our platform to assist landowners calculate their effective rainfall). Management action is the primary driver of effective rainfall. * How Agriprove will consider the outcome of Unique study (presentation scheduled on 16 January) We will use the outcomes of the Unique study to contribute to our continuous improvement of soil carbon project management and implement recommendations where possible to continue to optimise sampling processes – improving the confidence level of the statistical significance of measured results * this commitment to continuous improvement and actioning insights from the Unique study is evidenced through the implementation of preliminary findings into our operational processes. We now use a 4 x 4 sampling design (4 cores in 4 strata) as standard for all projects. This is designed to improve statistical confidence and is a change from the 3 x 3 configuration used as standard previously * we are also making use of our SOC model for optimised stratification to better capture soil variability. In general, where projects are listed as ‘Audit Pending’, we are awaiting unconditional declarations to be received (that is we have lodged the variations with the Regulator already). Receipt of the unconditional declaration is currently our trigger for audit. Anything under ‘Pre-Audit’ is working through eligible consent processes with third parties, where the timelines are harder to control, although we are now confident that they will come through with all the institutions we are currently dealing with (banks are required to provide their consent and this is becoming a business as usual activity). Regarding reduction in audit time, the other contributing factor is that for some of the upcoming engagements we are unertaking virtual site visits as a solution to remove the need for physical visits from the audit team. This theoretically should reduce time for audit completion as well as cost. We are working with the auditors to address their key risk areas. This is a longer term efficiency investment that will start to provide lower costs and earlier audit results. * What is planning to recover the delivery shortage of CMA1 and CMA2 to match contractual delivery schedule? CMA1 is on track for delivery according to schedule. CMA2 will have the shortfall roll over. We are confident of catching up the shortfall over the 24 months as project implementation catches up with some of the delays we experienced in completing the commercial module * When do you expect to issue the 7305 deferred ACCUs? At the November 2025 delivery date. The management question is to see how we could get the delivery schedule of CMA2 aligned with the M5 payment. engagements.body: Hi Finola, 1. The fundamental undertaking is that the land remain in an agricultural system for the term of the agreement. The specific restricted and activities not permitted are specified by the legislated method and were provided as attachments to the agreements provided previously but re-attached here. In terms of achieving outcomes, part of onboarding is a commitment that at least one of the eligible carbon building activities are implemented on farm. Looking at your records I understand that this is proposed to be a combination of altering stocking rates and pasture reestablishment/rejuvenation. For project registration we need to clearly establish that the intended management actions are new or materially different to what has been done in the 5 years prior to registration. For best outcomes it is important that the frequency, intensity, or duration of these activities is changed relative to the baseline management. Refer to s5-8 of our Master Terms and Conditions as relevant clauses. 2. This is not entirely accurate and depends on the scenario. BSR can discontinue at any point up until the point that ACCUs are issued to the project. A key decision point here is likely to be year 5. If no ACCUs have been issued by year 5, we are required to report to the regulator and incur sampling and audit costs for no return, so there may be no incentive for either party to continue at this point. If ACCUs have been issued to the project and BSR choose to terminate the agreement early for convenience and we need to revoke the project, AgriProve as project proponent will be required to return all ACCUs issued to the project to that point in time to the Clean Energy Regulator (CER). In this circumstance we require the operator (BSR) to return any ACCUs (or equivalent dollar value) to AgriProve so we can relinquish these to the CER. Refer to s10, 14, and 15 of the Master Terms and Conditions as relevant clauses. 3. Our model uses results obtained from our portfolio to date with factors applied for rainfall and enterprise type. It provides us with an indication of the project potential but is indicative only. As the method relies on physical measurement of soil organic carbon stocks, if the project achieves greater sequestration rates through successful management implementation, then this benefit is realised. 4. All re-sampling costs are absorbed in AgriProve's success fee. engagements.subject: Sampling Results - Nox 2024
engagements.body: Hi Ross, Please see attached the results from the last round of sampling completed on the two project areas. In summary: * Chifley Carbon Project is now 650 tC above the baseline carbon stock and has shown a consistent increasing trend since the sampling round completed in early 2023. This means we can go ahead and begin the process of reporting and applying for ACCUs for this project. * Daly Carbon Project is not above the baseline carbon stock to date however this project shows the same consistent increasing trend since the early 2023 sampling, with three of the 4 CEAs continuing to show gains since 2023. Overall I think these are really positive results. With regard to Chifley Carbon Project, before we can estimate the total ACCU yield we will need to do some work to estimate any emissions associated with the project period to feed into our calculations. I have copied Imogen Hickey to this email who is our crediting specialist, it would be great if we can arrange a time to jump on a video call to talk through the process from here and next steps to work toward lodging an application for ACCUs. Feel free to give me a call or otherwise let us know a time that might suit for a brief meeting. From: Ross Thompson Sent: Saturday, 7 June 2025 1:03 PM To: Kieren Whittock Subject: RE: Agriprove form for the CER Hi Kieren, I was wondering if it is possible that we could delay catching up on this until mid Spring? I feel you will have more chance of "cutting through" with me then, when I start heading into our slower time of year (Mid Spring til late Summer). As you know, I am pretty wound up with the CER and their demands and then the fact that "estimates" are OK. I just do not see how I can possibly justify loading up future generations with this burden. But I think, given all the work we have done up til now, I should listen carefully to you, and we should TRY to resolve it and move on. Rather than throwing the baby out with the bath water. No promises that you will be able to swing me around in my attitude. But if you can wait until I am more receptive, I think it gives us the best chance. What are your thoughts? If you are agreeable, have diarised to get in touch with you by email on October 1. I would simply be replying to your email below to get the ball rolling and set aside some time for us to work on it together as you suggested. Regards Ross From: Kieren Whittock > Sent: Friday, 28 March 2025 9:46 PM To: Ross Thompson > Subject: RE: Agriprove form for the CER Hi Ross, So having a look in some more detail here. As discussed we are trying to achieve two things with this information. 1. Show that at least one of the eligible activities has been implemented on the project area 2. Gather the data we need to quantify emissions associated with the project that feed into the calculations Regarding point 1, this is what we are trying to achieve with the Activity Log pages. What is important to note on these activities is that we only need to demonstrate that one of these has occurred, not all of them. As a starting point we could select one that may be the easiest to demonstrate, and only make reference to the others as complimentary activities without being required to demonstrate them in detail or provide detail that is difficult to obtain. From your notes it sounds like this may be achievable. Regarding point 2, if we put aside the stock numbers for the moment, we can strike a few things out from the start. I don't believe irrigation and landscape modification are relevant in your scenario and can be disregarded. That leaves the inputs, which it seems you have some records for, at least for total quantities which we will be able to work with. I also think residues will be able to be resolved given you are primarily a grazing operation and this section is more aimed at cropping operations. Regarding stock numbers, I think it would be worthwhile if we could jump on a quick call with Will at a time that suits you to ask some targeted questions that can help us better determine what can be done. Also, to clarify, the expectation is not for you to fill out the tables provided - we can do this work based on raw information provided, before cross-checking with you that we have interpreted correctly. As discussed, I would be more than happy to come and see you face to face, I could complete as much of this as I can on the fly while there - we have done this a few times previously and has b…

engagements.subject: National Carbon Farming Conference - Albury, 3–6 Nov
engagements.body: Hi Ross, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is coming up soon - it’s on 3–6 November in Albury. AgriProve will be there again this year. Our Chair, Matthew Warnken, is helping MC parts of the event, and we’re also co-sponsoring the Soil Carbon Day on the Tuesday. A few of us from the team will be around across the three days, so if you’re attending, it’d be great to catch up for a chat about your project or anything happening on farm. engagements.subject: National Carbon Farming Conference - Albury, 3–6 Nov
engagements.body: Hi Ross, Next week at the conference, AgriProve will be running a session (Wednesday 5th Nov) called: Project Ecosystem in Action: The Carbon Farming Value Chain It’s a practical look at how the different parts of the soil carbon value chain work together - from the producer and input suppliers to the technology side and the market. The idea is to show what’s actually happening on the ground and how soil carbon projects turn into real outcomes for producers and the broader market. If you’re coming along, it’d be great to see you there or have a chat at the stand afterwards. engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: Good Morning Ross, Thanks for sending those details through. We definitely haven't put it in the too hard basket - it just hasn't been an urgent priority up until now as it's coming up to the reporting period date. I will touch base with Kieren and have cc'ed him into this email to see what we can do. In terms of the record keeping - we would never expect you to guess, and it is a lot simpler than it sounds. Most of it is things that you would already have had to collect and would have given to your accountant eg. invoices for expenses such as seed and fertilizer, livestock numbers, fuel used ect. The main thing that the regulator needs is proof that you have changed practices in some way and that you have implemented what you said you would. They don't need extreme detail of every little thing that you have done on farm. If you would find it helpful, I can jump on a call with you and we can look at your map, go through what you've done on your project, what records you have, and put together a bit of a plan/list of what you need to proceed and get this done. Let me know and we can lock in a time to do that. Talk soon. If you need anything feel free to call me anytime. engagements.subject: AgriProve Soil Carbon Project Information
engagements.body: Hi Elliott, It was great to speak with you this afternoon about what you are looking to achieve on your property. Thanks for taking the time to discuss a carbon project with AgriProve today and I look forward to getting out to your farm as soon as possible. As discussed, I am sending through some documents for further information and a line of sight into the mapping stage of our process. Below I have outlined what each attachment is about to help you navigate them. 1. I have attached our FAQ document with some written answers to common questions that are asked. 2. Our next steps form is the Consent to Register, Commitment to Implement (CTR-CTI). This is the main one we need back from you to move forward. Once received, we can start gathering the background information required to register the projects and commence the mapping process in consultation with you. This document does not lock you into a project with us should you decide not to proceed. Based on our discussion I would recommend selecting 'Altering the stocking rate...' tick box for the eligible activity to be implemented but you might also like to consider 'Re-establishing or rejuvenating pasture...'. We typically recommend selecting only one or two eligible activities to start, and this can be updated in the future should you choose. 4. Also attached is our Universal Land Management Strategy that accompanies all AgriProve projects and details how they are managed and monitored. A land management strategy is required by the Clean Energy Regulator for all Carbon Projects registered with them. I am more than happy to talk you through these documents and discuss any questions that come up as a result. Feel free to reach out anytime. Looking forward to discussing further with you soon. engagements.subject: RE: Responses to Legal Review
engagements.body: Hi Elliot, Good to catch up last week. Apologies for the delay in getting this back to you, I am still catching up after my disrupted week last week with illness in the household. To summarise our conversation, I believe there were three key clauses that remained a concern: 1. Market Adjustment Fee. In this instance your concern stems from the interpretation that this clause may allow us to raise our service fee (for example from 25% to 30%) and pass this on to all existing contracts. As discussed on the call, this was not the intent of the clause, which was designed to not disadvantage early adopters if we ended up reducing our service fee (for example from 25% to 20%). I note that Cl. 21.2 of the master Ts and Cs notes that amendments can only be passed on if they have a materially adverse effect on the landholder/operator. Notwithstanding, I am happy to provide clarification that this market adjustment fee will only occur in your favour (ie. a reduction in our service fee), as this is the original intent of the clause. 2. Risk of ACCU Relinquishment. As discussed, this is not a clause we can amend as it is a function of the regulation that we are working under. This clause arises due to the requirement that if the operator elects to terminate the agreement early and ACCUs have been issued to the project and we are then required to revoke the project with the CER, the CER in all likelihood will request that all ACCUs issued to the project are returned by the project proponent (AgriProve). In this instance where the termination is initiated by the operator AgriProve will request that these are sourced (or the equivalent value thereof) by the landholder/operator, as it is their breach of terms that has led to the relinquishment requirement in this instance. The key undertaking on the landholder/operator here is that the land remain in agricultural system for the 25 year project period to mitigate this risk. 3. Liability. Regarding the disclaimer of liability in Cl. 20.6, this is specific to instances where further decisions based on information we provide (such as decisions regarding whether to sell or hold ACCUs) are made by the landholder/operator, the outcomes of which we have no control over, such as a reduction in ACCU price. We would always recommend that independent advice is sought on such decisions. In terms of 20.6 (2), similarly, we cannot be liable for actions taken by a New Project Proponent (not AgriProve) where they are nominated by the operator as per Cl. 10, as we have no control over the actions of an independent entity in this scenario. This is not removing our liability for negligence or non-performance which is covered by Cl. 10 (the ability to remove AgriProve as proponent/agent if we are not performing), and more specifically Cl. 20.1 under which we are liable for the greater of $50k or an equivalent value to AgriProve’s 25% fee over the preceding 12-month period if we are found to be negligent etc. As above, I am unable to amend these clauses, but I believe the liability clauses provide adequate protection for both parties to this agreement, with the intent to ensure that both parties have an interest in ensuring the success of the project by virtue of the overall structure. More than happy to continue the conversation as needed. engagements.subject: Re: Responses to Legal Review
engagements.body: Dear Kieren, Thank you again for your time and for the prior email. For the sake of clarity I went back and reformatted our discussions into each specific points. There were also a few that we glazed over but didn’t fully cover which I should have, but have put it on here to be complete. Note that I have highlighted your responses in blue and some questions from my end in red. Please review and confirm the accuracy along with any advise you can provide regarding my comments in red. * Point 6 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Market Adjustment for Agriprove Fee (Section 21.2) * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * Drafting appears to enable AgriProve to change the AgriProve Fee by an announcement in their newsletter. This provides significant discretion to AgriProve to unilaterally change the Agriprove Fee. There is a mechanism for how this will be dealt with where there is a reduction in AgriProve Fee, but there is no mechanism to deal with this where there is an increase. In relation to the mechanism dealing with a reduction, we query why there is a need to wait until the next anniversary to pass the benefit to the Operator. * Suggestion by MinterEllison * We recommend that drafting is included which restricts the ability for the AgriProve Fee to be increased without the Operator's consent. * Response by Kieren after meeting * Market Adjustment Fee. In this instance your concern stems from the interpretation that this clause may allow us to raise our service fee (for example from 25% to 30%) and pass this on to all existing contracts. As discussed on the call, this was not the intent of the clause, which was designed to not disadvantage early adopters if we ended up reducing our service fee (for example from 25% to 20%). I note that Cl. 21.2 of the master Ts and Cs notes that amendments can only be passed on if they do not have a materially adverse effect on the landholder/operator. Notwithstanding, I am happy to provide clarification that this market adjustment fee will only occur in your favour (ie. a reduction in our service fee), as this is the original intent of the clause. * Point 14 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Dealing with Project ACCUs (Clause 8.2) * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * In the event that Project ACCUs are dealt with other than in accordance with the Agreement, it is currently stated that it is a material breach of the Agreement. However, this will not cover the Operator's loss. AgriProve should be required to indemnify the Landholder against any loss incurred as a result of dealing with Project ACCUs in a way that is inappropriate. * Suggestion by MinterEllison * We recommend that an indemnity of this nature in included. * Response by Kieren during/after meeting * Suggests that AgriProve will create a separate ACCU management account controlled by CSP once ACCUs are granted by the government. This is something that AgriProve has done for others and is happy to do for CSP which would sidestep the issue. * Point 15 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Clause 9.2 – Cobenefits * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * Under the drafting, AgriProve will be entitled to 25% of all Project ACCUs and Co-benefits. While it is a commercial matter for CSPC as to whether 25% of all Project ACCUs is an appropriate figure, we recommend that CSPC calculates whether this is appropriate based on its understanding of the ACCUs which may be generated form the Carbon Projects and the expected current and future carbon price. For context, a graph showing the ACCU spot price is shown below: We also query the inclusion of Co-benefits in this arrangement. As CSPC may be aware, the Commonwealth Government has recently passed the Nature Repair Act 2023 (Cth) and the ability to generate biodiversity certificates on the Project Properties will be need to be assessed. AgriProve's services are purely related to carbon, so we don't see why AgriProve should get the benefits of any Co-benefits. As noted in the Agreement, arrangements…

From: Bill Hyem Sent: Thursday, October 12, 2023 10:59 AM To: Adam Subject: Request to resample Howson Carbon Projects 1-6, 8-13 and 15 Hi Adam, As per our previous conversations, we have completed another review of your project since our initial resampling of Howson Carbon Project 7 and 14. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. I am pleased to let you know that this additional assessment has again shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. We will be looking to re-sample as soon as possible, however the sampling schedule with our partner company Verterra is quite full. I will discuss with them and be in touch early next week with a more accurate idea so some dates that might work. We hope that it can be done prior to the end of November at this stage. We would also like to offer you the opportunity to have your projects resampled under the SAR grant which will afford you $100 worth of soil analyte information (0-30cm and 30-100cm resolution) per core for free across all 13 projects to be resampled. To access this grant there is a Date Collection and Use Agreement. I will send out both an online a flyer with further information on the grant and the accompanying agreement. Finally, I would like to discuss sacrificial paddocks you had mentioned previously, that might need to be removed from a project area. If this is still the case, it will need to be done prior to resampling the projects. From earlier conversations and looking at your digital paddock map the sacrificial paddocks may be named Buffalo Holding (29Ha) and Number 2 Long (42Ha). These would impact projects 5 and 6. It would be great if you could please give me a call when convenient to discuss. It is great to be working on your projects again and I look forward to speaking with you soon. engagements.subject: Formalising our approval process - customer facing materials
engagements.body: All, With our growth strategy gathering momentum - the amount of materials that go “customer facing” is on the up. It will be no news to any of you the risks that are inherent in this from both reputational and compliance perspectives. So, it’s time to formalise an approach. It’s very simple, but will add time and you will need to plan time for an approval process. What’s the Approval process? 1. Any customer facing material (for now), but we’ll likely need to extend this later. 2. Must have a review and approval from AB, KW and DW before going to SU. 3. The author requesting an approval from SU must include either the email chain or attach the emails with the approvals. 4. AB, KW and DW – in your review you are accountable for, grammar, formatting, brand, tone of voice, technical and process accuracy. By the time it gets to SU it should be in tip top shape. You may think this is a pain. But reflect on every typo you’ve picked up in an email you’ve received. How you’ve commented on poor formatting, confusing messaging or thought. “I got the same detail from someone else yesterday”, or worse still “someone told me something different yesterday”. The idea is to make sure that everything we do is high quality and consistent. engagements.subject: Thanks for reaching out to AgriProve, let's connect to discuss!
engagements.body: Hi Bill​, Kieren from AgriProve here, I hope you don't mind me reaching out. I'm keen to hear if you're interested in discussing the opportunity for a soil carbon project with AgriProve. Are you open to a quick call to discuss your operation and see if you're a good fit? You can also book a video call directly with me here: : The farmers we work with have built more resilient and profitable businesses by implementing practices that build soil organic carbon and are generating ACCUs for additional revenue, as well as yearly data insights into their production performance and soil health. I'd be delighted to share some customer case studies to highlight the benefits of working with us. Explanation for the delayed reporting of the first reporting period, and relevant correspondence with the CER Projects were in Operation with Corporate Carbon acting as project proponent. Corporate Carbon's responsibility in a JV with Regenerative Australian Farmers (RAF) was to secure a Carbon Aabtement Contract, and assist in facilitating registration and reporting to the CER, all other project management was being undertaken by RAF. In forming AgriProve, all soil carbon projects were to be transitioned across to AgriProve. AgriProve then undertook Agency of the projects on behalf of corporate carbon. The process to change project proponent from Corpoate Carbon took 4 years to negotiate the commercial agreements to ensure AgriProve had the ongoing legal right to operate the projects. Whilst the commercial negotiations were taking place, the soil sampling, eligible interst holder consents and preparation of the offsets report(s) were undertaken, in good faith, according to the 2021 Soil Carbon Methodology. Once the project proponent was agreed and transferred, the final variation was the transition to the 2021 Soil Carbon Method under the AgriProve LMS. The CER has been consistently notified and consulated on the 'Legacy' projects, with approvals granted for extenstion of submission to the offsets reports due to the transition from Corporate Carbon to AgriProve 10. engagements.subject: Integrated Farm and Land Management Method Issues consultation
engagements.body: UPDATE 25/10/23 – Attachments Non-legal early drafting Method from DCCEEW - not for circulation Non-legal early drafting Guide from DCCEEW - not for circulation Non-legal early drafting Supplement from DCCEEW - not for circulation DCCEEW Conceptual Issues Paper – not for circulation Response to stakeholder feedback – Draft – not for circulation Email invitation to proposed workshops for the development of the IFLM Agenda 1) General scoping of IFLM for SCIG, noting the pace/ twice weekly cadence CMI and DCCEEW are operating to. 2) Position statement for CMI – Any suggestions we can add? 3) General discussion around IFLM and what to look for as consultation progresses. 4) Should SCIG request for at least one technical workshop on soil carbon? Dear SCIG Members, This is a placeholder for an opportunity to explore soil carbon issues in early drafting of the Integrated Farm and Land Management Method under the Australian ACCU Scheme. Our input here will be fed through the Carbon Market Institute IFLM Taskforce. It will also help us explore and develop SCIG positions on IFLM method issues. For context, the government has agreed to continue to develop the IFLM with the ERAC (Emissions Reduction Advisory Committee) in the interim as the Chubb Review recommendations particularly the CAIC (Carbon Abatement Integrity Committee) are implemented and established. Method Development Interim Framework (dcceew.gov.au) You might like to share this opportunity a little wider within your company with people experienced in method development. Within SCIG I will develop a ‘tag’ for contacts who can help with method issues. People who attend from your companies can be added to this list. These people may not be the voting SCIG member or CEO. engagements.subject: RE: Meeting wIth Agriprove and RAF: Summary Points
engagements.body: Hi Deane, Some comments below: 1. We will amend and restate (ie replace) the current agreements between Corporate Carbon and the farmers and Corporate Carbon and RAF (“New Agreements”) - Agreed; new agreements also to replace Corporate Carbon with AgriProve. 2. The New Agreements will limit the application of the Projects to the contracted based-line trial areas (~10% of the total farm areas) - Agreed; new agreements will only relate to the registered project areas. All cases have now had area variations lodged and approved by the CER to limit the registered projects to the baselined area. 3. Similarly Corporate Carbon will remove any wording relating to ownership or rights over the Farmer’s soil carbon as currently appearing in the Participation Deed - Agreed; any reference to claim on ownership on landholders soil carbon will be removed. 4. The Farmers and RAF shall receive their respective proportion of verified ACCUs (following completion of the audit process) for T0-T1 (first 5 years) into their own ANREU accounts, to sell on the secondary market, hold as carbon offsets or otherwise, based on initial splits assuming ~$12/ACCU: a. 66.5% Farmers Agreed; 66.5% of ACCUs to landholder. Landholders are individually responsible for establishing ANREU accounts. b. 25% RAF c. 8.5% Agriprove (for them to deal with as they see fit) - Points b and c pertaining to the remaining 33.5% to be agreed between RAF and AgriProve based on work completed to date (refer to the attached spreadsheet) and CAC servicing obligations. 5. ACCUs generated and verified for T1-T2 (next 5 years of which we are already 2-3 years into) will be received by farmers into their own ANREU accounts in a proportion of 72.5-75%. The balance will be split between Agriprove and RAF which shall be determined following a clear and agreed definition of the respective roles and responsibilities of Agriprove and RAF for T1 -T2; this will occur during May. Farmers will deal solely with RAF (as the ‘Agent’) but some services may be provided by Agriprove to RAF. The details of the service and % allocation will be shared with farmers - Agreed in principle; please see attached breakdown of tasks and responsibilities for further discussion between RAF/AgriProve. 6. All audit costs for ACCU verification shall be borne by the individual farmers - Agreed; the audit process will be managed by AgriProve and audit quotes provided to RAF for approval with landholders before progressing. 7. Following the conclusion of T2 and for T3 and beyond (at completion of 10 year ERF contract period plus), Agriprove will exit the Projects and the farmers will become their own project Proponents under regulation and RAF shall be appointed as Project Agents. At this time, the splits may be renegotiated between Farmers and RAF - Agreed; AgriProve to be removed as Proponent at year 10 and replaced with landholder, RAF to be registered as Agent. AgriProve have no further involvement in the projects after the proponent has been varied. 8. Upon acceptance of the ’New Agreements’ by all parties, the following steps will be undertaken prior to ACCU creation: a. The Novation of Project Proponent transferring from Corporate Carbon Australia to AgriProve; Agreed; AgriProve to manage proponency variation process once agreements are signed and AgriProve has legal right to do so. Note the assessment period can be a minimum of 3 months at the CER and we cannot initiate audit until this variation is approved. b. Auditing of the Offsets Report; Agreed; AgriProve to manage this process. Noting that proponent and method variations need to be lodged and approved by the CER once AgriProve has legal right; it may take up to 6 months before these variations are approved. c. Completion and submission of the Offsets Report (aligned to 2021 Methodology) to the Regulator; Agreed; AgriProve to manage this process, refer to the point above. d. Setup of respective ANREU accounts for Farmers and RAF; Agreed; This is to be manage…

engagements.subject: Re: Meeting wIth Agriprove and RAF: Summary Points to Progress Project Agreements
engagements.body: Dear Kieren, My apologies for being hard to contact over the last 10 days (been in Africa). Below is a summary our collective position. We refer to our letter dated 3 April 2024 and our meeting dated 2 May 2024. As per the meeting, all splits for T0-T1 were to remain as per the original contract being: a. 66.5% Farmers Agreed; 66.5% of ACCUs to landholder. Landholders are individually responsible for establishing ANREU accounts. b. 25% RAF c. 8.5% Agriprove (for them to deal with as they see fit) If Corporate Carbon believes that it is entitled to compensation for any additional tasks or previously nominated/agreed RAF tasks that it performed during this period, then it should specify these tasks and invoice for them based on a market time-cost recovery rate. For T1-T2, RAF is prepared to accept a revenue split proportionate to the indicative roles and responsibilities suggested in your spreadsheet. RAF does not however believe that this equates to 50%/50% on the remaining non-landholder ACCUs, specifically the 25% RAF portion. The monetisation of this (@$32/ACCU) will far exceed the original 8.5% split (@$10/ACCU) - assuming the carbon price is projected to exceed $80/ACCU by 2030. Therefore, Agriprove is already making a substantial uplift. We may be prepared to move down from 25% and lift Agriprove up from 8.5%, but we need to analyse the spreadsheet and agree proportional roles, responsibilities and benefit. We are available to do this at your convenience. If this approach is acceptable, let’s organise a call next week and please prepare new restated agreement for our review, amendment (if required) and approval based on the above and the below agreed points (subject to T1-T2 splits); this should demonstrate to the Regulator that we are progressing these projects as a matter of priority. If this is not acceptable, based on legal advice, RAF and the Farmers shall terminate its arrangement with Corporate Carbon for breach of contract. However we trust that this provides the basis for a mutually 'shared benefit' arrangement to be struck. Regards Regards Deane Belfield Director Regenerative Australian Farmers (soil carbon project developers) ￼ Winner Leadership Award - National Carbon Cocky Awards E: deane@regenfarmers.com.au W: www.regenfarmers.com.au M: 0414 v617542

engagements.body: Updating with notes from SCIG meeting today. Dear SCIG Members, One outcome from the ‘Listening tour’ of members was that we would appreciate getting together for a Summit. DRAFT SCIG Summit Objectives Need a headline GOAL SUGGESTED HEADER: The Soil Carbon Industry Group announces the Second Australasian Soil Carbon Summit BYLINE: Expanding opportunity, showcasing success, on farm productivity gains. – Expanding opportunity, - Farmers decarbonising the atmosphere - Showing success on the farm - on farm productivity gains Teir 1 Objectives (in order of priority) Engage Farmers - To engage and connect with as many farmers as possible who would like to learn more about soil carbon and meet with SCIG members Cross pollination node for discussion across the value chain with developers and regulators and markets Share Case Studies - To openly share success stories (and challenges faced) in the soil carbon industry Platform for Science and Innovation - To hear from scientific developments and innovation successes in soil carbon. Noting need to engage farmers with practical implementation dynamics. Addressing fear and building trust in specialised service providers. Showcase Soil Carbon Method - To showcase and reinforce the strong regulatory environment for soil carbon projects Tier 2 Objectives To publish Soil Carbon Summit proceedings as a stepping stone in the knowledge and development of our industry. To conduct associated meetings, planning and strategic interaction at an industry level To connect with the International soil carbon agenda To present a leading Summit outcome statement collectively agreed by the conference committee – developed by SLIDO or similar Site visits before and after tour – high value way of showing people what is done Agenda - 4 days Pre-conference tour Science symposium Practical ‘how to’ day of presentations – The SUMMIT day, productivity focus Trade displays Conference dinner Industry strategy and roadmap meetings – Markets, Policy… Post conference tour ________________________________________________________________________________ Microsoft Teams Need help? engagements.body: Dear Stuart, My general comments regarding the agreements are as follows: 1. Deed of Novation 1. This needs to be a Deed of Novation “AND VARIATION”, to accommodate the changes 2. I understand that this is a template, and that this revision is in respect of each of the ACCU Sales Agreements with each Seller 3. Clause 1.3 - All definitions of the Original Agreement should be retained and those clauses also with the Novation and Variation Agreement taking precedence to the extent of any inconsistency - 4. Clause 2.2 – Agreement is “varied” and (a) – Annexure “2” not “B”; 5. Clause 6.6 and 6.10 of the Original Agreement needs to be varied as the farmer’s proportions of ACCU’s will be vested in farmers own registry accounts, balance will go into RAF and Agriprove accounts 6. “Price” is no longer defined in the Transaction Particulars and should be replaced with “Percentages” as per the agreed T0-T1 and T1 -T2 splits, and definition of Surplus ACCU’s should be deleted 7. We need to define the T0-T1 and T1 -T2 period and exclude T2-T3 as per agreed position (no relationship post T2 end) 8. Need to await description of titles in Annexure 2 and 3 to ensure reserved to “trial baseline areas” 9. Where is the $5k cap on Buyer services charges? 10. We need reference to “No ownership rights over Seller’s Soil Carbon” as per the agreement 11. All other agreements other than the ACCU Sales and Agreements and the ERF Participation Deed mentioned in the attached letter need to be terminated 12. I will defer to Deane regarding breakdown of T2 responsibilities (assume this is as per previous spreadsheet) I can make these amendments if necessary but please note that the costs of my review and amendments are to be covered by Agriprove, as per our previous agreement. 1. Soil ERF Participation Deed 1. Replace ERF with ACCU scheme throughout 2. Delete clause 2.1(3) as Proponent will be issued its proportion to satisfy ERF requirements (unless I am missing something?) engagements.body: Dear Simon, We have updated the Deed of Novation and ERF Participation Deed as requested referencing answers to your comments below: 1. Deed of Novation 1. This needs to be a Deed of Novation “AND VARIATION”, to accommodate the changes - Complete 2. I understand that this is a template, and that this revision is in respect of each of the ACCU Sales Agreements with each Seller – no action 3. Clause 1.3 - All definitions of the Original Agreement should be retained and those clauses also with the Novation and Variation Agreement taking precedence to the extent of any inconsistency – Complete 4. Clause 2.2 – Agreement is “varied” and (a) – Annexure “2” not “B”; - Complete Clause 6.6 and 6.10 of the Original Agreement needs to be varied as the farmer’s proportions of ACCU’s will be vested in farmers own registry accounts, balance will go into RAF and AgriProve accounts - Clause 2.2(e) specifies the percentages of ACCUs to be distributed in place of Schedule 1 of the Original Agreement. 1. “Price” is no longer defined in the Transaction Particulars and should be replaced with “Percentages” as per the agreed T0-T1 and T1 -T2 splits, and definition of Surplus ACCU’s should be deleted – Complete 2. We need to define the T0-T1 and T1 -T2 period and exclude T2-T3 as per agreed position (no relationship post T2 end) – Complete 3. Need to await description of titles in Annexure 2 and 3 to ensure reserved to “trial baseline areas” – Acknowledged, once the ‘template’ novation and variation deed, ACCU Scheme Participation Deed, and Varied ACCU Sales and Licence Agreement are approved, each project will have updates to the particulars for each landholder and project. 4. Where is the $5k cap on Buyer services charges? – not relevant. Any agreed services cap between landholders and RAF is separate to this. AgriProve is not party to that. If you are referring to the $5,00 per project ($25,000 total) agreed payment for work performed AgriProve will invoice RAF for this amount, not the landholders as previously agreed. 5. We need reference to “No ownership rights over Seller’s Soil Carbon” as per the agreement – there is no reference to having rights to the Seller’s soil carbon therefore this is not necessary 6. All other agreements other than the ACCU Sales and Agreements and the ERF Participation Deed mentioned in the attached letter need to be terminated – This is covered by Clause 8.7 of the Novation and Variation Deed. All agreements between the outgoing party and the incoming party and the landholders will follow this agreement. 7. I will defer to Deane regarding breakdown of T2 responsibilities (assume this is as per previous spreadsheet) – yes. Not part of this process with landholders. I can make these amendments if necessary but please note that the costs of my review and amendments are to be covered by AgriProve, as per our previous agreement. No previous agreement was made. Each party is responsible for their own legal costs. 1. Soil ERF Participation Deed 1. Replace ERF with ACCU scheme throughout - Complete 2. Delete clause 2.1(3) as Proponent will be issued its proportion to satisfy ERF requirements (unless I am missing something?) – the nominated registry account is issued all project ACCUs which are then transferred within 10 business days. From a functional perspective, it is the requirement of the CER and in the CFI Act, that the Project’s nominated registry account is where project ACCUs will be issued. This is where all ACCUs are issued. The CER does not have the capacity or capability to issue ACCUs to multiple registry accounts. Re: Request to resample Townley Carbon Project - ERF167963
engagements.body: Hi Bill, just following up to see if you have the results from the re sampling at this point ? best regards Bruce > On 24 Apr 2023, at 11:16 am, AgriProve wrote: > > Hi Bruce, > > > As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. > > The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. > > Can you please confirm that you are happy for us to come and resample your project areas within the month of May? engagements.subject: Re: Request to resample Townley Carbon Project
engagements.body: You don't often get email from brucewhiteford@bigpond.com. Learn why this is important Hi Barbara , the farm was sampled in June/July of this year does it make sense to be sampling again only 5 months later? best regards Bruce On 6 Dec 2023, at 2:24 pm, AgriProve wrote: Hi Bruce, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator, there are many other factors that can influence sequestration that does not guarantee soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. Can you please confirm that you are happy for us to come and resample your project areas within the period of 18th to 22nd December 2023? Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. The attached factsheet has information regarding resampling process but if you have any other questions, please let me know. engagements.subject: Property Sale
engagements.body: Hi Bruce, Claudia has asked me to reach out regarding potential sale of your property. As you are aware we have Townley Carbon Project (ERF167693) currently registered on the property. The best-case scenario for us in the event of property sale is that the incoming owner takes on the soil carbon project, and if this remains an option we are more than happy to provide any additional material or speak directly to any interested parties to determine whether this is feasible. If this is not the case, you can request for us to voluntarily revoke the project with the CER (noting once we lodge this revocation it may take a minimum of three months for the CER to formally terminate the project). In this instance, this is quite straightforward given that: * ACCUs have not been issued on the project * Baseline sampling costs were paid in full at the time Please let us know if there is any scope to continue the project, and if not please notify us at any time that you would like us to revoke the project and we will send through confirmation that we have lodged this notification with the CER. Happy to discuss at any time. engagements.subject: Formalising our approval process - customer facing materials
engagements.body: All, With our growth strategy gathering momentum - the amount of materials that go “customer facing” is on the up. It will be no news to any of you the risks that are inherent in this from both reputational and compliance perspectives. So, it’s time to formalise an approach. It’s very simple, but will add time and you will need to plan time for an approval process. What’s the Approval process? 1. Any customer facing material (for now), but we’ll likely need to extend this later. 2. Must have a review and approval from AB, KW and DW before going to SU. 3. The author requesting an approval from SU must include either the email chain or attach the emails with the approvals. 4. AB, KW and DW – in your review you are accountable for, grammar, formatting, brand, tone of voice, technical and process accuracy. By the time it gets to SU it should be in tip top shape. You may think this is a pain. But reflect on every typo you’ve picked up in an email you’ve received. How you’ve commented on poor formatting, confusing messaging or thought. “I got the same detail from someone else yesterday”, or worse still “someone told me something different yesterday”. The idea is to make sure that everything we do is high quality and consistent. At this stage Monday the 27th will be the best date in the next fortnight if this works for Michael and yourself? engagements.subject: RE: Responses to Legal Review
engagements.body: Hi Elliot, Good to catch up last week. Apologies for the delay in getting this back to you, I am still catching up after my disrupted week last week with illness in the household. To summarise our conversation, I believe there were three key clauses that remained a concern: 1. Market Adjustment Fee. In this instance your concern stems from the interpretation that this clause may allow us to raise our service fee (for example from 25% to 30%) and pass this on to all existing contracts. As discussed on the call, this was not the intent of the clause, which was designed to not disadvantage early adopters if we ended up reducing our service fee (for example from 25% to 20%). I note that Cl. 21.2 of the master Ts and Cs notes that amendments can only be passed on if they have a materially adverse effect on the landholder/operator. Notwithstanding, I am happy to provide clarification that this market adjustment fee will only occur in your favour (ie. a reduction in our service fee), as this is the original intent of the clause. 2. Risk of ACCU Relinquishment. As discussed, this is not a clause we can amend as it is a function of the regulation that we are working under. This clause arises due to the requirement that if the operator elects to terminate the agreement early and ACCUs have been issued to the project and we are then required to revoke the project with the CER, the CER in all likelihood will request that all ACCUs issued to the project are returned by the project proponent (AgriProve). In this instance where the termination is initiated by the operator AgriProve will request that these are sourced (or the equivalent value thereof) by the landholder/operator, as it is their breach of terms that has led to the relinquishment requirement in this instance. The key undertaking on the landholder/operator here is that the land remain in agricultural system for the 25 year project period to mitigate this risk. 3. Liability. Regarding the disclaimer of liability in Cl. 20.6, this is specific to instances where further decisions based on information we provide (such as decisions regarding whether to sell or hold ACCUs) are made by the landholder/operator, the outcomes of which we have no control over, such as a reduction in ACCU price. We would always recommend that independent advice is sought on such decisions. In terms of 20.6 (2), similarly, we cannot be liable for actions taken by a New Project Proponent (not AgriProve) where they are nominated by the operator as per Cl. 10, as we have no control over the actions of an independent entity in this scenario. This is not removing our liability for negligence or non-performance which is covered by Cl. 10 (the ability to remove AgriProve as proponent/agent if we are not performing), and more specifically Cl. 20.1 under which we are liable for the greater of $50k or an equivalent value to AgriProve’s 25% fee over the preceding 12-month period if we are found to be negligent etc. As above, I am unable to amend these clauses, but I believe the liability clauses provide adequate protection for both parties to this agreement, with the intent to ensure that both parties have an interest in ensuring the success of the project by virtue of the overall structure. More than happy to continue the conversation as needed. engagements.subject: Re: Responses to Legal Review
engagements.body: Dear Kieren, Thank you again for your time and for the prior email. For the sake of clarity I went back and reformatted our discussions into each specific points. There were also a few that we glazed over but didn’t fully cover which I should have, but have put it on here to be complete. Note that I have highlighted your responses in blue and some questions from my end in red. Please review and confirm the accuracy along with any advise you can provide regarding my comments in red. * Point 6 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Market Adjustment for Agriprove Fee (Section 21.2) * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * Drafting appears to enable AgriProve to change the AgriProve Fee by an announcement in their newsletter. This provides significant discretion to AgriProve to unilaterally change the Agriprove Fee. There is a mechanism for how this will be dealt with where there is a reduction in AgriProve Fee, but there is no mechanism to deal with this where there is an increase. In relation to the mechanism dealing with a reduction, we query why there is a need to wait until the next anniversary to pass the benefit to the Operator. * Suggestion by MinterEllison * We recommend that drafting is included which restricts the ability for the AgriProve Fee to be increased without the Operator's consent. * Response by Kieren after meeting * Market Adjustment Fee. In this instance your concern stems from the interpretation that this clause may allow us to raise our service fee (for example from 25% to 30%) and pass this on to all existing contracts. As discussed on the call, this was not the intent of the clause, which was designed to not disadvantage early adopters if we ended up reducing our service fee (for example from 25% to 20%). I note that Cl. 21.2 of the master Ts and Cs notes that amendments can only be passed on if they do not have a materially adverse effect on the landholder/operator. Notwithstanding, I am happy to provide clarification that this market adjustment fee will only occur in your favour (ie. a reduction in our service fee), as this is the original intent of the clause. * Point 14 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Dealing with Project ACCUs (Clause 8.2) * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * In the event that Project ACCUs are dealt with other than in accordance with the Agreement, it is currently stated that it is a material breach of the Agreement. However, this will not cover the Operator's loss. AgriProve should be required to indemnify the Landholder against any loss incurred as a result of dealing with Project ACCUs in a way that is inappropriate. * Suggestion by MinterEllison * We recommend that an indemnity of this nature in included. * Response by Kieren during/after meeting * Suggests that AgriProve will create a separate ACCU management account controlled by CSP once ACCUs are granted by the government. This is something that AgriProve has done for others and is happy to do for CSP which would sidestep the issue. * Point 15 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Clause 9.2 – Cobenefits * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * Under the drafting, AgriProve will be entitled to 25% of all Project ACCUs and Co-benefits. While it is a commercial matter for CSPC as to whether 25% of all Project ACCUs is an appropriate figure, we recommend that CSPC calculates whether this is appropriate based on its understanding of the ACCUs which may be generated form the Carbon Projects and the expected current and future carbon price. For context, a graph showing the ACCU spot price is shown below: We also query the inclusion of Co-benefits in this arrangement. From: Elliott Choi Sent: Tuesday, 17 September 2024 3:42 PM To: Kieren Whittock Cc: Bill Hyem ; Michael Lee Subject: Re: Responses to Legal Review Dear Kieren, Thank you again for your time and for the prior email. For the sake of clarity I went back and reformatted our discussions into each specific points. There were also a few that we glazed over but didn’t fully cover which I should have, but have put it on here to be complete. Note that I have highlighted your responses in blue and some questions from my end in red. Please review and confirm the accuracy along with any advise you can provide regarding my comments in red. * Point 6 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Market Adjustment for Agriprove Fee (Section 21.2) * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * Drafting appears to enable AgriProve to change the AgriProve Fee by an announcement in their newsletter. This provides significant discretion to AgriProve to unilaterally change the Agriprove Fee. There is a mechanism for how this will be dealt with where there is a reduction in AgriProve Fee, but there is no mechanism to deal with this where there is an increase. In relation to the mechanism dealing with a reduction, we query why there is a need to wait until the next anniversary to pass the benefit to the Operator. * Suggestion by MinterEllison * We recommend that drafting is included which restricts the ability for the AgriProve Fee to be increased without the Operator's consent. * Response by Kieren after meeting * Market Adjustment Fee. In this instance your concern stems from the interpretation that this clause may allow us to raise our service fee (for example from 25% to 30%) and pass this on to all existing contracts. As discussed on the call, this was not the intent of the clause, which was designed to not disadvantage early adopters if we ended up reducing our service fee (for example from 25% to 20%). I note that Cl. 21.2 of the master Ts and Cs notes that amendments can only be passed on if they do not have a materially adverse effect on the landholder/operator. Notwithstanding, I am happy to provide clarification that this market adjustment fee will only occur in your favour (ie. a reduction in our service fee), as this is the original intent of the clause. * No additional comments. * Point 14 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Dealing with Project ACCUs (Clause 8.2) * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * In the event that Project ACCUs are dealt with other than in accordance with the Agreement, it is currently stated that it is a material breach of the Agreement. However, this will not cover the Operator's loss. AgriProve should be required to indemnify the Landholder against any loss incurred as a result of dealing with Project ACCUs in a way that is inappropriate. * Suggestion by MinterEllison * We recommend that an indemnity of this nature in included. * Response by Kieren during/after meeting * Suggests that AgriProve will create a separate ACCU management account controlled by CSP once ACCUs are granted by the government. This is something that AgriProve has done for others and is happy to do for…

engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: HI Mitch, No Worries. I will check in with Geoff about where Beale and Cooper are up to. The most recent result for Watson was positive, and we are planning to resample. You should hear from Will soon about logistics with that soon. For the NDRE: All we get is what we send you with the line ( attached in case you didn't see the recent email I sent). We are working on building some NDRE and making it a bit more useful into the platform at the moment, but it is a little while away from being more than that line for now. We did run the project through the HORIZON model, and things are looking very promising. The output it gives at the moment is not very friendly to send or view. Its basically a lot of numbers, it requires a lot of interpretation and it is still a prototype, so we aren't going to share the results until we have calibrated it a bit more. It has suggested though that it is very likely that you have had an increase significant enough to be credited a second time around. From next week you will be able to see some of the HORIZON information in the platform - it will show you zones of your best performing, average, and lower performing areas in terms of carbon sequestration. This will be interesting to see what's happening across the area and in future will be able to give you carbon predictions. Would love your feedback on that once it is up and running. In forming AgriProve, all soil carbon projects were to be transitioned across to AgriProve. AgriProve then undertook Agency of the projects on behalf of corporate carbon. The process to change project proponent from Corpoate Carbon took 4 years to negotiate the commercial agreements to ensure AgriProve had the ongoing legal right to operate the projects. Whilst the commercial negotiations were taking place, the soil sampling, eligible interst holder consents and preparation of the offsets report(s) were undertaken, in good faith, according to the 2021 Soil Carbon Methodology. Once the project proponent was agreed and transferred, the final variation was the transition to the 2021 Soil Carbon Method under the AgriProve LMS. The CER has been consistently notified and consulated on the 'Legacy' projects, with approvals granted for extenstion of submission to the offsets reports due to the transition from Corporate Carbon to AgriProve 10.
