Explanation for the delayed reporting of the first reporting period, and relevant correspondence with the CER Projects were in Operation with Corporate Carbon acting as project proponent. Corporate Carbon's responsibility in a JV with Regenerative Australian Farmers (RAF) was to secure a Carbon Aabtement Contract, and assist in facilitating registration and reporting to the CER, all other project management was being undertaken by RAF. In forming AgriProve, all soil carbon projects were to be transitioned across to AgriProve. AgriProve then undertook Agency of the projects on behalf of corporate carbon. The process to change project proponent from Corpoate Carbon took 4 years to negotiate the commercial agreements to ensure AgriProve had the ongoing legal right to operate the projects. Whilst the commercial negotiations were taking place, the soil sampling, eligible interst holder consents and preparation of the offsets report(s) were undertaken, in good faith, according to the 2021 Soil Carbon Methodology. Once the project proponent was agreed and transferred, the final variation was the transition to the 2021 Soil Carbon Method under the AgriProve LMS. The CER has been consistently notified and consulated on the 'Legacy' projects, with approvals granted for extenstion of submission to the offsets reports due to the transition from Corporate Carbon to AgriProve 10. Expecting timing of availability of Offsets Reports and for the audit to be conducted Nov-25 Nov-25 Nov-25 Nov-2…

In forming AgriProve, all soil carbon projects were to be transitioned across to AgriProve. AgriProve then undertook Agency of the projects on behalf of corporate carbon. The process to change project proponent from Corpoate Carbon took 4 years to negotiate the commercial agreements to ensure AgriProve had the ongoing legal right to operate the projects. Whilst the commercial negotiations were taking place, the soil sampling, eligible interst holder consents and preparation of the offsets report(s) were undertaken, in good faith, according to the 2021 Soil Carbon Methodology. Once the project proponent was agreed and transferred, the final variation was the transition to the 2021 Soil Carbon Method under the AgriProve LMS. The CER has been consistently notified and consulated on the 'Legacy' projects, with approvals granted for extenstion of submission to the offsets reports due to the transition from Corporate Carbon to AgriProve 10. engagements.subject: AgriProve mapping and engagement document
engagements.body: Hi Wayne, Great to speak with you again today. Attached are the draft maps for soil carbon projects across Towarra, Andys and Wowan. We are happy to take feedback on these and they are flexible to change as needed. I have attached our engagement form, called the Consent to Register - Commitment to Implement in this email for your visibility. I am happy to walk through this with you and I typically help pre-fill it for landholders to ensure language is correct for the regulators assessment. This pre-filling of information can be done whenever you are ready before being reviewed by your father for final signature as the name on the land titles. Please note that baseline sampling of Towarra at a preliminary estimate would come to around $60,000-65,000. This is dependent on final sampling plans and configuration so this is subject to change. Regarding the revenue opportunity of increasing your soil carbon levels, I have run some numbers based on the draft project area for Towarra of 2616Ha and a chart found in pg16 of our Information Pack (attached). If you achieved a 0.25% increase in soil organic carbon over the project lifetime that would equate to 31 ACCUs/Ha after 25% risk of reversal reduction. 31x 2616Ha = 81,096 ACCUs This would be a sequestration rate of 1.65ACCUs/Ha/Year (before risk of reversal). If you achieved a 0.5% increase in soil organic carbon over the project lifetime that would equate to 62 ACCUs/Ha after a 25% risk of reversal reduction. 62 x 2616Ha = 162,192 ACCUs This would be a sequestration rate of 3.3ACCUs/Ha/Year (before risk of reversal). The current price per ACCU can be found at accus.com.au: http://accus.com.au/ Let me know how you get on with all of this information and if you would like me to assist with questions or conversations. Speak soon! engagements.subject: Grant for baseline subsidy
engagements.body: Hi Wayne, As discussed, I want to let you know that a National Soil Carbon Innovation Challenge (NSCIC) grant is currently available to help subsidies baseline sampling. We will be working with Hone, a remote sensing company, to deliver this grant and they are looking for properties across various geographical locations. I put your location forward for pre-approval and have heard back that you are eligible. By participating, laboratory cost for 30 soil cores (approx. 300 Ha) are subsidised which equates to roughly $6,000. You will also get access to the Hone Soil Carbon Device, made available with a $1 for 1 year lease agreement. Hone's hand-held device measures soil organic carbon using near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy. The ask is a data sharing agreement and commitment to complete 30 scans per quarter for 1 year. The Hone grant flyer and Data Use Agreement are attached below. I think the Wowan property would be a great fit for a ~$6,000 subsidy. Please be aware of the following: Limited Availability: Only a limited number of places are available, and once these places are filled, the offer will no longer be available. Expiry: This offer will expire the earlier of: All places filled or 30th September 2024. From: Dylan Jones Sent: Friday, 13 September 2024 4:01 PM To: Wayne Hanrahan Subject: AgriProve - Soil Carbon Project Hi Wayne, I've attached a .kml file that should load into Google earth. The file is a revised version of the draft avoided clearing areas done up by GreenCollar. Hopefully you're able to see the two different areas I've split out as Avoided Clearing and Soil Carbon. I've had a brief chat to our team around the attractiveness of AC vs SC, and it seems to come down to the upfront payment potential of avoided clearing, as opposed to the delayed generation of ACCUs under a soil carbon project. From my interpretation of the proposed GreenCollar maps, it may be questionable whether some of the areas would qualify based on satellite imagery, but I couldn't say what the tolerance is for how finely tuned it needs to be. You may prefer to have grazing areas under a soil carbon project so that they aren't bound by the same clearing restrictions of an AC project. Of the proposed areas I've revised, an extra 82ha looks like it could be put under a soil carbon project. For your consideration, using a rough yield of 3 ACCUs/ha/yr over the 25-year lifespan of the project would approximate to ~$215k using the current spot price of $35/ACCU. Have a look at the map and let know me know if you think my reasoning is justified, happy to go either way. engagements.subject: Formalising our approval process - customer facing materials
engagements.body: All, With our growth strategy gathering momentum - the amount of materials that go “customer facing” is on the up. It will be no news to any of you the risks that are inherent in this from both reputational and compliance perspectives. So, it’s time to formalise an approach. It’s very simple, but will add time and you will need to plan time for an approval process. What’s the Approval process? 1. Any customer facing material (for now), but we’ll likely need to extend this later. 2. Must have a review and approval from AB, KW and DW before going to SU. 3. The author requesting an approval from SU must include either the email chain or attach the emails with the approvals. 4. AB, KW and DW – in your review you are accountable for, grammar, formatting, brand, tone of voice, technical and process accuracy. By the time it gets to SU it should be in tip top shape. You may think this is a pain. But reflect on every typo you’ve picked up in an email you’ve received. engagements.subject: AgriProve Soil Carbon Project Information
engagements.body: Hi Kylie, It was great to speak with you this afternoon about what you are doing on your property. Thanks for taking the time to discuss a carbon project with AgriProve and I look forward to moving to the next stage of the process. As discussed, I am sending through some relevant information for you to look over. Below I have outlined what each attachment is about, to help you navigate them. 1 and 2. I have attached our Information Pack that provides an overview of what a project with AgriProve will entail, along with an FAQ document containing helpful written answers to some general questions that come up. 3. Our next steps form is the Consent to Register, Commitment to Implement (CTR-CTI). This is the main one we need back from you to move forward. Filling this out allows us to start gathering the background information required to register the project and commence the mapping process in consultation with you. This document does not lock you into a project with us should you decide not to proceed. Based on our discussion I would recommend selecting 'Establishing, and permanently maintaining, a pasture where there was previously no pasture, such as on cropland or bare fallow (for example, converting cropland to pasture)". However, this is up to you. We typically recommend selecting only one eligible activity to start, and this can be updated in the future should you choose. 4. I have also attached our Universal Land Management Strategy that accompanies all AgriProve projects. A land management strategy is required by the Clean Energy Regulator for all Carbon Projects registered with them. I am more than happy to talk you through these documents and discuss any questions that come up as a result. Feel free to reach out anytime at the contact details in my signature. I am looking forward to speaking further with you next month, after you have had time to speak with Christophe. I will reach out in a month if I haven't heard from you beforehand. All the best! engagements.subject: RE: Rocky Springs Carbon Project - Key Commercial Terms letter
engagements.body: Hi Kobi, Great to catch up yesterday and thanks again for your time. As we went through together, I have updated the letter and had our two Directors, Matthew and Stephen Warnken, sign it overnight. Please see attached for your counter signatures. Regarding point 14.2.3 of the Master Terms, I have confirmed that it only references the ACCUs which may have been issued to the project to that time. It is a way for the Operator to terminate the agreement of their own volition (i.e. not due to any wrong-doing by AgriProve) without exposing AgriProve to the liability of repaying any issued ACCUs. Essentially this would be an avenue to exit the agreement when the project is otherwise successful (with the issuance of ACCUs). I hope that makes more sense? engagements.body: Hi Justin, Booking some time for us to set you up in the new AgriProve Software. It should take no more than 30 minutes. Let me know if you need us to reschedule. Basic steps that we’ll guide you through are: We’ll email you an invite to the software – you set up a password and login. We’ll get you to set up your own Ceres Portal at https://manage.cerestag.com/account/register - you set up a login and add your property as a location. Once were all set we can send invitation to your farm software to any other users who you’d like to have access Speak to you then. discovery call with Justin: feedback for becoming a growth engine: We are busy - the life of the carbon project together - need to be able to bring forward the milestones of a carbon project. Key Pieces of Feedback: Transparency Transparency with the operational procedure - "were busy running our own businesses, put together a piece so farmers have an understanding of key times and what is required by the farmer - i.e. a piece of collateral that reflects the project lifecycle" Project Milestones Contact points Regular touch points either en masse or 1:1 AgriProve needs to come in to guide the project and where it needs to go. Goal oriented: Validate that carbon sequestration is possible Was "Mr Skeptical" and wanted to road-test it, so others could take these thing on. Big gap between Operations and the Producer We need guide Tech notes that come with it as well - when sharing technical information from other projects - we haven't done this very well. Provide the farmer with simple takeaways: So the producer is able to communicate, or guide people in a process where they can verbalise their soil mission - how many tonnes we are trying to sequester. Education is needed regularly - e.g. webinars, seminars, tutorials. attend 3-4 webinars a year - so they're engaged with what is happening reality on pay-offs, discussing the newest content. Value Propositions for Customer Success and Recruitment Linkage between production and carbon building: improvements to farm, lead to increase in production, the co-benefit is carbon. Tags for tonnes helps with this as the co-benefits: Compared the Customer success challenge with Ruminati program - they provide a very strong user experience around Baselining and understanding where they're at; Integrates for day to day farming with the carbon project What does it mean being in a carbon project? Similar thinking to superannuation; payback period is significantly further down the line, but the need to regularly check in on progress is important Vital piece is providing a producer with a really simple, value proposition for starting know that shade is super important, improving water, shade, pasture utilisation The more we can break down those barriers for customer success, if we can get that right, participants will be happier with the model, the model is a bit fractured as a result of not setting clear agendas/milestones/guidance - what is working and not working when it comes to carbon building and production benefit. "what were not doing enough of, investing in the production model, but not investing enough time into learning how this relates this back to carbon farming." Long term goal: asset growth and a carbon project Short term goal: animal production and outcomes from that Align short-term to long-term goals, but adding value and clear linkage between short term and long term goals. AgriProve needs to become a producer-oriented organisation: What would the farmer tell the consumer? I'm in an accredited carbon project and using data driven insights to improve my farm Stakeholders: Processors, get a green premium when speaking with processors on ESG programs Banks: Potentially beneficial interest rate when engaging with an ESG Program Teys - Grasslands - they pay a premium for productivity JBS - pay a premium for being a steward of their land Processors - they are talking about the ESG program, but not sure what that program looks like: what sort of value they can give people how do we attach benefits to the 240 farmers, will they get a better rate at the bank? What if they got 0.2% better rate because they're joined to an ESG program with AgriProve. Consumers: Reason other tech companies he's worked with have been successful: AgriWebb gives you a stewardship program, but AgriProve does not - need collateral, AgriProve Environmental Farming Program. "Bank is stoked that you're part of a carbon project, they really look at ESG We will get a premium to these 240 participants? Apart from Off-se…

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Discussion around Greenhams certification. Notes below: Looking at Greenhams 'Never Ever' Greenhams - 10c premium per kg - $32 per animal Needs to be higher Need to reward early adopters with a bigger reward - $100 a head / $0.30 per kg Co-benefit of being in a carbon projects Don’t want to be a price taker, being a price maker - put the responsibly How do you get into the exclusive club - rare air - rewarding those who follow the process especially Something juicy you can hang your hat on Marketing cattle through $0.30 premium market - on 100 head it's $10,000 There is not enough money in it to keep re-investing in it - with a yearly benefit makes it worth it to keep the practices going Adopting a philosophy with the carbon project and then it becomes Delayed return to drip feed of annual return through the premium Market needs to head this way if you want uptake Consensus is for 10c they don't give a shit MSA graded to 57-61 (eating quality) Marble score 6+ - carbon premium Deep dive into the marble scoring Story is the most important thing - don't sell the story short Farmers are terrible story tellers Let the farmer tell the story about the climate aspect Go down and deep dive on premium branded meat for sale and look at the story of never ever, great southern, little joe, maccas beef Tier 1 - in it (carbon project) Tier 2 - generating carbon (baby Dylan has f Get JC and someone else to round-table with us Complete against eating quality with good and validated story - government taking full control Do the practice change (which is hard) and get rewarded and paid more Let the carbon cattle enter a premium market with the branded story Going to have a meeting in 10 days in Singapore Regen farmers and the story telling - paddock to plate regen product How do we put the AgriProve validated branding out there - already have the validation process Environmentally friendly - touch hearts and souls about the premium product - unique and nothing that anyone else can offer Something that catches your eye in a meat cooler Eco-credits - we need to look into it

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Discussion around Greenhams certification and the criteria they needed. Sent him EOS imagery and gave him account for Crop Monitoring as an observer Vegetation score - groundcover Kg of carbon emitted/kg of weight gain

Chat with Justin RE: Ruminati (8th May 24) Ruminati provide tangible accounting of farm management decisions Moving from what we think we know to something visual and easy to interact with What value prop can we give our customers - something like this is perfect for client interaction We need to have an active mechanism to give this sort of information Currently our emissions discussions are not a good visual representation of management decisions (spreadsheet based) Wen need to (through a tool like this) give them (our landholders and prospects) active scenarios with calcs of how their management changes would effect their carbon balance We need to go on a competitor watch and see the partners they are creating (highly influential) - would give us massive market penetration to partner with Ruminati What does this really give a farmer? - speeds up the process to get a quicker result on the validation piece to their management This is what we are lacking in our offering - pathways to get to net a quicker result - how do we make it easier to do a carbon audit Gives our landholders a triple A rating - auditing - great baseline tool that is farmer and supply chain accepted + government validated emissions sequestration AP should do a validation every 6 months - would be significantly easier and less time consuming with a product such as this AgriProve could provide EOFY Ruminati report AP shouldn't want to replicate the same product - partner and make a commercial agreement - and make the exponential progress Look at who they are ready integrated to - leverage their network We are a $150,000 (300 clients at $500 each) client for 25 years - that's a huge value add for them Want to have tools in the tool box - already have ceres tags and the soil testing internally - this could be a great add-on Rumninati cover the negative aspect - emissions - why wouldn't we look to just buy them out? And tell the whole story Bring on their existing clients and tell the other half of the story Gotta tell the positive - they will want to bring that in their suite of products - they don't do the positive aspects but they are tied in to a suite of partners As a farmer with their service you pay just to know you are a polluter - let us tell your positive aspect - fill their gap with landholders they already have on-board Create a licence agreement or partnership or a pathway for integrating into their clientele Potential for a commercial subscription? Once landholders are signed up create a baseline score for them and give them the option to play with management scenarios Works hand in hand with our products Helps grass fed producers get better market access - we need to look at end producer - grassfed programs Justin sees holes in his story - these are hard to explain - this plugs a massive hole - need to work on our enemy (emissions story tellers) Go to end user - Coles - pitch our product to tell whole picture - negative and positive - do you want to know more - show them Ready Graze with carbon accounting Justin wants $0.20 more per every kg produced due to validation - hard to make a profit right now because of the market - needs to show something different More market access for the positive management the more money landholders can put into the management of their carbon project

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Spoke to Justin about the certification and sustainability piece. Gave great responses, very interested

Responses to sustainability questionnaire: Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? - Yes - GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy - If no, then why not? - N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? - GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management - How can we make the testing attractive and simple - Very honourous - Teas - JBS - TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? - Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? - If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business - Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? - Not direct to consumers - Have looked at the big supply chains - Looked into Greenham’s - Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand - Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? - TBD - Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to - Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals

engagements.subject: Sustainability certification questions
engagements.body: Good afternoon Justin, Thank you for being so generous with your time today. Below are the responses to the questions we discussed. Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? * Yes * GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy If no, then why not? * N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? * GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management * How can we make the testing attractive and simple * Very honourous * Teas * JBS * TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? * Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? * If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business * Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? * Not direct to consumers * Have looked at the big supply chains * Looked into Greenham’s * Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand * Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? * TBD * Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to * Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals Kind regards, Dylan

RMIT would like to sample only CEA 1, the highest performing CEA, and to resample T0, T1, and T2 points to understand change over time. Please note that this will have no impact on your compliant project sampling rounds and this data is not shared with the regulator. engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Chatted to JC about his ACCUs and sharing his profile. He has an idea around the data we are collecting and wanting to create a provenance story using combined AP data and genomics. Looking to put together a proposal to articulate his ideas. Notes from meeting below: Need to validate outcomes Outcomes of carbon project aligned with high quality cattle management AgriProvenance - a failsafe system to prove the traceability Genomics - outcomes of the cattle (when the herd is at feed conversion) T4T, EOS, genomics = package to producers Genomically verify all the bulls - create auditable trails Prove the animals are the best ranking in a carbon sense Potentially use Gallagher / optiweigh and validate the measurements Collect the information and overlay into the program - herd/provenance Each animal verified through genomics, lifetime carbon project measured, kgs produced, kgs emitted, ongoing efficiencies - totalling a value MSA graded product vs reliability Whole of life information - green training wheels on the animal Breed outcome - market ready at a certain time Steer select - animals that will produce best on farm AgriProvenance , net emissions, credits, management strategy - making the farm very transparent Metrics - DOB Genomic testing $40 per head - data to make key decisions Give the data to make an assumption after birth (6 months) these are my highest ranking individuals - keep only the efficient animals on farm (carbon benefit based on efficiency) Improvement on feed efficiency and outcomes Making decisions based on long-term gains Is breeders are inefficient they enter the food supply Over the carbon project you have a high performing herd - go to for efficiencies AgriProvenance adds value to customer - health protocol, vaccine's, health status What AP has is soil - JC can provide the stable products Provenance also goes into the grains/timber, etc. Real tool is good outcomes Validation of bloodline, performance, and carbon story - QR to public page (T carbon produced, T carbon emitted, carbon story and ACCUs) Everything auditbale in a CP and passing audits Best practice and best management that is scalable Go and target Angus Australia

engagements.subject: AgriProve preliminary baseline estimate
engagements.body: Hi Kobi, I hope you are well. I have just complete a preliminary assessment of your property for you. I hope this will help to give you an indication of cost to baseline the remaining eligible project areas across your properties. After speaking with Christophe he has informed me that all eligible areas of Polma have been covered by the FarmLab sampling. AgriProve can offer you 30 cores or approximately 350Ha of baseline sampling costs covered by the Hone Grant. This equates to around $13,000 of subsidies. To maximize the amount of hectares covered by the grant we would suggest utilising the Hone grant on Rocky Springs at this stage. A remaining 400Ha across the two properties would need to be covered by you. This would cost approximately $15,000-$17,000 depending on the final size of the project areas once mapping has been complete. This price is only cost recovery and AgriProve does not make any money off this service. AgriProve offers two methods of payment for the baseline cost. The first is a standard invoice to be paid after baseline sampling has been complete. The second is a no-interest deferred payment option paid back in Australian Carbon Credit Units (ACCUs) issued to the project at a rate of $12.50 per ACCU. If there is any outstanding amount after 5 years, it must be paid in full by cash. To take advantage of the Hone grant offer available to the first 25 landholders who accept it, you will need to complete our engagement form called the Consent to Register - Commitment to Implement (CTR-CTI) and also complete our Data Use and Collection Agreement for the grant (both attached). While crediting won't take place on an annual basis, over the long term this is a number you could expect to see. engagements.body: Hi Kobi, Great to catch up yesterday and thanks again for your time. As we went through together, I have updated the letter and had our two Directors, Matthew and Stephen Warnken, sign it overnight. Please see attached for your counter signatures. Regarding point 14.2.3 of the Master Terms, I have confirmed that it only references the ACCUs which may have been issued to the project to that time. It is a way for the Operator to terminate the agreement of their own volition (i.e. not due to any wrong-doing by AgriProve) without exposing AgriProve to the liability of repaying any issued ACCUs. engagements.body: Hi Kobi, I hope you’re well. Just clarifying that 100% of ACCUs issued to that point would need to be repaid by the Operator in that scenario. If a 25% success fee had already been paid to AgriProve (as that is the fee for service) then this would need to be repaid by the Operator too. It’s not 125% of ACCUs, it’s still 100%, however AgriProve’s service fee is ACCUs not cash so that’s where the confusion lies. If we charged cash for the service provided then AgriProve obviously would not be paying back our fee, and the Operator would still need to pay back 100% of the ACCUs whether they had used them or not, given the situation would only arise if the Operator chooses to terminate a successful project. It is the same situation but 25% have been used to pay AgriProve for the services already rendered. Happy to jump on a call if I can clarify it further. Would it help to hear from anyone else, I can certainly facilitate feedback from another landholder for example? engagements.subject: Grazing Management Changes and Timeline
engagements.body: Hi Jeff, Thanks for your time just before, as discussed, the CER has asked about the grazing practice changes you have made. Specifically, the first water upgrades in 2021, and some sub-divisions of paddocks. We need to show a clear timeline of additional fencing upgrades/changes post the April 2022 declaration, as well as changes to stocking rates/durations of grazing following the seeding and application of Rural Boss. When we were on site, I remember you saying you're constantly making changes, based on behaviours to optimise the approach and your grazing management, so I do not think we will have an issue showing this change. As a first step, whilst you're putting together some timelines against your notes, can you please send me some photos of your grazing charts (as many years back as you have) We did have an option to not have grazing included as an eligible activity, however given it is central to your operation, I do not want to let this eligible activity go. The positive is that whilst there is a query on this aspect of grazing, the other implementation activities of pasture rejuvenation and nutrient application (Rural Boss spray) have been accepted and there is no risk to the overall application of credits. engagements.subject: RE: Re questions re "Reef Credits"
engagements.body: Hi Jeff, Yes, the platform is basing its assessment of eligibility off geographical location within the reef catchment areas. A Reef Credit project and Soil Carbon sequestration project can co-exist and we are actively targeting those landholders with an existing project with us that may be interested in Reef credits under the Grazing Land Management (GLM) method. I’ll pass your query over to Bill Hyem in our team to look further into this for you. Natural sequence farming seems like it would be a great addition to the property from my limited knowledge on it, and should help reduce fine sediment loss and nutrient runoff. However, there are some points to be aware of to be eligible for a GLM Reef credit project: * one or more additional or new management activities is implemented, * management activities are reasonably expected to improve ground cover for water quality improvement that are beyond what is required by legislation or pre-existing formal obligations, * grazing is the principle land use for the last seven years, and * broad scale clearing of woody vegetation has not occurred within the previous seven years. From the looks of it, if you were to start a reef credit project based purely on implementing natural sequence farming principles the project would go under the “Gully Method” which involves landscape rehabilitation and construction. We may struggle to prove additionality under the Grazing method as it would need to be a new activity relative to what you’re already doing with the carbon project. See attached guidance on Reef credits under the Grazing Land Management Methodology. We’ll get back to you with our thoughts after reviewing the situation further. From: Jeff Bell Sent: Sunday, 2 February 2025 2:55 PM To: Dylan Jones Subject: Re questions re "Reef Credits" Hi Dylan, The Agriprove platform said "Generate income through a Reef Credit project Your property is eligible to undertake a Reef Credit Project." Is this correct or is it just that we are geographically eligible? Can a reef credit project co-exist with a carbon project? I have been looking into "natural sequence farming" which is all about keeping water and dissolved nutrients on farm through modifying existing contour drains and/or constructing level contours.(which fits neatly into what the "reef credit project" would be looking to achieve. Attended a "natural sequence farming" field day yesterday and there was so much that explained why areas of our farm have limited performance compared to the mean. If we spend money on training and earthworks to keep more water and nutrients on our farm(approx 94 % of which is under a carbon project) would we be eligible for a "reef credit project"? Jeff Bell

engagements.subject: Re: Re questions re "Reef Credits"
engagements.body: Hi Dylan, Definitely would not be grazing management as that is already done. It would be remedial earth works to modify the existing drain contours and where needed construct new contours to slow the flow of water and nutrients and keep both on farm rather than running off down the waterway which does come in the list of gully management methodology activities. Most of the farm can benefit from this in productivity(and consequently carbon sequestration) but only about 30 percent of the farm(my guestimate) has substandard ground cover which in my opinion could release some sediment and nutrients off farm. My take is that the amount of sediment lost from the farm in its current condition would be to low to bother with. The only place where there would be any amount would be a bit hard to manage as it comes pouring through from next door in a water way only a couple of hundred metres from our bottom fence. If Agriprove think there is anything worth pursuing then I will think about it. I myself think not but that is an opinion not based on knowledge. engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Jeff, I have just completed your yearly satellite assessment for your carbon project. As you know we use this as an indicator for if we think resampling would be worthwhile. Your assessment this year ( attached) has shown an increase in the average NDRE from baseline to current period and an increase in the past year. This indicates that re-sampling this year would be worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration. This does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased. We need to complete the physical sampling to know what is happening in the ground. Next steps: Before we schedule the resampling date, we need to complete the phone call section of the review. Is there a time next week that would suit to do that? I have some prep I need to do before the call so locking in a time in advance works best. If you have any questions please let me know. Talk soon. engagements.body: Good Moring Jeff, Yeah it is completely possible for us to do that. Do you know exactly what tests you want done? engagements.subject: Tags for Tonnes Update and Webinar
engagements.body: Good afternoon Tony, Happy Beef Week! I hope you and the family are doing well. I thought I would provide you an update on AgriProve's Tags for Tonnes, and provide you some of the thoughts expressed from a early participant in the program. Here's our latest webinar where you can hear the insights gained already by one of our early participants, Justin Costello: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dO20F2IcxSo [cid:9b0f43b8-d8f1-443f-a265-ef701d8f8a65] Tags for Tonnes Webinar - Unlocking Your Farms Potential www.youtube.com AgriProve has been roaring along with the Tags for Tonnes program delivering actionable insights for landholders involved in carbon projects. The software is already providing the best in-class translation of the insights offered through Ceres Tags. We are now developing additional insights to complement those currently available. Watch this space for upcoming features: * Digitised hands-free and objective grazing diary (no data inputs required). * Pasture health monitoring - assistive satellite indices focussed on pasture health and rest and recovery, to assist your grazing rotations for optimal pasture to carbon conversion. * Additional IoT integrations. I hope everything is going well on farm and that you are happy, healthy and profitable. Have a great week!! engagements.body: Hi Bill, YesBill happy for you to retest and see how the soil carbon is going we are very dry at present but in one paddock I have planted a mix of all species and it is improving ground cover species and having a active growing plant. Improvements in NDRE > relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for > increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. > > > > The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the > current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project > is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there > are many other factors that can influence sequestration and these results > do not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased. We will not know > until the physical sampling has been undertaken. engagements.subject: Re: Request to resample Howson Carbon Projects
engagements.body: G'day Bill, Thanks for the email. That sounds great and will work in well to do a retest starting May 22. I just need to sit down and look at the at the different projects but i'm happy to go with the 2 that showed the biggest movement from the satellite data if that works for you? Regards, Adam Gunthorpe Tarramba Red Brahmans "Tarramba" Banana QLD 4702 Ph:0402630907 www.tarramba.com.au ________________________________ From: AgriProve Sent: Monday, 24 April 2023 2:24 AM To: tracy@tarramba.com ; adam@tarramba.com Subject: Request to resample Howson Carbon Projects Hi Adam and Tracy, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your projects. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached) for 14 of the 15 projects you have registered, which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. engagements.subject: AgriProve community event
engagements.body: Good evening Adam, I hope you and your family are all well! AgriProve is excited to invite you to join us in Colosseum at Kylie and Lance Stephenson’s property for an AgriProve community event. A big thank you to Kylie and Lance for hosting the occasion! The event will be held on Wednesday 22nd of November at 1142 Blackmans Gap Road, Colosseum. Kick off will be at 10am, finishing at approximately 2pm. The days agenda: Morning Presentations: 10am – 12:00pm The morning will be a chance to learn about some of AgriProve’s new initiatives. Learn about the new opportunity to integrate cattle monitoring with your AgriProve soil carbon project and find out about the new reef credit opportunities upcoming through the Reef Credits: Grazing Land Management method, developed in partnership with Verterra and Greencollar. We are also excited to have a presentation from our keynote speaker, Mr Hobbs Magaret, coming all the way from the USA. Hobbs is a rancher from east Texas, founder of Sisters Cattle Co. and an expert in using ultra-high density grazing to maximise carbon drawdown and production efficiency. BBQ Lunch: 12:00 – 12:45 Following presentations there will be a chance to unwind with BBQ lunch and refreshments provided. Afternoon Farm Tour: 12:45 – 2:00pm To wrap up the day we will all head out for a farm tour led by Lance and Kylie to see what they are focusing on currently. It will also be an opportunity for everyone share stories about what has worked for them. If you are able to make it, we would love to see you there for what will be a great opportunity to meet others, share knowledge and a bite to eat. Please accept this invitation as soon as possible to RSVP. This will help us get an idea of numbers ahead of time. For any dietary requirements for yourself or the two others with you, please let me know in advance at william@agriprove.io or team@agriprove.io. Kind regards, Team at AgriProve

engagements.subject: Call with Adam Gunthorpe
engagements.body: Had a chat with Adam to follow up on T4T pitch. Key focus is genetics piece, would only be looking for cash payment (sees the ACCU as rip off) - discussed line of credit and pricing similar to credit card as well as fact that ACCUs allow improved management outcomes for them to pay themselves. Has passed info on to breeding group (David Johnson and Matt Willcot). They want to validate everything through BreedPlan. They don't want raw data they want to feed outcomes into BreedPlan - want us to connect with AGBU and feed Net feed intake into their systems. Interest is in Net feed intake and methane quantification - probably requires tailored plan addressing these aspects. Talked to the fact Methane is quantified and validated in the tags by CSIRO's calibration farm - if we can produce a link between AGBU research and CSIRO think will help validate the tech for him as he doesn't currently have a plan for how they quantify their methane.

engagements.subject: Request to Resample Howson Carbon Project 11
engagements.body: Hi Adam & Tracy, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. Can you please confirm that you are happy for us to come and resample your project areas within the period of June/July 2024? Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. The attached factsheet has information regarding resampling process but if you have any other questions, please let me know. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. Kind regards, Jo. engagements.body: Good afternoon Adam, As mentioned yesterday, we are currently expanding our online customer portal capability and onboarding process. Following up from our conversation, here is some additional information and we request that you please confirm via response to this email that you are happy and agree that we can use details of you and your farm for the purposes outlined below. For the online customer portal, we are building a mock-up version to demonstrate our new capabilities. The app and information shown is for the purpose of showcasing our capabilities to prospective investors. It will not be available or used beyond this confidential environment. The process flow of the app will show onboarding a new landholder and will capture land titles, enterprise information necessary to calculate a farm's emissions and the emissions intensity of farm outputs along with some other sustainability scores. We are also looking to showcase carbon projects that are in action and achieving results from our 'Champion' producers, which we would like to use your carbon projects as an example. The personally identifiable information that would be displayed include: • Name (although we could rename if you prefer) • Tile picture showing your photo (again if you prefer we can use a mock image or farm image) • Carbon Project and Strata boundaries • Sampling results – points on a map with hover over basic lab result info • Modelled ground cover map • Modelled Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) variability map • Summarised SOC measurements • Farm management activities • Livestock turnoff numbers (head and class of livestock) • Stocking rate (head and class of livestock) • Farm area (ha) • Potential ACCU yield based on rainfall band and soil type and internal data etc. Could you please confirm we can use your farm and profile as the Champion Farmer and Project? I have looped Andrew into this email, and let the team known that much of this detail will be useful in a prospectus of your own, to showcase your business outcomes to the market. Formalising our approval process - customer facing materials
engagements.body: All, With our growth strategy gathering momentum - the amount of materials that go “customer facing” is on the up. It will be no news to any of you the risks that are inherent in this from both reputational and compliance perspectives. So, it’s time to formalise an approach. It’s very simple, but will add time and you will need to plan time for an approval process. What’s the Approval process? 1. Any customer facing material (for now), but we’ll likely need to extend this later. 2. Must have a review and approval from AB, KW and DW before going to SU. 3. The author requesting an approval from SU must include either the email chain or attach the emails with the approvals. 4. AB, KW and DW – in your review you are accountable for, grammar, formatting, brand, tone of voice, technical and process accuracy. By the time it gets to SU it should be in tip top shape. You may think this is a pain. But reflect on every typo you’ve picked up in an email you’ve received. How you’ve commented on poor formatting, confusing messaging or thought. “I got the same detail from someone else yesterday”, or worse still “someone told me something different yesterday”. The idea is to make sure that everything we do is high quality and consistent. Thanks TH Toby Hedgeland | Head of Product and Delivery [AgriProve] Phone: 1300 GO SOIL (1300 46 7645) Mobile: 0466602196 Email: toby@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [AgriProve Email Signature Designs (3).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:image003.png@01DA6FE8.F7AFCB80] [cid:image004.png@01DA6FE8.F7AFCB80] [cid:image005.png@01DA6FE8.F7AFCB80] [cid:image006.png@01DA6FE8.F7AFCB80] Here at we care for your privacy. engagements.subject: Formalising our approval process - customer facing materials
engagements.body: All, With our growth strategy gathering momentum - the amount of materials that go “customer facing” is on the up. It will be no news to any of you the risks that are inherent in this from both reputational and compliance perspectives. So, it’s time to formalise an approach. It’s very simple, but will add time and you will need to plan time for an approval process. What’s the Approval process? 1. Any customer facing material (for now), but we’ll likely need to extend this later. 2. Must have a review and approval from AB, KW and DW before going to SU. 3. The author requesting an approval from SU must include either the email chain or attach the emails with the approvals. 4. AB, KW and DW – in your review you are accountable for, grammar, formatting, brand, tone of voice, technical and process accuracy. By the time it gets to SU it should be in tip top shape. You may think this is a pain. But reflect on every typo you’ve picked up in an email you’ve received. How you’ve commented on poor formatting, confusing messaging or thought. “I got the same detail from someone else yesterday”, or worse still “someone told me something different yesterday”. The idea is to make sure that everything we do is high quality and consistent. Thanks TH Toby Hedgeland | Head of Product and Delivery [AgriProve] Phone: 1300 GO SOIL (1300 46 7645) Mobile: 0466602196 Email: toby@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [AgriProve Email Signature Designs (3).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:image003.png@01DA6FE8.F7AFCB80] [cid:image004.png@01DA6FE8.F7AFCB80] [cid:image005.png@01DA6FE8.F7AFCB80] [cid:image006.png@01DA6FE8.F7AFCB80] Here at we care for your privacy. Please be respectful of people’s time and avoid requesting approval ASAP as this may not always be possible. The longer lead time the better. Call with Maki Update from Julien Ready to keep rolling out projects Not a deep pool of projects, max 250 worldwide (80 in Australia) Because of this will need to roll out other services Focus is on how they get close to fighting fire Fire technologies and selling those outside of carbon MRV system in Africa (doesn't exist) Think their blueprint should look a lot like AP tech stack Ideally would just use the AgriProve platform: Use the marketplace to sell fire equipment Fire insights Want us to build for them Theirs is a forecasting model - GIS analysis then calculations around sequestration, also developing platform to inform Model for working together? Do we have the same overlapping clients? Mostly graziers, family owned, but majority in monsoonal areas in FNQ. Not super obvious that we would have overlapping customers. How to build soil carbon in savannah landscapes? engagements.subject: AgriProve - Lynch Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Hi Derek, Thank you for your patience with us completing your annual review. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The increase from the previous period to the current period has not met our threshold (shown in the attached report), we will not be resampling this year. Your project will be reviewed again next year. Note that we have a requirement under the method to sample your project a minimum of once every five years. I am working on the other items that we discussed on Friday regarding T0-T1 results and an overlay of your paddocks with the carbon project boundaries. As always if you have any questions, feel free to reach out to any of the team. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Morning Derek, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon project. We do these every 12 months using satellite imagery of the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) on your farm to get an idea of if the vegetation has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample at this time. As you will see in the attached document, your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it means that compared to baseline the average trend has not be positive comparatively - which is an indicator that carbon sequestration has been unlikely at this time. This result means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. We will review this again next year or when our HORIZON model is fully up and running to decide if resampling would be worthwhile then. if you have any questions or would like to touch base about your carbon project- feel free to call me anytime. engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Lynch CP
engagements.body: Dear Derek, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. Hi Adam, I hope you are having a great week! Lovely to meet you in person a couple of weeks ago, thanks again for having us. Please see attached your updated results maps for the RMIT project sampling. The method used for the visualisation is called Inverse Distance Weighted, Manual Interval. This extrapolates the results over the whole project area. We have included the points so you can see how this method has extrapolated over the broader area. We also get a lot of questions on the moisture vs gravimetric water tests - The moisture % is reported on a dry basis = (wet weight – dry weight) / dry weight. Whilst the gravimetric water is the loss of mass in grams on drying at 105 degrees C. As they are reported on a different basis you cannot calculate the moisture % from the gravimetric water. Any questions please give me a bell. Mel

engagements.subject: CERES TAG data issue update
engagements.body: Good evening Adam, I’d like to provide an update on the data matter appearing since activation on your new batch of CERES RANCH Tags. We were the first to report an issue showing our diligence and care towards your projects. In summary, in March 2024, CERES TAG had firmware updated with a new design from CSIRO to improve battery life, accuracy, reliability and flexibility to update with additional algorithms. The Pasture Feed Intake (PFI) was not anticipated to operate differently from the previous firmware on this updated and improved model, however this was not the case. The team at CERES TAG and CSIRO are working to remedy the algorithm now to restore to performance equivalent to that pre-March. This week a patch fix was deployed to in-field testing. There is no issue with the GPS location data. Your animal location monitoring is unaffected. As we learn more about their progress towards a resolution, we will keep you informed. We thank you for your support, understanding and patience. If you have any questions, don’t hesitate to contact me. engagements.subject: Questions from todays sustainability convo
engagements.body: Evening Adam thank you for being so generous with your time today. Below are the answers, please feel free to add anything you may think of. Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? * No * Very, very limited amount * Someone else doing sustainability certification – biology outsomes and plant outcomes If no, then why not? * Wasn’t sure how to get value from it * Not direct selling so criteria you he needs to meet is more what the processors want – grass fed/ * Not a sustainability credential to give you more money through * Teys Wagga Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? * Not really Would you want to explore the criteria to have a sustainability certification applied to your produce? * Yep Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? * Yeah – need to be some kind of payback for it – need to see the return Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? * Looked into a Provenir pathway but nothing happened with it What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? * Not sure as of now * What can help us build carbon faster * Utilizing sampling as a service and get more info from the samples (nutrients) and providing a mapping representation * Change of soil quality over time (pH as example) * Haney style testing (sampling as a service) * Change of available nutrients over time – proof point of management providing what is there * * Kind regards, Dylan Cronje | Innovation Project Coordinator [AgriProve] Phone: 1300 GO SOIL (1300 46 7645) Mobile: +61419940230 Email: dylan@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [AgriProve Email Signature Designs (3).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:dfdde679-d4de-4546-bf4c-29fda0f434fc] [cid:5c366fe3-a84a-44c3-8fcb-9f8cfb700027] [cid:75b93eaa-9be3-4f65-a65c-f68707a39740] [cid:d935d0dc-8a0f-4355-ad19-74fe46085322] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. engagements.subject: Consent request - use of Leeston farm maps in promotional material
engagements.body: Hi Adam, Hope things are travelling well in the Rabjohn's household at the moment. As one of our pioneering landholders you are often trying new things ahead of the crowd. These test and trials are often of great value to our other landholders and interesting for those considering a carbon project. To that end I wanted to formally check in on what you are, and most importantly aren't comfortable sharing. We have quite the repository of great imagery and maps of your property! I've attached a piece that I would like your consent to use in promotional material. The document is our new Carbon Ready Report (CRR). The reports assess the carbon sequestration potential of land, so that landholders have an idea of what they might be able to achieved with commitment to improved land management before starting a project. To promote the CRR we would like to have a dummy report that can be shared with prospects. In preparing the dummy I have used your farm maps. On the first page the map includes the name "Woodhouselee road" so makes it location-identifiable. This is my key concern and reason for checking in with you. Can you please confirm that you are happy for us to use this dummy report. It will not reference you or your property - it will just be the maps that are potentially identifiable. Happy to discuss this or any question you have on this. And as always thanks for your continued support! engagements.subject: Call with Adam Rabjohns
engagements.body: Spoke to Adam Rabjohns about the arrival of his Optiweigh unit. Optiweigh has arrived and in paddock. Main motivations being to remove guess work out of management - the data providing him with a guide to adaptive management and understanding if some of his mob are ready for AI. Couldn't be more stoked about the unit and the animals seem to love the protein supplement.

Reached out to Adam via Whatsapp to see if he was happy to chat to a prospect of Bill's who wants to speak to someone who has introduced dung beetles. Happy to chat with them and also shared a post from his FB about the topic. His FB is a great resource for management practice we would like to encourage. https://www.facebook.com/share/p/jL1bcbjYEox4LRgB/

Adam is redesigning his paddocks so he can intensify grazing and allow for automation (fence lifters) - to facilitate 3 moves + per day. Blue lines = permanent water lane - can walk back through areas grazed without having to access/overgraze other paddocks Green lines = permanent electric fencing (150m wide) Mob is 240 cows with 240 calves - get 3 chunks (paddock rotations) per day - 8am, 12pm, 6pm Rotations dependent on rain, grass and rest - currently paddocks they are grazing now are 100+ days rest (Some areas of them are even more) - recovery on some areas due to low spring rains are only just happening.

engagements.subject: Call with Adam Rabjohns
engagements.body: Notes stored.

Called Adam to let him know about the platform launch and his Ready Graze account being integrated. Feedback as follows: sign up to platform was quick and easy has been hearing about rewards for farmers ($20 / head) for adopting feed supplements (asparagopsis) and wanted to know who provides that and why (is it market driven or gvt) tags are not relevant to his situation - they are just another data source with little use, because he is physically seeing and moving them every day they have no real advantage - data is too descript with no0 real outcome context Optiweigh is incredibly useful for adaptive management and understanding how they are performing and where to improve dung beetles on farm are popping out everywhere and exploding in numbers

Had a recent chat with Adam notes as follows: He is no longer using the Optiweigh unit and is open to us gifting it to someone else The reason is he is grazing too intensively and can't keep up with the labour requirements to move that frequently @Claudia Bryant he is a great manager moving 3 times a day using a Total grazing approach (super high density, single mob (420 head over 1ha) he has just re-fenced his farm to facilitate strip grazing so he can utilise automatic fence lifters to facilitate the 3 moves per day

We can then do the upstream training which we usually do over 3 sessions (all usually 30 mins of content and scheduled for 45mins): 1. What to do when first logged in. Aimed at making sure everyone is set up correctly. * Ensure the team know where to connect email to log communications * Outlook add on * How to navigate around and find information * Leave it there and let them explore 2. Justin Costello rang alongside farmer who is interested, and I explained the model and process, and sent follow up info as below.

Hi Phil,Great to chat just now. Please see attached the information pack, an overview and the fine print. Sounds like it's a good time to baseline!Baseline sampling costs for a 330ha area would be approximately $7000-$8000. As I said we are covering the costs of future sampling rounds. In general these are conducted and credits awarded every 2-5 years depending on how quickly carbon is sequestered.If you would like to sign up the first step is completing and returning the Consent to Register form attached, which provides us with permission to register your project on your behalf. Some basic farm management history is required.If your brother is interested in carbon for vegetation projects, he can find out more from our sister company Green Collar on 03 8080 8916 or greencollar.com.au.If you have any further questions, please feel free to give me a call on 0439 457 799.Kind regards,Melanie

Followed up Phil and had a good talk through all the detail. Sent follow up email as below. The area has been neglected and he would like to do pasture improvement anyway. It needs a lot of lime as very acidic to unlock nutrients. There is an area that has scrub that he'd like to clear to implement pastures. Some 1.2 to 1.5 meters high, some 5-6m high. I need to look up regs and get back to him on how this impacts soil carbon project. He has a secondary business building water controls, fish ladders and screens etc.

Hi Phil,Great to chat just now! Please see attached the Land Management Strategy as discussed and also the Sales and Licence Agreement.I have also attached the Consent to Register which is the first step.It does take a month or so to get registered and get the mapping done, so if you are keen it would be ideal to get registered sooner rather than later as to baseline in the sweet spot.If you have any other questions please feel free to give me a call on 0439 457 799.Kind regards,Melanie
Spoke to Phil. He is going to speak with Justin about his experience. Then call me back to let me know where he is at.

engagements.subject: RE: McClelland Carbon Project variation (ERF173553)- Online Services RFI [SEC=OFFICIAL]
engagements.body: OFFICIAL Hi Imogen, The following was sent to the project primary contact via Online Services: Further information is required by the Clean Energy Regulator (the Regulator) to assess whether your application made under s31 of the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011 (the CFI Act) meets the eligibility requirements for the variation of the declaration of an eligible offsets project. This notice to give information has been made by the Regulator in accordance with s26(1) of the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Rule 2015 (the CFI Rule). S26(1) of the CFI Rule enables the Regulator to require, by written notice, an applicant to give the Regulator, within the period specified in the notice, further information in connection with the application. The further information required by the Regulator to assess the application, and the timeframe within which it must be supplied by, is provided with this notice. Under s25(3) of the CFI Rule, the Regulator must take all reasonable steps to ensure that a decision is made on the application within 90 days after the applicant gives the Regulator the information required in the notice. Under s26(2) of the CFI Rule, failure to comply with the notice may result in the Regulator refusing to consider the application, or refuse to take any action, or any further action, in relation to the application. Under the Criminal Code Act 1995, it is an offence for a person to give information or documents to a Commonwealth entity if the person providing the information or documents knows that the information or documents are false or misleading. The provision of false or misleading information or documentation may also have consequences under the Act and other laws. The Regulator may retain the documents for as long as necessary. The Notice requires the required information or documents to be provided through Online Services. If you are not able to comply with this requirement, or you have any queries regarding this notice, please contact the CER Contact Centre on 1300 553 542 or email enquiries@cer.gov.au, using the RFI ID supplied with this notice as a reference. * Under the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011, section 28A(3), eligible interest holder consent must be in a form approved by the Regulator. * Please provide a completed EIH form signed by the landholder. * Part 2 subsection 7(g), (h) and (i) of the CFI Rule require signed statements by the applicant. The provided authority to sign on behalf of the applicant document only has the signature of one company director. Section 127 of the Corporations Act 2001 requires documents to be signed by: (a) 2 directors of the company; or (b) a director and a company secretary of the company. Please provide an updated authority to sign that has been signed by 2 directors or a director and secretary. Kind regards, Bonnie [cid:image007.png@01DB02B3.7A93A6E0] [signature_410057662] [signature_1894695697] [cid:image010.png@01DB02B3.7A93A6E0] [signature_1646576931] Bonnie Scott (she/her) Assistant Manager - Savanna, Agriculture and Soil Section Soi, Emissions Avoidance and Contracts Branch | Scheme Operations Division Contact Centre P: 1300 553 542 E: enquiries@cer.gov.au [A black text on a white background Description automatically generated] OFFICIAL From: Imogen Hickey Sent: Monday, September 9, 2024 10:14 AM To: CER - ERF Soil Savanna and Agriculture Subject: McClelland Carbon Project variation (ERF173553)- Online Services RFI [SEC=OFFICIAL] Hi Ruby, I am responding to your email regarding the RFI for McClelland Carbon Project on behalf of Rebekah Ash as she is currently completing her PhD overseas and is only working one day a week with AgriProve. engagements.subject: AgriProve Baseline timeline
engagements.body: Hi Melissa, I spoke with Kieren our Head of Operations and he advised me that we must meet The Clean Energy Regulators consent to operate the carbon project in order to baseline. In essence that means we need to agree to consent to register, the sales and license agreement and the terms and conditions in order to proceed with baselining. engagements.body: Hi Merlin, I've added some more information in the attachment above. We need to align this Consent to Register (CTR) with the terminology that the Clean Energy Regulator requests. There are a couple of points: 1. Signatures, those that need to sign If the landtitle is under a company, we will need at least two signatures unless it is a sole director. In the instance of two owners, we would need a director and secretary or both directors to sign off. If you send me through those names of the owners, I can add those to the CTR. 1. Additional Comments Can we include some top level history of the farmers stewardship of the land, such as years of experience, any awarded courses etc. We have experienced requests for additional information by the clean energy regulator. 1. Historic Farm Records These can come later, but we will need to collect 5 years of farm management history as we register the project. engagements.subject: Re: AgriProve Baseline timeline
engagements.body: Hi Merlin, A soil carbon project under the Australian Carbon Credit Scheme, the land must have been in agricultural production for the past 5 years and evidenced with management records. Often historic records are often guestimates (often the case with farmers) or has changed ownership, which is totally fine. In the instance of no/patchy records, we would take any information as a statutory declaration to form the emissions baseline, i.e. the positive side of the carbon equation. For the duration of the project, we would re-assess emissions to give a relative carbon footprint to the sequestration into soils. Based on our conversation to date, it has been my understanding that the parcel of land has been in agricultural production. @Melissa Murchison I have also been advised that we are happy to proceed with baseline sampling if we have a complete consent to register document. This will require historic records in some form before proceeding. I appreciate this can be a complicated data collection exercise, so I'm happy to help where I can. engagements.subject: Finalised Consent to Register
engagements.body: Hi Melissa and Merlin, Please see the attached Consent to Register that we will require sign off from the landowners. Once these are signed off by the landowners we will have the ability to begin the registration process. The blank historic records are fine, as we will make claim to the land being in Bare Fallow for the previous 5 years. In the attached CTR we will need 3 signatures from the joint landowners, we will need landowner initials on page 1 names and signatures on page 5 (image below). [cid:f2b4ed5e-504c-4de1-bf82-621ee7040356] The next steps once the Consent to Register documentation is received, we will need to do the following: * Accurately map out the areas, and provide explanation for how the land is deemed eligible, and the approach we will take to sampling * When mapping out areas and infrastructure, determine whether it meets our threshold for carbon project (CTR has 67ha of land, if we map out 20Ha due to solar panels and infrastructure, does that preclude us from undertaking the project) * Understand the timeline for construction of the panels – as it’s unlikely that there will be no carbon building activities, and in all likelihood will decrease the current soil carbon stocks. Which would also make it preferable to sample after construction for the two reasons above. * Draft up Key Commercial Term and send out asap, so that we can all appropriate structures and signatures in place for ongoing legal right, as it’s unclear who will be carrying out activities, who is receiving the ACCUs, who is responsible for on-ground compliance, monitoring, reporting, record keeping etc, and for our communications. Again, those dot points can be all managed once we get the signatures off the landowners. engagements.subject: AgriProve, novation clauses and sale of property
engagements.body: Hi Melissa, Thanks for the call yesterday and great to hear we are making progress with the landholder on the carbon project. In the attached Master Terms and Conditions, there are several clauses around the Operator (in this case BSR): * "If Operator is to cease being the operator of any Project Property, Landholder and Operator agree to notify AgriProve as soon as they are aware and to novate this Agreement (to the extent it applies to Operator and the relevant Project Property) to the new operator of the Project Property." In the scenario where BSR sells the project AND/OR the landholder sells the underlying land asset, AgriProve holds responsibility for continuing the project - with the novation clause above, we would re-contract with the incoming Operator or Landholder. AgriProve is the proponent to all of our customers soil carbon projects - as seen here on the ERF registry . This means we absorb all requirements to continue the project under the scenarios mentioned above. Please let me know if there are any further questions. engagements.subject: Sampling Results - Nox 2024
engagements.body: Hi Ross, Please see attached the results from the last round of sampling completed on the two project areas. In summary: * Chifley Carbon Project is now 650 tC above the baseline carbon stock and has shown a consistent increasing trend since the sampling round completed in early 2023. This means we can go ahead and begin the process of reporting and applying for ACCUs for this project. * Daly Carbon Project is not above the baseline carbon stock to date however this project shows the same consistent increasing trend since the early 2023 sampling, with three of the 4 CEAs continuing to show gains since 2023. Overall I think these are really positive results. With regard to Chifley Carbon Project, before we can estimate the total ACCU yield we will need to do some work to estimate any emissions associated with the project period to feed into our calculations. I have copied Imogen Hickey to this email who is our crediting specialist, it would be great if we can arrange a time to jump on a video call to talk through the process from here and next steps to work toward lodging an application for ACCUs. Feel free to give me a call or otherwise let us know a time that might suit for a brief meeting.
