From: Ross Thompson Sent: Saturday, 7 June 2025 1:03 PM To: Kieren Whittock Subject: RE: Agriprove form for the CER Hi Kieren, I was wondering if it is possible that we could delay catching up on this until mid Spring? I feel you will have more chance of "cutting through" with me then, when I start heading into our slower time of year (Mid Spring til late Summer). As you know, I am pretty wound up with the CER and their demands and then the fact that "estimates" are OK. I just do not see how I can possibly justify loading up future generations with this burden. But I think, given all the work we have done up til now, I should listen carefully to you, and we should TRY to resolve it and move on. Rather than throwing the baby out with the bath water. No promises that you will be able to swing me around in my attitude. But if you can wait until I am more receptive, I think it gives us the best chance. What are your thoughts? If you are agreeable, have diarised to get in touch with you by email on October 1. I would simply be replying to your email below to get the ball rolling and set aside some time for us to work on it together as you suggested. Regards Ross From: Kieren Whittock > Sent: Friday, 28 March 2025 9:46 PM To: Ross Thompson > Subject: RE: Agriprove form for the CER Hi Ross, So having a look in some more detail here. As discussed we are trying to achieve two things with this information. 1. Show that at least one of the eligible activities has been implemented on the project area 2. Gather the data we need to quantify emissions associated with the project that feed into the calculations Regarding point 1, this is what we are trying to achieve with the Activity Log pages. What is important to note on these activities is that we only need to demonstrate that one of these has occurred, not all of them. As a starting point we could select one that may be the easiest to demonstrate, and only make reference to the others as complimentary activities without being required to demonstrate them in detail or provide detail that is difficult to obtain. From your notes it sounds like this may be achievable. Regarding point 2, if we put aside the stock numbers for the moment, we can strike a few things out from the start. I don't believe irrigation and landscape modification are relevant in your scenario and can be disregarded. That leaves the inputs, which it seems you have some records for, at least for total quantities which we will be able to work with. I also think residues will be able to be resolved given you are primarily a grazing operation and this section is more aimed at cropping operations. Regarding stock numbers, I think it would be worthwhile if we could jump on a quick call with Will at a time that suits you to ask some targeted questions that can help us better determine what can be done. Also, to clarify, the expectation is not for you to fill out the tables provided - we can do this work based on raw information provided, before cross-checking with you that we have interpreted correctly. As discussed, I would be more than happy to come and see you face to face, I could complete as much of this as I can on the fly while there - we have done this a few times previously and has b…

engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: Good Morning Ross, Thanks for sending those details through. We definitely haven't put it in the too hard basket - it just hasn't been an urgent priority up until now as it's coming up to the reporting period date. I will touch base with Kieren and have cc'ed him into this email to see what we can do. In terms of the record keeping - we would never expect you to guess, and it is a lot simpler than it sounds. Most of it is things that you would already have had to collect and would have given to your accountant eg. invoices for expenses such as seed and fertilizer, livestock numbers, fuel used ect. The main thing that the regulator needs is proof that you have changed practices in some way and that you have implemented what you said you would. They don't need extreme detail of every little thing that you have done on farm. If you would find it helpful, I can jump on a call with you and we can look at your map, go through what you've done on your project, what records you have, and put together a bit of a plan/list of what you need to proceed and get this done. Let me know and we can lock in a time to do that. Talk soon. If you need anything feel free to call me anytime. engagements.body: Outbound answered call via Dylan Jones made by Dylan Jones - Call back Ross Thompson +61439179269 Call ID: 3770419144 Chifley Carbon Project — Call Summary Parties: Dylan Jones (AgriProve) & Ross Thompson (landholder) Paddock Configuration Paddock layout has changed since baseline — new fence lines were added in 2021–22 , marked on a sketch map Ross sent through during the call. Eligible Activity — Pasture Rejuvenation (Paddock J4A) Paddock J4A is the only paddock where additional work was carried out. It was cropped for three years (zero-till) , then zero-till pasture was re-established. This occurred last year (i.e. FY2024–25), not FY22–23 as previously recorded — Ross confirmed the earlier record was incorrect. Ross noted he hadn't included it in records due to its small size, but Dylan confirmed it should be documented regardless. Eligible Activity — Grazing Management (Main Activity) Start date confirmed: 01/01/2022. Ross linked this to a significant bull sale in September 2021, after which capital works and intensified grazing management commenced. Dylan had initially suggested 07/01/2021 but Ross preferred 01/01/2022 as more accurate. Declaration date on file: April 2021. Stocking Rate / Grazing Practice Changes Ross does not manage to a specific LSU or head-per-paddock target. His grazing targets are: Maintain pasture sward at 10 cm minimum at all times Target 100% ground cover Average grazing duration per paddock: ~1 week (5–10 days) Previously, stock were set-stocked for up to 6 weeks — a significant change in grazing intensity/duration At any one time, approximately 90% of the property is rested Next Steps Dylan to finalise the landholder statement document and send to Ross for review Ross to sign page 3 (landholder statement page) Following sign-off, move to audit engagement

engagements.subject: Sampling Results - Nox 2024
engagements.body: Hi Ross, Please see attached the results from the last round of sampling completed on the two project areas. In summary: * Chifley Carbon Project is now 650 tC above the baseline carbon stock and has shown a consistent increasing trend since the sampling round completed in early 2023. This means we can go ahead and begin the process of reporting and applying for ACCUs for this project. * Daly Carbon Project is not above the baseline carbon stock to date however this project shows the same consistent increasing trend since the early 2023 sampling, with three of the 4 CEAs continuing to show gains since 2023. Overall I think these are really positive results. With regard to Chifley Carbon Project, before we can estimate the total ACCU yield we will need to do some work to estimate any emissions associated with the project period to feed into our calculations. I have copied Imogen Hickey to this email who is our crediting specialist, it would be great if we can arrange a time to jump on a video call to talk through the process from here and next steps to work toward lodging an application for ACCUs. Feel free to give me a call or otherwise let us know a time that might suit for a brief meeting. From: Ross Thompson Sent: Saturday, 7 June 2025 1:03 PM To: Kieren Whittock Subject: RE: Agriprove form for the CER Hi Kieren, I was wondering if it is possible that we could delay catching up on this until mid Spring? I feel you will have more chance of "cutting through" with me then, when I start heading into our slower time of year (Mid Spring til late Summer). As you know, I am pretty wound up with the CER and their demands and then the fact that "estimates" are OK. I just do not see how I can possibly justify loading up future generations with this burden. But I think, given all the work we have done up til now, I should listen carefully to you, and we should TRY to resolve it and move on. Rather than throwing the baby out with the bath water. No promises that you will be able to swing me around in my attitude. But if you can wait until I am more receptive, I think it gives us the best chance. What are your thoughts? If you are agreeable, have diarised to get in touch with you by email on October 1. I would simply be replying to your email below to get the ball rolling and set aside some time for us to work on it together as you suggested. Regards Ross From: Kieren Whittock > Sent: Friday, 28 March 2025 9:46 PM To: Ross Thompson > Subject: RE: Agriprove form for the CER Hi Ross, So having a look in some more detail here. As discussed we are trying to achieve two things with this information. 1. Show that at least one of the eligible activities has been implemented on the project area 2. Gather the data we need to quantify emissions associated with the project that feed into the calculations Regarding point 1, this is what we are trying to achieve with the Activity Log pages. What is important to note on these activities is that we only need to demonstrate that one of these has occurred, not all of them. As a starting point we could select one that may be the easiest to demonstrate, and only make reference to the others as complimentary activities without being required to demonstrate them in detail or provide detail that is difficult to obtain. From your notes it sounds like this may be achievable. Regarding point 2, if we put aside the stock numbers for the moment, we can strike a few things out from the start. I don't believe irrigation and landscape modification are relevant in your scenario and can be disregarded. That leaves the inputs, which it seems you have some records for, at least for total quantities which we will be able to work with. I also think residues will be able to be resolved given you are primarily a grazing operation and this section is more aimed at cropping operations. Regarding stock numbers, I think it would be worthwhile if we could jump on a quick call with Will at a time that suits you to ask some targeted questions that can help us better determine what can be done. Also, to clarify, the expectation is not for you to fill out the tables provided - we can do this work based on raw information provided, before cross-checking with you that we have interpreted correctly. As discussed, I would be more than happy to come and see you face to face, I could complete as much of this as I can on the fly while there - we have done this a few times previously and has b…

engagements.body: Good Morning Ross, Thanks for sending those details through. We definitely haven't put it in the too hard basket - it just hasn't been an urgent priority up until now as it's coming up to the reporting period date. I will touch base with Kieren and have cc'ed him into this email to see what we can do. In terms of the record keeping - we would never expect you to guess, and it is a lot simpler than it sounds. Most of it is things that you would already have had to collect and would have given to your accountant eg. invoices for expenses such as seed and fertilizer, livestock numbers, fuel used ect. The main thing that the regulator needs is proof that you have changed practices in some way and that you have implemented what you said you would. They don't need extreme detail of every little thing that you have done on farm. If you would find it helpful, I can jump on a call with you and we can look at your map, go through what you've done on your project, what records you have, and put together a bit of a plan/list of what you need to proceed and get this done. engagements.subject: RE: AgriProve, Next Steps
engagements.body: Hi Finola, 1. The fundamental undertaking is that the land remain in an agricultural system for the term of the agreement. The specific restricted and activities not permitted are specified by the legislated method and were provided as attachments to the agreements provided previously but re-attached here. In terms of achieving outcomes, part of onboarding is a commitment that at least one of the eligible carbon building activities are implemented on farm. Looking at your records I understand that this is proposed to be a combination of altering stocking rates and pasture reestablishment/rejuvenation. For project registration we need to clearly establish that the intended management actions are new or materially different to what has been done in the 5 years prior to registration. For best outcomes it is important that the frequency, intensity, or duration of these activities is changed relative to the baseline management. Refer to s5-8 of our Master Terms and Conditions as relevant clauses. 2. This is not entirely accurate and depends on the scenario. BSR can discontinue at any point up until the point that ACCUs are issued to the project. A key decision point here is likely to be year 5. If no ACCUs have been issued by year 5, we are required to report to the regulator and incur sampling and audit costs for no return, so there may be no incentive for either party to continue at this point. If ACCUs have been issued to the project and BSR choose to terminate the agreement early for convenience and we need to revoke the project, AgriProve as project proponent will be required to return all ACCUs issued to the project to that point in time to the Clean Energy Regulator (CER). In this circumstance we require the operator (BSR) to return any ACCUs (or equivalent dollar value) to AgriProve so we can relinquish these to the CER. Refer to s10, 14, and 15 of the Master Terms and Conditions as relevant clauses. 3. Our model uses results obtained from our portfolio to date with factors applied for rainfall and enterprise type. It provides us with an indication of the project potential but is indicative only. As the method relies on physical measurement of soil organic carbon stocks, if the project achieves greater sequestration rates through successful management implementation, then this benefit is realised. 4. All re-sampling costs are absorbed in AgriProve's success fee. engagements.subject: RE: AgriProve, Next Steps
engagements.body: Hi Kieren, Hope you are well. We have prepared the attached zip folder which includes: 1. All of the standard Agriprove documents (which were amended by Agriprove to include both an ‘Operator’ and ‘Landholder’ definition in September / October last year) 2. Our draft ‘Special Conditions’ document (which our legal team has created for both Special Conditions to the ‘Key Commercial Terms’ and the ‘Master Terms & Conditions’). 3. Drat sampling plan. Please note that the attached sample map, which includes indicative soil sampling points, is for preliminary purposes only. As previously confirmed, Agri Prove only generate the final sampling locations for BSR approval after you have submitted a registration application with the CER. engagements.subject: AgriProve Soil Carbon Project Information
engagements.body: Hi Elliott, It was great to speak with you this afternoon about what you are looking to achieve on your property. Thanks for taking the time to discuss a carbon project with AgriProve today and I look forward to getting out to your farm as soon as possible. As discussed, I am sending through some documents for further information and a line of sight into the mapping stage of our process. Below I have outlined what each attachment is about to help you navigate them. 1. I have attached our FAQ document with some written answers to common questions that are asked. 2. Our next steps form is the Consent to Register, Commitment to Implement (CTR-CTI). This is the main one we need back from you to move forward. Once received, we can start gathering the background information required to register the projects and commence the mapping process in consultation with you. This document does not lock you into a project with us should you decide not to proceed. Based on our discussion I would recommend selecting 'Altering the stocking rate...' tick box for the eligible activity to be implemented but you might also like to consider 'Re-establishing or rejuvenating pasture...'. We typically recommend selecting only one or two eligible activities to start, and this can be updated in the future should you choose. 4. Also attached is our Universal Land Management Strategy that accompanies all AgriProve projects and details how they are managed and monitored. A land management strategy is required by the Clean Energy Regulator for all Carbon Projects registered with them. I am more than happy to talk you through these documents and discuss any questions that come up as a result. Feel free to reach out anytime. Looking forward to discussing further with you soon. @Bill Hyem Hi Elliot, Thanks for your time earlier in the week, it was great to meet you. I have summarised the key points we discussed below. As discussed on the call, while we are not able to make amendments, I am happy to provide clarifications and formally sign off on those under the provision of cl. 21.3 of our Master Terms and Conditions. Cl 7.3: To clarify, the mention of financial statements and tax returns is an example only. This clause relates to the provision of management data that we require to show implementation of eligible activities and to quantify project emissions (for example invoices for fencing, or fertiliser quantities). We do not require full financial statements or tax returns, and if the required data and documentation can be provided in other ways, that will satisfy our requirements. There is no requirement or need for us to have access to full company financial statements. Conditions of Default: The main conditions of default on the Operator side are twofold. Firstly, a material breach of the agreement, the most likely case being removal of the land relating to the project from an agricultural system (such as a residential subdivision), or a decision by the operator to terminate the agreement (not a default event per se). Cl 14.3 outlines the requirements for termination, including purchase of any project ACCUs issued to date and transferring those to AgriProve. Property sale does not represent default, provided AgriProve is notified of the sale as per Cl 2.6 and best efforts are made to novate the agreement, but as proponent the risks associated with continuation of the projects with new owners are borne by AgriProve. We do not have any ability under this agreement to block property sales. Happy to discuss further if required. Regards, Kieren Whittock | National Operations Manager

engagements.subject: RE: Responses to Legal Review
engagements.body: Hi Elliot, Good to catch up last week. Apologies for the delay in getting this back to you, I am still catching up after my disrupted week last week with illness in the household. To summarise our conversation, I believe there were three key clauses that remained a concern: 1. Market Adjustment Fee. In this instance your concern stems from the interpretation that this clause may allow us to raise our service fee (for example from 25% to 30%) and pass this on to all existing contracts. As discussed on the call, this was not the intent of the clause, which was designed to not disadvantage early adopters if we ended up reducing our service fee (for example from 25% to 20%). I note that Cl. 21.2 of the master Ts and Cs notes that amendments can only be passed on if they have a materially adverse effect on the landholder/operator. Notwithstanding, I am happy to provide clarification that this market adjustment fee will only occur in your favour (ie. a reduction in our service fee), as this is the original intent of the clause. 2. Risk of ACCU Relinquishment. As discussed, this is not a clause we can amend as it is a function of the regulation that we are working under. This clause arises due to the requirement that if the operator elects to terminate the agreement early and ACCUs have been issued to the project and we are then required to revoke the project with the CER, the CER in all likelihood will request that all ACCUs issued to the project are returned by the project proponent (AgriProve). In this instance where the termination is initiated by the operator AgriProve will request that these are sourced (or the equivalent value thereof) by the landholder/operator, as it is their breach of terms that has led to the relinquishment requirement in this instance. The key undertaking on the landholder/operator here is that the land remain in agricultural system for the 25 year project period to mitigate this risk. 3. Liability. Regarding the disclaimer of liability in Cl. 20.6, this is specific to instances where further decisions based on information we provide (such as decisions regarding whether to sell or hold ACCUs) are made by the landholder/operator, the outcomes of which we have no control over, such as a reduction in ACCU price. We would always recommend that independent advice is sought on such decisions. In terms of 20.6 (2), similarly, we cannot be liable for actions taken by a New Project Proponent (not AgriProve) where they are nominated by the operator as per Cl. 10, as we have no control over the actions of an independent entity in this scenario. This is not removing our liability for negligence or non-performance which is covered by Cl. 10 (the ability to remove AgriProve as proponent/agent if we are not performing), and more specifically Cl. 20.1 under which we are liable for the greater of $50k or an equivalent value to AgriProve’s 25% fee over the preceding 12-month period if we are found to be negligent etc. As above, I am unable to amend these clauses, but I believe the liability clauses provide adequate protection for both parties to this agreement, with the intent to ensure that both parties have an interest in ensuring the success of the project by virtue of the overall structure. More than happy to continue the conversation as needed. engagements.subject: Re: Responses to Legal Review
engagements.body: Dear Kieren, Thank you again for your time and for the prior email. For the sake of clarity I went back and reformatted our discussions into each specific points. There were also a few that we glazed over but didn’t fully cover which I should have, but have put it on here to be complete. Note that I have highlighted your responses in blue and some questions from my end in red. Please review and confirm the accuracy along with any advise you can provide regarding my comments in red. * Point 6 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Market Adjustment for Agriprove Fee (Section 21.2) * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * Drafting appears to enable AgriProve to change the AgriProve Fee by an announcement in their newsletter. This provides significant discretion to AgriProve to unilaterally change the Agriprove Fee. There is a mechanism for how this will be dealt with where there is a reduction in AgriProve Fee, but there is no mechanism to deal with this where there is an increase. In relation to the mechanism dealing with a reduction, we query why there is a need to wait until the next anniversary to pass the benefit to the Operator. * Suggestion by MinterEllison * We recommend that drafting is included which restricts the ability for the AgriProve Fee to be increased without the Operator's consent. * Response by Kieren after meeting * Market Adjustment Fee. In this instance your concern stems from the interpretation that this clause may allow us to raise our service fee (for example from 25% to 30%) and pass this on to all existing contracts. As discussed on the call, this was not the intent of the clause, which was designed to not disadvantage early adopters if we ended up reducing our service fee (for example from 25% to 20%). I note that Cl. 21.2 of the master Ts and Cs notes that amendments can only be passed on if they do not have a materially adverse effect on the landholder/operator. Notwithstanding, I am happy to provide clarification that this market adjustment fee will only occur in your favour (ie. a reduction in our service fee), as this is the original intent of the clause. * Point 14 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Dealing with Project ACCUs (Clause 8.2) * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * In the event that Project ACCUs are dealt with other than in accordance with the Agreement, it is currently stated that it is a material breach of the Agreement. However, this will not cover the Operator's loss. AgriProve should be required to indemnify the Landholder against any loss incurred as a result of dealing with Project ACCUs in a way that is inappropriate. * Suggestion by MinterEllison * We recommend that an indemnity of this nature in included. * Response by Kieren during/after meeting * Suggests that AgriProve will create a separate ACCU management account controlled by CSP once ACCUs are granted by the government. This is something that AgriProve has done for others and is happy to do for CSP which would sidestep the issue. * Point 15 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Clause 9.2 – Cobenefits * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * Under the drafting, AgriProve will be entitled to 25% of all Project ACCUs and Co-benefits. While it is a commercial matter for CSPC as to whether 25% of all Project ACCUs is an appropriate figure, we recommend that CSPC calculates whether this is appropriate based on its understanding of the ACCUs which may be generated form the Carbon Projects and the expected current and future carbon price. For context, a graph showing the ACCU spot price is shown below: We also query the inclusion of Co-benefits in this arrangement. As CSPC may be aware, the Commonwealth Government has recently passed the Nature Repair Act 2023 (Cth) and the ability to generate biodiversity certificates on the Project Properties will be need to be assessed. AgriProve's services are purely related to carbon, so we don't see why AgriProve should get the benefits of any Co-benefits. As noted in the Agreement, arrangements…

engagements.subject: RE: Responses to Legal Review
engagements.body: Hi Elliot, Good to catch up last week. Apologies for the delay in getting this back to you, I am still catching up after my disrupted week last week with illness in the household. To summarise our conversation, I believe there were three key clauses that remained a concern: 1. Market Adjustment Fee. In this instance your concern stems from the interpretation that this clause may allow us to raise our service fee (for example from 25% to 30%) and pass this on to all existing contracts. As discussed on the call, this was not the intent of the clause, which was designed to not disadvantage early adopters if we ended up reducing our service fee (for example from 25% to 20%). I note that Cl. 21.2 of the master Ts and Cs notes that amendments can only be passed on if they have a materially adverse effect on the landholder/operator. Notwithstanding, I am happy to provide clarification that this market adjustment fee will only occur in your favour (ie. a reduction in our service fee), as this is the original intent of the clause. 2. Risk of ACCU Relinquishment. As discussed, this is not a clause we can amend as it is a function of the regulation that we are working under. This clause arises due to the requirement that if the operator elects to terminate the agreement early and ACCUs have been issued to the project and we are then required to revoke the project with the CER, the CER in all likelihood will request that all ACCUs issued to the project are returned by the project proponent (AgriProve). In this instance where the termination is initiated by the operator AgriProve will request that these are sourced (or the equivalent value thereof) by the landholder/operator, as it is their breach of terms that has led to the relinquishment requirement in this instance. The key undertaking on the landholder/operator here is that the land remain in agricultural system for the 25 year project period to mitigate this risk. 3. Liability. Regarding the disclaimer of liability in Cl. 20.6, this is specific to instances where further decisions based on information we provide (such as decisions regarding whether to sell or hold ACCUs) are made by the landholder/operator, the outcomes of which we have no control over, such as a reduction in ACCU price. We would always recommend that independent advice is sought on such decisions. In terms of 20.6 (2), similarly, we cannot be liable for actions taken by a New Project Proponent (not AgriProve) where they are nominated by the operator as per Cl. 10, as we have no control over the actions of an independent entity in this scenario. This is not removing our liability for negligence or non-performance which is covered by Cl. 10 (the ability to remove AgriProve as proponent/agent if we are not performing), and more specifically Cl. 20.1 under which we are liable for the greater of $50k or an equivalent value to AgriProve’s 25% fee over the preceding 12-month period if we are found to be negligent etc. As above, I am unable to amend these clauses, but I believe the liability clauses provide adequate protection for both parties to this agreement, with the intent to ensure that both parties have an interest in ensuring the success of the project by virtue of the overall structure. More than happy to continue the conversation as needed. Regards, Kieren Whittock | National Operations Manager Agriprove Pty Ltd Phone: 1300 GO SOIL (1300 467 645) Mobile: +61 400 216 548 Email: kieren@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. engagements.body: Dear Kieren, Thank you again for your time and for the prior email. For the sake of clarity I went back and reformatted our discussions into each specific points. There were also a few that we glazed over but didn’t fully cover which I should have, but have put it on here to be complete. Note that I have highlighted your responses in blue and some questions from my end in red. Please review and confirm the accuracy along with any advise you can provide regarding my comments in red. * Point 6 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Market Adjustment for Agriprove Fee (Section 21.2) * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * Drafting appears to enable AgriProve to change the AgriProve Fee by an announcement in their newsletter. This provides significant discretion to AgriProve to unilaterally change the Agriprove Fee. There is a mechanism for how this will be dealt with where there is a reduction in AgriProve Fee, but there is no mechanism to deal with this where there is an increase. In relation to the mechanism dealing with a reduction, we query why there is a need to wait until the next anniversary to pass the benefit to the Operator. * Suggestion by MinterEllison * We recommend that drafting is included which restricts the ability for the AgriProve Fee to be increased without the Operator's consent. * Response by Kieren after meeting * Market Adjustment Fee. In this instance your concern stems from the interpretation that this clause may allow us to raise our service fee (for example from 25% to 30%) and pass this on to all existing contracts. As discussed on the call, this was not the intent of the clause, which was designed to not disadvantage early adopters if we ended up reducing our service fee (for example from 25% to 20%). I note that Cl. 21.2 of the master Ts and Cs notes that amendments can only be passed on if they do not have a materially adverse effect on the landholder/operator. Notwithstanding, I am happy to provide clarification that this market adjustment fee will only occur in your favour (ie. a reduction in our service fee), as this is the original intent of the clause. * Point 14 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Dealing with Project ACCUs (Clause 8.2) * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * In the event that Project ACCUs are dealt with other than in accordance with the Agreement, it is currently stated that it is a material breach of the Agreement. However, this will not cover the Operator's loss. AgriProve should be required to indemnify the Landholder against any loss incurred as a result of dealing with Project ACCUs in a way that is inappropriate. * Suggestion by MinterEllison * We recommend that an indemnity of this nature in included. * Response by Kieren during/after meeting * Suggests that AgriProve will create a separate ACCU management account controlled by CSP once ACCUs are granted by the government. This is something that AgriProve has done for others and is happy to do for CSP which would sidestep the issue. * Point 15 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Clause 9.2 – Cobenefits * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * Under the drafting, AgriProve will be entitled to 25% of all Project ACCUs and Co-benefits. While it is a commercial matter for CSPC as to whether 25% of all Project ACCUs is an appropriate figure, we recommend that CSPC calculates whether this is appropriate based on its understanding of the ACCUs which may be generated form the Carbon Projects and the expected current and future carbon price. For context, a graph showing the ACCU spot price is shown below: We also query the inclusion of Co-benefits in this arrangement. As CSPC may be aware, the Commonwealth Government has recently passed the Nature Repair Act 2023 (Cth) and the ability to generate biodiversity certificates on the Project Properties will be need to be assessed. AgriProve's services are purely related to carbon, so we don't see why AgriProve should get the benefits of any Co-benefits. As noted in the Agreement, arrangements…

engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review
engagements.body: Good afternoon Elliott, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon projects. We do this every 12 months using satellite imagery of the NDRE (Normalized Difference Red Edge) on your farm to get an idea of if the vegetation has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample at this time. As you will see in the attached document, your projects' average NDRE has had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it means that compared to baseline the average trend has not been positive — which is an indicator that carbon sequestration has been unlikely at this time. This result means that your projects have not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. We will review this again next year to decide if resampling would be worthwhile then. To tick off your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your projects and any key requirements for this year. Is there a time that suits you for me or someone from our team to give you a call and complete this phone check in? Please note we have a bit of a backlog of these at the moment, so it may be longer than a few weeks before we get around to completing this call. engagements.subject: RE: Responses to Legal Review
engagements.body: Hi Elliot, Good to catch up last week. Apologies for the delay in getting this back to you, I am still catching up after my disrupted week last week with illness in the household. To summarise our conversation, I believe there were three key clauses that remained a concern: 1. Market Adjustment Fee. In this instance your concern stems from the interpretation that this clause may allow us to raise our service fee (for example from 25% to 30%) and pass this on to all existing contracts. As discussed on the call, this was not the intent of the clause, which was designed to not disadvantage early adopters if we ended up reducing our service fee (for example from 25% to 20%). I note that Cl. 21.2 of the master Ts and Cs notes that amendments can only be passed on if they have a materially adverse effect on the landholder/operator. Notwithstanding, I am happy to provide clarification that this market adjustment fee will only occur in your favour (ie. a reduction in our service fee), as this is the original intent of the clause. 2. Risk of ACCU Relinquishment. As discussed, this is not a clause we can amend as it is a function of the regulation that we are working under. This clause arises due to the requirement that if the operator elects to terminate the agreement early and ACCUs have been issued to the project and we are then required to revoke the project with the CER, the CER in all likelihood will request that all ACCUs issued to the project are returned by the project proponent (AgriProve). In this instance where the termination is initiated by the operator AgriProve will request that these are sourced (or the equivalent value thereof) by the landholder/operator, as it is their breach of terms that has led to the relinquishment requirement in this instance. The key undertaking on the landholder/operator here is that the land remain in agricultural system for the 25 year project period to mitigate this risk. 3. Liability. Regarding the disclaimer of liability in Cl. 20.6, this is specific to instances where further decisions based on information we provide (such as decisions regarding whether to sell or hold ACCUs) are made by the landholder/operator, the outcomes of which we have no control over, such as a reduction in ACCU price. We would always recommend that independent advice is sought on such decisions. In terms of 20.6 (2), similarly, we cannot be liable for actions taken by a New Project Proponent (not AgriProve) where they are nominated by the operator as per Cl. 10, as we have no control over the actions of an independent entity in this scenario. This is not removing our liability for negligence or non-performance which is covered by Cl. 10 (the ability to remove AgriProve as proponent/agent if we are not performing), and more specifically Cl. 20.1 under which we are liable for the greater of $50k or an equivalent value to AgriProve’s 25% fee over the preceding 12-month period if we are found to be negligent etc. As above, I am unable to amend these clauses, but I believe the liability clauses provide adequate protection for both parties to this agreement, with the intent to ensure that both parties have an interest in ensuring the success of the project by virtue of the overall structure. More than happy to continue the conversation as needed. engagements.body: Dear Kieren, Thank you again for your time and for the prior email. For the sake of clarity I went back and reformatted our discussions into each specific points. There were also a few that we glazed over but didn’t fully cover which I should have, but have put it on here to be complete. Note that I have highlighted your responses in blue and some questions from my end in red. Please review and confirm the accuracy along with any advise you can provide regarding my comments in red. * Point 6 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Market Adjustment for Agriprove Fee (Section 21.2) * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * Drafting appears to enable AgriProve to change the AgriProve Fee by an announcement in their newsletter. This provides significant discretion to AgriProve to unilaterally change the Agriprove Fee. There is a mechanism for how this will be dealt with where there is a reduction in AgriProve Fee, but there is no mechanism to deal with this where there is an increase. In relation to the mechanism dealing with a reduction, we query why there is a need to wait until the next anniversary to pass the benefit to the Operator. * Suggestion by MinterEllison * We recommend that drafting is included which restricts the ability for the AgriProve Fee to be increased without the Operator's consent. * Response by Kieren after meeting * Market Adjustment Fee. In this instance your concern stems from the interpretation that this clause may allow us to raise our service fee (for example from 25% to 30%) and pass this on to all existing contracts. As discussed on the call, this was not the intent of the clause, which was designed to not disadvantage early adopters if we ended up reducing our service fee (for example from 25% to 20%). I note that Cl. 21.2 of the master Ts and Cs notes that amendments can only be passed on if they do not have a materially adverse effect on the landholder/operator. Notwithstanding, I am happy to provide clarification that this market adjustment fee will only occur in your favour (ie. a reduction in our service fee), as this is the original intent of the clause. * Point 14 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Dealing with Project ACCUs (Clause 8.2) * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * In the event that Project ACCUs are dealt with other than in accordance with the Agreement, it is currently stated that it is a material breach of the Agreement. However, this will not cover the Operator's loss. AgriProve should be required to indemnify the Landholder against any loss incurred as a result of dealing with Project ACCUs in a way that is inappropriate. * Suggestion by MinterEllison * We recommend that an indemnity of this nature in included. * Response by Kieren during/after meeting * Suggests that AgriProve will create a separate ACCU management account controlled by CSP once ACCUs are granted by the government. This is something that AgriProve has done for others and is happy to do for CSP which would sidestep the issue. * Point 15 of MinterEllison Comment Document: Clause 9.2 – Cobenefits * Issue brought up by MinterEllison * Under the drafting, AgriProve will be entitled to 25% of all Project ACCUs and Co-benefits. While it is a commercial matter for CSPC as to whether 25% of all Project ACCUs is an appropriate figure, we recommend that CSPC calculates whether this is appropriate based on its understanding of the ACCUs which may be generated form the Carbon Projects and the expected current and future carbon price. For context, a graph showing the ACCU spot price is shown below: We also query the inclusion of Co-benefits in this arrangement. As CSPC may be aware, the Commonwealth Government has recently passed the Nature Repair Act 2023 (Cth) and the ability to generate biodiversity certificates on the Project Properties will be need to be assessed. AgriProve's services are purely related to carbon, so we don't see why AgriProve should get the benefits of any Co-benefits. As noted in the Agreement, arrangements…

engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review
engagements.body: Good afternoon Elliott, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon projects. We do this every 12 months using satellite imagery of the NDRE (Normalized Difference Red Edge) on your farm to get an idea of if the vegetation has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample at this time. As you will see in the attached document, your projects' average NDRE has had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it means that compared to baseline the average trend has not been positive — which is an indicator that carbon sequestration has been unlikely at this time. This result means that your projects have not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. We will review this again next year to decide if resampling would be worthwhile then. To tick off your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your projects and any key requirements for this year. Is there a time that suits you for me or someone from our team to give you a call and complete this phone check in? Please note we have a bit of a backlog of these at the moment, so it may be longer than a few weeks before we get around to completing this call. engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. engagements.subject: National Carbon Farming Conference - Albury, 3–6 Nov
engagements.body: Hi Mitch, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is coming up soon - it’s on 3–6 November in Albury. engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. WH William Hyem 19 Jun, 23 Hi Geoff, Please see the attached results for Cooper and Beale soil carbon projects. When the results were returned in June, we did find that some of the samples did not reach the full 30cm depth requirement for the methodology, and so we are likely going to need to resample and potentially re-stratify based on what is known of the area. Also, please find in three separate follow up emails the forwarded Sales and Licence Agreements for all projects, originally sent to gbfox@nidebra.com in December 2021. We have updated our Sales and Licence Agreement since then, so if you have received legal advice on the attached and are happy to sign that’s great – if you have not yet received legal advice please let me know and I will get you a single SLA on the updated terms. The terms are mostly the same, there have been some additions for data management and also non-performance clauses to remove AgriProve as project proponent under certain conditions as well which gives a bit more flexibility. I have attached the terms of the new agreement for your reference. Finally, with regards to invoicing the baseline sampling quote in an email 14/12/2021 was Beale: $4,000 ex. GST upfront and Cooper: $6,000 ex. GST upfront, or $12.50 ACCU forward abatement loan (let me know if you want to discuss this option, I believe last we spoke payment upfront was your preference). There was also the extra cost for agricultural analytes which were sent to yourself and Mitch last year. We have discussed the invoice for Watson Carbon Project previously and we cannot find record in xero or transaction history that this has been paid (original invoice attached). engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. Cheers Mitch On 22 Jan 2026, at 12:06 pm, Claudia Bryant wrote: Your project is coming up to its 5th anniversary and there is some actions we need to tick off before then. Here is what you need to know. Hi Mitch, I hope you are well and had a restful time over the holidays. I am reaching out as your carbon project is approaching its 5- year anniversary since base line sampling. This is a key time in a carbon project as there is a number of things that we need to tick off to meet your reporting requirements that are due before this date. This includes an audit in which you will need to supply your management records, we will need to re-sample if that has not been completed since baselining , and we need consent from everyone on your land titles to participate in your project including the bank if you have a mortgage. We are currently working through these steps and will contact you in the very near future with more detail as we work through this process behind the scenes. For Now, Your first steps are we need to get the Eligible interest holders consent process started as this is the part that can take the longest in this process. To get this started we just need you to answer a couple of quick questions below so we can get the ball rolling on this. Please reply answering these questions: 1. Do you wish to continue with your Carbon Project? 2. Has anything on your land title changed since you started the project? eg. sold, bought out, new partners, solar panels or power line companies operating on your land. 3. Who is on your land titles? MS Mat Silver 9 May, 22 Dear Bruce I have recently been appointed as AgriProves first Farmer Liaison Manager. The establishment of this role is part of an increased focus on project implementation support to all our clients. I am getting in touch with you to outline just a few of the practical things we are doing to increase support for you and your soil carbon project. 1. An annual review cycle We are moving to an annual project review cycle that will involve us assessing indicators of soil carbon change and determining whether soil sampling is likely to demonstrate an increase in your carbon stocks. As you are hopefully aware, once baselined all soil monitoring and sampling costs are now covered by AgriProve. Your AgriProve Project Manager will be in contact with you to discuss where your project is at in its annual cycle and if necessary to arrange soil sampling. 2. Technical webinar series with Q&A There is so much going on in agriculture at the moment and much of it relates to practices that can increase soil carbon and farm productivity. We are putting together a list of topics that we will engage speakers to provide a webinar followed by a session to answer all your questions on the topic. Some speakers will be technical specialists and academics, others will be fellow land managers sharing their experience with a particular practice. If you have any topics you would like to see added to this webinar series please email me at mat@agriprove.io 3. Support is just a call away If you have any questions about your soil carbon project please do not hesitate to contact your Project Manager. Your AgriProve Project Manager is: Kieren Whittock 0400 216 548 kieren.whittock@agriprove.io Please also feel free to contact me at any time to discuss any issues you have with your project or feedback you wish to provide on AgriProve service. My contact details are: Mat Silver - Farmer Liaison Manager 0466 302 850 mat@agriprove.io Regards, Mat

engagements.subject: Property Sale
engagements.body: Hi Bruce, Claudia has asked me to reach out regarding potential sale of your property. As you are aware we have Townley Carbon Project (ERF167693) currently registered on the property. The best-case scenario for us in the event of property sale is that the incoming owner takes on the soil carbon project, and if this remains an option we are more than happy to provide any additional material or speak directly to any interested parties to determine whether this is feasible. If this is not the case, you can request for us to voluntarily revoke the project with the CER (noting once we lodge this revocation it may take a minimum of three months for the CER to formally terminate the project). In this instance, this is quite straightforward given that: * ACCUs have not been issued on the project * Baseline sampling costs were paid in full at the time Please let us know if there is any scope to continue the project, and if not please notify us at any time that you would like us to revoke the project and we will send through confirmation that we have lodged this notification with the CER. Happy to discuss at any time. engagements.subject: Property Sale
engagements.body: Hi Bruce, Claudia has asked me to reach out regarding potential sale of your property. As you are aware we have Townley Carbon Project (ERF167693) currently registered on the property. The best-case scenario for us in the event of property sale is that the incoming owner takes on the soil carbon project, and if this remains an option we are more than happy to provide any additional material or speak directly to any interested parties to determine whether this is feasible. If this is not the case, you can request for us to voluntarily revoke the project with the CER (noting once we lodge this revocation it may take a minimum of three months for the CER to formally terminate the project). In this instance, this is quite straightforward given that: * ACCUs have not been issued on the project * Baseline sampling costs were paid in full at the time Please let us know if there is any scope to continue the project, and if not please notify us at any time that you would like us to revoke the project and we will send through confirmation that we have lodged this notification with the CER. Happy to discuss at any time. engagements.body: Hi Kobi, Great to catch up yesterday and thanks again for your time. As we went through together, I have updated the letter and had our two Directors, Matthew and Stephen Warnken, sign it overnight. Please see attached for your counter signatures. Regarding point 14.2.3 of the Master Terms, I have confirmed that it only references the ACCUs which may have been issued to the project to that time. From: Will Frecheville Sent: Tuesday, 27 May 2025 1:33 PM To: kobischooley101@gmail.com Cc: Kieren Whittock ; Imogen Hickey Subject: FW: Rocky Springs 1-3 Projects [SEC=OFFICIAL] Hi Kobi, As discussed, please see further request for information regarding the Rocky Springs Carbon Project from the Clean Energy Regulator. “Regarding the Rocky Springs 1–3 Projects (ERF191532, ERF193438, ERF193440), I’ve reviewed the “Current or Historic Land Management Activities” section in the CTR-CTI. It notes that “improved pastures and legumes” are to be planted within the project area. Given that one of the proposed EMAs is “Re-establishing or rejuvenating a pasture by seeding (for example, mixed species forage seeding),” this may raise concerns regarding the newness requirement. Could you please confirm whether any legumes or pasture-improving species have already been implemented in the project area? If so, could you outline what was implemented and explain how the proposed activity will be materially different from the baseline? If you believe that including this EMA may breach the newness requirement, you may submit an updated CTR-CTI with the EMA “Re-establishing or rejuvenating a pasture by seeding” removed.” Based on our discussion – my proposed response to address the query is as follows: Can you please confirm this is accurate to what has occurred on Rocky Springs 1-3; and your intentions for rejuvenating pasture as an eligible activity for the carbon project. Baseline Period: The current land that Rocky Springs 1-3 sits on is unimproved pasture, which is comprised of spear and wire grass. There has been no pasture improvement activities on this land during the baseline period or in the time we have owned the property. Proposed Carbon Project Eligible Activity: Rejuvenating a Pasture by seeding or pasture cropping. As a part of the carbon project, it is the intention to commence a program of pasture development that will be supported with appropriate grazing practices. The intention is to seed the pasture with a mixture of Hatch Creeping Blue grass, Rhodes grass and Biloela Buffel grass and with a legume mix of Siratro, Seca and Desmanthus. The seeding will occur in two passes, with an initial plough and then a second pass where seeding occurs. Each of these grass species are aimed an increasing biodiversity, root matter and improving the nitrogen fixation in the soil as a result of planting the legumes. These activities have not commenced and are awaiting declaration of the projects prior to commencing the first seeding event. engagements.body: Hi Kobi, Great to catch up yesterday and thanks again for your time. As we went through together, I have updated the letter and had our two Directors, Matthew and Stephen Warnken, sign it overnight. Please see attached for your counter signatures. Regarding point 14.2.3 of the Master Terms, I have confirmed that it only references the ACCUs which may have been issued to the project to that time. It is a way for the Operator to terminate the agreement of their own volition (i.e. not due to any wrong-doing by AgriProve) without exposing AgriProve to the liability of repaying any issued ACCUs. Essentially this would be an avenue to exit the agreement when the project is otherwise successful (with the issuance of ACCUs). I hope that makes more sense? Please let me know if you have any further questions but hopefully, we can get this progressed and start baselining before the rains. engagements.subject: Grazing Management Changes and Timeline
engagements.body: Hi Jeff, Thanks for your time just before, as discussed, the CER has asked about the grazing practice changes you have made. Specifically, the first water upgrades in 2021, and some sub-divisions of paddocks. We need to show a clear timeline of additional fencing upgrades/changes post the April 2022 declaration, as well as changes to stocking rates/durations of grazing following the seeding and application of Rural Boss. When we were on site, I remember you saying you're constantly making changes, based on behaviours to optimise the approach and your grazing management, so I do not think we will have an issue showing this change. As a first step, whilst you're putting together some timelines against your notes, can you please send me some photos of your grazing charts (as many years back as you have) We did have an option to not have grazing included as an eligible activity, however given it is central to your operation, I do not want to let this eligible activity go. The positive is that whilst there is a query on this aspect of grazing, the other implementation activities of pasture rejuvenation and nutrient application (Rural Boss spray) have been accepted and there is no risk to the overall application of credits. Appreciate your help. Feel free to give me a call to discuss. engagements.subject: RE: Re questions re "Reef Credits"
engagements.body: Hi Jeff, Yes, the platform is basing its assessment of eligibility off geographical location within the reef catchment areas. A Reef Credit project and Soil Carbon sequestration project can co-exist and we are actively targeting those landholders with an existing project with us that may be interested in Reef credits under the Grazing Land Management (GLM) method. I’ll pass your query over to Bill Hyem in our team to look further into this for you. Natural sequence farming seems like it would be a great addition to the property from my limited knowledge on it, and should help reduce fine sediment loss and nutrient runoff. However, there are some points to be aware of to be eligible for a GLM Reef credit project: * one or more additional or new management activities is implemented, * management activities are reasonably expected to improve ground cover for water quality improvement that are beyond what is required by legislation or pre-existing formal obligations, * grazing is the principle land use for the last seven years, and * broad scale clearing of woody vegetation has not occurred within the previous seven years. From the looks of it, if you were to start a reef credit project based purely on implementing natural sequence farming principles the project would go under the “Gully Method” which involves landscape rehabilitation and construction. We may struggle to prove additionality under the Grazing method as it would need to be a new activity relative to what you’re already doing with the carbon project. See attached guidance on Reef credits under the Grazing Land Management Methodology. We’ll get back to you with our thoughts after reviewing the situation further. From: Jeff Bell Sent: Sunday, 2 February 2025 2:55 PM To: Dylan Jones Subject: Re questions re "Reef Credits" Hi Dylan, The Agriprove platform said "Generate income through a Reef Credit project Your property is eligible to undertake a Reef Credit Project." Is this correct or is it just that we are geographically eligible? Can a reef credit project co-exist with a carbon project? I have been looking into "natural sequence farming" which is all about keeping water and dissolved nutrients on farm through modifying existing contour drains and/or constructing level contours.(which fits neatly into what the "reef credit project" would be looking to achieve. Attended a "natural sequence farming" field day yesterday and there was so much that explained why areas of our farm have limited performance compared to the mean. If we spend money on training and earthworks to keep more water and nutrients on our farm(approx 94 % of which is under a carbon project) would we be eligible for a "reef credit project"? Jeff Bell

engagements.subject: Re: Re questions re "Reef Credits"
engagements.body: Hi Dylan, Definitely would not be grazing management as that is already done. It would be remedial earth works to modify the existing drain contours and where needed construct new contours to slow the flow of water and nutrients and keep both on farm rather than running off down the waterway which does come in the list of gully management methodology activities. Most of the farm can benefit from this in productivity(and consequently carbon sequestration) but only about 30 percent of the farm(my guestimate) has substandard ground cover which in my opinion could release some sediment and nutrients off farm. My take is that the amount of sediment lost from the farm in its current condition would be to low to bother with. The only place where there would be any amount would be a bit hard to manage as it comes pouring through from next door in a water way only a couple of hundred metres from our bottom fence. If Agriprove think there is anything worth pursuing then I will think about it. I myself think not but that is an opinion not based on knowledge. engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Jeff, I have just completed your yearly satellite assessment for your carbon project. As you know we use this as an indicator for if we think resampling would be worthwhile. Your assessment this year ( attached) has shown an increase in the average NDRE from baseline to current period and an increase in the past year. This indicates that re-sampling this year would be worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration. This does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased. We need to complete the physical sampling to know what is happening in the ground. Next steps: Before we schedule the resampling date, we need to complete the phone call section of the review. Is there a time next week that would suit to do that? I have some prep I need to do before the call so locking in a time in advance works best. If you have any questions please let me know. Talk soon. engagements.subject: Re: Soil testing extras?
engagements.body: Good Moring Jeff, Yeah it is completely possible for us to do that. Do you know exactly what tests you want done? For an idea of potential price and difference tests I have attached an example of a quote we got for someone else and the full price list. Keeping in mind this is an older one and they may have changed since then. I had a look at your project, and you have 9 sample sites. You would see that on your results in the past you have 18 because they test the top layer (0-30cm) and then a deeper piece of that sample ( 30-100cm). If you wanted to do both depths, you would need to pay for 18 samples. ( 2x 9) Dylan did mention though that generally for agronomic based things having the deeper samples may not give you a lot of value but that depends on what you want to look at. engagements.subject: Grant for baseline subsidy
engagements.body: Hi Wayne, As discussed, I want to let you know that a National Soil Carbon Innovation Challenge (NSCIC) grant is currently available to help subsidies baseline sampling. We will be working with Hone, a remote sensing company, to deliver this grant and they are looking for properties across various geographical locations. I put your location forward for pre-approval and have heard back that you are eligible. By participating, laboratory cost for 30 soil cores (approx. 300 Ha) are subsidised which equates to roughly $6,000. You will also get access to the Hone Soil Carbon Device, made available with a $1 for 1 year lease agreement. Hone's hand-held device measures soil organic carbon using near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy. The ask is a data sharing agreement and commitment to complete 30 scans per quarter for 1 year. The Hone grant flyer and Data Use Agreement are attached below. I think the Wowan property would be a great fit for a ~$6,000 subsidy. Please be aware of the following: Limited Availability: Only a limited number of places are available, and once these places are filled, the offer will no longer be available. Expiry: This offer will expire the earlier of: All places filled or 30th September 2024. Acceptance: To apply for this offer the data sharing and use agreement and a completed KCT must be returned to AgriProve before the offer expires. Successful applicants will be notified by AgriProve. Your signature will be fine on the attached data sharing and use agreement, if you could complete and return it as the first step. Please give me a call anytime to discuss. engagements.subject: RE: AgriProve - Key Commercial Terms Agreement Griffin CP1&2 (Wowan)
engagements.body: Hi Melanie, I am responding on behalf of Dylan. Thankyou for providing the proposed amendments. To clarify, while we do accept addendums in some cases, this is only where the amendments have no material impact on the commercial and compliance obligations for both parties under the agreement, such as a landholder/property specific biosecurity plan as an example. As such there are fundamental issues with the proposed addendum that we cannot accept. 1. AgriProve Fee: This is not negotiable. 1. Clause 14: This is not negotiable. Noting that Cl. 14 is specific to the circumstance where the Operator elects to terminate the agreement and the project, resulting in a requirement to relinquish any ACCUs issued. In this instance AgriProve as proponent must hand back 100% of ACCUs due to a decision to terminate made by the Operator, and therefore AgriProve does not bear the cost of re-sourcing the AgriProve fee ACCUs (25%) 1. Clause 20.1: This is not negotiable. 1. Clause 6: As proponent we are required to gain all required consents, and the projects will not be able to generate ACCUs until this is done, and therefore it is in the best interests of both parties to work collaboratively to ensure these consents are gained. AgriProve is happy to lead the engagement and administrative requirements as per Cl. 6.2 but may require input and introductions from the Landholder/Operator where appropriate. With this in mind, some further context as to why these amendments are sought would be appreciated. 1. Project Areas: The project areas are clearly defined in the Key Commercial Terms and the project area maps supplied. The agreements only pertain to the project areas shown, and not the entirety of the relevant titles. Once registered this can be verified against the ERF register. Regarding the GreenCollar projects, it is important to note that it is not possible to stack the Greencollar method type with soil carbon (they cannot be registered on the same area), and we have spent considerable time completing a detailed mapping process taking into account their proposed project areas to ensure the projects can co-exist. We will only register the areas agreed as per these maps. I note that this should also be a requirement for Greencollar, as if their applications are not restricted to their project areas (eg. whole land titles), this will render the area ineligible for soil carbon unless area variations are completed which will delay the projects commencing. We have made every attempt to ensure this is not the case to date. I would welcome the opportunity to further discuss any of the points raised above. engagements.subject: Grant for baseline subsidy
engagements.body: Hi Wayne, As discussed, I want to let you know that a National Soil Carbon Innovation Challenge (NSCIC) grant is currently available to help subsidies baseline sampling. We will be working with Hone, a remote sensing company, to deliver this grant and they are looking for properties across various geographical locations. I put your location forward for pre-approval and have heard back that you are eligible. By participating, laboratory cost for 30 soil cores (approx. 300 Ha) are subsidised which equates to roughly $6,000. You will also get access to the Hone Soil Carbon Device, made available with a $1 for 1 year lease agreement. Hone's hand-held device measures soil organic carbon using near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy. The ask is a data sharing agreement and commitment to complete 30 scans per quarter for 1 year. The Hone grant flyer and Data Use Agreement are attached below. I think the Wowan property would be a great fit for a ~$6,000 subsidy. Please be aware of the following: Limited Availability: Only a limited number of places are available, and once these places are filled, the offer will no longer be available. Expiry: This offer will expire the earlier of: All places filled or 30th September 2024. Acceptance: To apply for this offer the data sharing and use agreement and a completed KCT must be returned to AgriProve before the offer expires. Successful applicants will be notified by AgriProve. Your signature will be fine on the attached data sharing and use agreement, if you could complete and return it as the first step. Please give me a call anytime to discuss. That is why we have taken appropriate measures to ensure that the data you have provided to us is always secure. Also note that as a signatory to the Carbon Industry Code of Conduct, we recommend that independent legal and/or financial advice is sought before signing our Key Commercial Terms. engagements.subject: RE: AgriProve - Key Commercial Terms Agreement Griffin CP1&2 (Wowan)
engagements.body: Hi Melanie, I am responding on behalf of Dylan. Thankyou for providing the proposed amendments. To clarify, while we do accept addendums in some cases, this is only where the amendments have no material impact on the commercial and compliance obligations for both parties under the agreement, such as a landholder/property specific biosecurity plan as an example. As such there are fundamental issues with the proposed addendum that we cannot accept. 1. AgriProve Fee: This is not negotiable. 1. Clause 14: This is not negotiable. Noting that Cl. 14 is specific to the circumstance where the Operator elects to terminate the agreement and the project, resulting in a requirement to relinquish any ACCUs issued. In this instance AgriProve as proponent must hand back 100% of ACCUs due to a decision to terminate made by the Operator, and therefore AgriProve does not bear the cost of re-sourcing the AgriProve fee ACCUs (25%) 1. Clause 20.1: This is not negotiable. 1. Clause 6: As proponent we are required to gain all required consents, and the projects will not be able to generate ACCUs until this is done, and therefore it is in the best interests of both parties to work collaboratively to ensure these consents are gained. AgriProve is happy to lead the engagement and administrative requirements as per Cl. 6.2 but may require input and introductions from the Landholder/Operator where appropriate. With this in mind, some further context as to why these amendments are sought would be appreciated. 1. Project Areas: The project areas are clearly defined in the Key Commercial Terms and the project area maps supplied. The agreements only pertain to the project areas shown, and not the entirety of the relevant titles. Once registered this can be verified against the ERF register. Regarding the GreenCollar projects, it is important to note that it is not possible to stack the Greencollar method type with soil carbon (they cannot be registered on the same area), and we have spent considerable time completing a detailed mapping process taking into account their proposed project areas to ensure the projects can co-exist. We will only register the areas agreed as per these maps. I note that this should also be a requirement for Greencollar, as if their applications are not restricted to their project areas (eg. whole land titles), this will render the area ineligible for soil carbon unless area variations are completed which will delay the projects commencing. We have made every attempt to ensure this is not the case to date. I would welcome the opportunity to further discuss any of the points raised above. Regards, Kieren Whittock | National Operations Manager Agriprove Pty Ltd Phone: 1300 GO SOIL (1300 467 645) Mobile: +61 400 216 548 Email: kieren@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. That is why we have taken appropriate measures to ensure that the data you have provided to us is always secure. If you have any questions related compliance or data protection, please contact our Data Protection Officer . AgriProve Pty Ltd ACN 624 305 371 is an authorised representative (AR No. 001275434) of Corporate Carbon Advisory (AFS Licence No: 430199).
