discovery call with Justin: feedback for becoming a growth engine: We are busy - the life of the carbon project together - need to be able to bring forward the milestones of a carbon project. Key Pieces of Feedback: Transparency Transparency with the operational procedure - "were busy running our own businesses, put together a piece so farmers have an understanding of key times and what is required by the farmer - i.e. a piece of collateral that reflects the project lifecycle" Project Milestones Contact points Regular touch points either en masse or 1:1 AgriProve needs to come in to guide the project and where it needs to go. Goal oriented: Validate that carbon sequestration is possible Was "Mr Skeptical" and wanted to road-test it, so others could take these thing on. Big gap between Operations and the Producer We need guide Tech notes that come with it as well - when sharing technical information from other projects - we haven't done this very well. Provide the farmer with simple takeaways: So the producer is able to communicate, or guide people in a process where they can verbalise their soil mission - how many tonnes we are trying to sequester. Education is needed regularly - e.g. webinars, seminars, tutorials. attend 3-4 webinars a year - so they're engaged with what is happening reality on pay-offs, discussing the newest content. Value Propositions for Customer Success and Recruitment Linkage between production and carbon building: improvements to farm, lead to increase in production, the co-benefit is carbon. Tags for tonnes helps with this as the co-benefits: Compared the Customer success challenge with Ruminati program - they provide a very strong user experience around Baselining and understanding where they're at; Integrates for day to day farming with the carbon project What does it mean being in a carbon project? Similar thinking to superannuation; payback period is significantly further down the line, but the need to regularly check in on progress is important Vital piece is providing a producer with a really simple, value proposition for starting know that shade is super important, improving water, shade, pasture utilisation The more we can break down those barriers for customer success, if we can get that right, participants will be happier with the model, the model is a bit fractured as a result of not setting clear agendas/milestones/guidance - what is working and not working when it comes to carbon building and production benefit. "what were not doing enough of, investing in the production model, but not investing enough time into learning how this relates this back to carbon farming." Long term goal: asset growth and a carbon project Short term goal: animal production and outcomes from that Align short-term to long-term goals, but adding value and clear linkage between short term and long term goals. AgriProve needs to become a producer-oriented organisation: What would the farmer tell the consumer? I'm in an accredited carbon project and using data driven insights to improve my farm Stakeholders: Processors, get a green premium when speaking with processors on ESG programs Banks: Potentially beneficial interest rate when engaging with an ESG Program Teys - Grasslands - they pay a premium for productivity JBS - pay a premium for being a steward of their land Processors - they are talking about the ESG program, but not sure what that program looks like: what sort of value they can give people how do we attach benefits to the 240 farmers, will they get a better rate at the bank? What if they got 0.2% better rate because they're joined to an ESG program with AgriProve. Consumers: Reason other tech companies he's worked with have been successful: AgriWebb gives you a stewardship program, but AgriProve does not - need collateral, AgriProve Environmental Farming Program. Chat with Justin RE: Ruminati (8th May 24) Ruminati provide tangible accounting of farm management decisions Moving from what we think we know to something visual and easy to interact with What value prop can we give our customers - something like this is perfect for client interaction We need to have an active mechanism to give this sort of information Currently our emissions discussions are not a good visual representation of management decisions (spreadsheet based) Wen need to (through a tool like this) give them (our landholders and prospects) active scenarios with calcs of how their management changes would effect their carbon balance We need to go on a competitor watch and see the partners they are creating (highly influential) - would give us massive market penetration to partner with Ruminati What does this really give a farmer? - speeds up the process to get a quicker result on the validation piece to their management This is what we are lacking in our offering - pathways to get to net a quicker result - how do we make it easier to do a carbon audit Gives our landholders a triple A rating - auditing - great baseline tool that is farmer and supply chain accepted + government validated emissions sequestration AP should do a validation every 6 months - would be significantly easier and less time consuming with a product such as this AgriProve could provide EOFY Ruminati report AP shouldn't want to replicate the same product - partner and make a commercial agreement - and make the exponential progress Look at who they are ready integrated to - leverage their network We are a $150,000 (300 clients at $500 each) client for 25 years - that's a huge value add for them Want to have tools in the tool box - already have ceres tags and the soil testing internally - this could be a great add-on Rumninati cover the negative aspect - emissions - why wouldn't we look to just buy them out? And tell the whole story Bring on their existing clients and tell the other half of the story Gotta tell the positive - they will want to bring that in their suite of products - they don't do the positive aspects but they are tied in to a suite of partners As a farmer with their service you pay just to know you are a polluter - let us tell your positive aspect - fill their gap with landholders they already have on-board Create a licence agreement or partnership or a pathway for integrating into their clientele Potential for a commercial subscription? Once landholders are signed up create a baseline score for them and give them the option to play with management scenarios Works hand in hand with our products Helps grass fed producers get better market access - we need to look at end producer - grassfed programs Justin sees holes in his story - these are hard to explain - this plugs a massive hole - need to work on our enemy (emissions story tellers) Go to end user - Coles - pitch our product to tell whole picture - negative and positive - do you want to know more - show them Ready Graze with carbon accounting Justin wants $0.20 more per every kg produced due to validation - hard to make a profit right now because of the market - needs to show something different More market access for the positive management the more money landholders can put into the management of their carbon project

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Spoke to Justin about the certification and sustainability piece. Gave great responses, very interested

Responses to sustainability questionnaire: Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? - Yes - GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy - If no, then why not? - N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? - GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management - How can we make the testing attractive and simple - Very honourous - Teas - JBS - TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? - Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? - If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business - Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? - Not direct to consumers - Have looked at the big supply chains - Looked into Greenham’s - Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand - Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? - TBD - Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to - Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Chatted to JC about his ACCUs and sharing his profile. He has an idea around the data we are collecting and wanting to create a provenance story using combined AP data and genomics. Looking to put together a proposal to articulate his ideas. Notes from meeting below: Need to validate outcomes Outcomes of carbon project aligned with high quality cattle management AgriProvenance - a failsafe system to prove the traceability Genomics - outcomes of the cattle (when the herd is at feed conversion) T4T, EOS, genomics = package to producers Genomically verify all the bulls - create auditable trails Prove the animals are the best ranking in a carbon sense Potentially use Gallagher / optiweigh and validate the measurements Collect the information and overlay into the program - herd/provenance Each animal verified through genomics, lifetime carbon project measured, kgs produced, kgs emitted, ongoing efficiencies - totalling a value MSA graded product vs reliability Whole of life information - green training wheels on the animal Breed outcome - market ready at a certain time Steer select - animals that will produce best on farm AgriProvenance , net emissions, credits, management strategy - making the farm very transparent Metrics - DOB Genomic testing $40 per head - data to make key decisions Give the data to make an assumption after birth (6 months) these are my highest ranking individuals - keep only the efficient animals on farm (carbon benefit based on efficiency) Improvement on feed efficiency and outcomes Making decisions based on long-term gains Is breeders are inefficient they enter the food supply Over the carbon project you have a high performing herd - go to for efficiencies AgriProvenance adds value to customer - health protocol, vaccine's, health status What AP has is soil - JC can provide the stable products Provenance also goes into the grains/timber, etc. Real tool is good outcomes Validation of bloodline, performance, and carbon story - QR to public page (T carbon produced, T carbon emitted, carbon story and ACCUs) Everything auditbale in a CP and passing audits Best practice and best management that is scalable Go and target Angus Australia

discovery call with Justin: feedback for becoming a growth engine: We are busy - the life of the carbon project together - need to be able to bring forward the milestones of a carbon project. Key Pieces of Feedback: Transparency Transparency with the operational procedure - "were busy running our own businesses, put together a piece so farmers have an understanding of key times and what is required by the farmer - i.e. a piece of collateral that reflects the project lifecycle" Project Milestones Contact points Regular touch points either en masse or 1:1 AgriProve needs to come in to guide the project and where it needs to go. Goal oriented: Validate that carbon sequestration is possible Was "Mr Skeptical" and wanted to road-test it, so others could take these thing on. Big gap between Operations and the Producer We need guide Tech notes that come with it as well - when sharing technical information from other projects - we haven't done this very well. Provide the farmer with simple takeaways: So the producer is able to communicate, or guide people in a process where they can verbalise their soil mission - how many tonnes we are trying to sequester. Education is needed regularly - e.g. webinars, seminars, tutorials. attend 3-4 webinars a year - so they're engaged with what is happening reality on pay-offs, discussing the newest content. Value Propositions for Customer Success and Recruitment Linkage between production and carbon building: improvements to farm, lead to increase in production, the co-benefit is carbon. Tags for tonnes helps with this as the co-benefits: Compared the Customer success challenge with Ruminati program - they provide a very strong user experience around Baselining and understanding where they're at; Integrates for day to day farming with the carbon project What does it mean being in a carbon project? Similar thinking to superannuation; payback period is significantly further down the line, but the need to regularly check in on progress is important Vital piece is providing a producer with a really simple, value proposition for starting know that shade is super important, improving water, shade, pasture utilisation The more we can break down those barriers for customer success, if we can get that right, participants will be happier with the model, the model is a bit fractured as a result of not setting clear agendas/milestones/guidance - what is working and not working when it comes to carbon building and production benefit. "what were not doing enough of, investing in the production model, but not investing enough time into learning how this relates this back to carbon farming." Long term goal: asset growth and a carbon project Short term goal: animal production and outcomes from that Align short-term to long-term goals, but adding value and clear linkage between short term and long term goals. AgriProve needs to become a producer-oriented organisation: What would the farmer tell the consumer? I'm in an accredited carbon project and using data driven insights to improve my farm Stakeholders: Processors, get a green premium when speaking with processors on ESG programs Banks: Potentially beneficial interest rate when engaging with an ESG Program Teys - Grasslands - they pay a premium for productivity JBS - pay a premium for being a steward of their land Processors - they are talking about the ESG program, but not sure what that program looks like: what sort of value they can give people how do we attach benefits to the 240 farmers, will they get a better rate at the bank? What if they got 0.2% better rate because they're joined to an ESG program with AgriProve. Consumers: Reason other tech companies he's worked with have been successful: AgriWebb gives you a stewardship program, but AgriProve does not - need collateral, AgriProve Environmental Farming Program. "Bank is stoked that you're part of a carbon project, they really look at ESG We will get a premium to these 240 participants? Apart from Off-se…

Chat with Justin RE: Ruminati (8th May 24) Ruminati provide tangible accounting of farm management decisions Moving from what we think we know to something visual and easy to interact with What value prop can we give our customers - something like this is perfect for client interaction We need to have an active mechanism to give this sort of information Currently our emissions discussions are not a good visual representation of management decisions (spreadsheet based) Wen need to (through a tool like this) give them (our landholders and prospects) active scenarios with calcs of how their management changes would effect their carbon balance We need to go on a competitor watch and see the partners they are creating (highly influential) - would give us massive market penetration to partner with Ruminati What does this really give a farmer? - speeds up the process to get a quicker result on the validation piece to their management This is what we are lacking in our offering - pathways to get to net a quicker result - how do we make it easier to do a carbon audit Gives our landholders a triple A rating - auditing - great baseline tool that is farmer and supply chain accepted + government validated emissions sequestration AP should do a validation every 6 months - would be significantly easier and less time consuming with a product such as this AgriProve could provide EOFY Ruminati report AP shouldn't want to replicate the same product - partner and make a commercial agreement - and make the exponential progress Look at who they are ready integrated to - leverage their network We are a $150,000 (300 clients at $500 each) client for 25 years - that's a huge value add for them Want to have tools in the tool box - already have ceres tags and the soil testing internally - this could be a great add-on Rumninati cover the negative aspect - emissions - why wouldn't we look to just buy them out? And tell the whole story Bring on their existing clients and tell the other half of the story Gotta tell the positive - they will want to bring that in their suite of products - they don't do the positive aspects but they are tied in to a suite of partners As a farmer with their service you pay just to know you are a polluter - let us tell your positive aspect - fill their gap with landholders they already have on-board Create a licence agreement or partnership or a pathway for integrating into their clientele Potential for a commercial subscription? Once landholders are signed up create a baseline score for them and give them the option to play with management scenarios Works hand in hand with our products Helps grass fed producers get better market access - we need to look at end producer - grassfed programs Justin sees holes in his story - these are hard to explain - this plugs a massive hole - need to work on our enemy (emissions story tellers) Go to end user - Coles - pitch our product to tell whole picture - negative and positive - do you want to know more - show them Ready Graze with carbon accounting Justin wants $0.20 more per every kg produced due to validation - hard to make a profit right now because of the market - needs to show something different More market access for the positive management the more money landholders can put into the management of their carbon project

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Spoke to Justin about the certification and sustainability piece. Gave great responses, very interested

Responses to sustainability questionnaire: Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? - Yes - GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy - If no, then why not? - N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? - GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management - How can we make the testing attractive and simple - Very honourous - Teas - JBS - TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? - Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? - If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business - Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? - Not direct to consumers - Have looked at the big supply chains - Looked into Greenham’s - Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand - Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? - TBD - Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to - Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals

Hi Justin, I hope you are going well! Lovely to chat to you last week about our research project with RMIT University, about our sampling study, the Australian Soil Carbon Sampling Optimisation Study. As discussed, please see attached the sampling plan, for your approval. RMIT would like to sample only CEA 1, the highest performing CEA, and to resample T0, T1, and T2 points to understand change over time. They would also like to sample 2 extra points at each point 1m and 2m out, like the diagram below, to gain and understanding of spatial variability at a high resolution. Also please note in the plan attached, not all labels are showing due to them being too close together. Please note that this will have no impact on your compliant project sampling rounds and this data is not shared with the regulator. However, this sampling may be used to assist us to better stratify your project to reduce variability within strata. Please let me know if you are happy with this plan. We aim to sample next week, and the guys will be in touch direct to arrange a time. We have also sent you a consent form via panda docs, to say that you are happy for AgriProve to share this data with RMIT for the purposes of the study. Thanks again for being part of the project and please feel free to give me a call if you’d like to discuss. Melanie

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Chatted to JC about his ACCUs and sharing his profile. He has an idea around the data we are collecting and wanting to create a provenance story using combined AP data and genomics. Looking to put together a proposal to articulate his ideas. Notes from meeting below: Need to validate outcomes Outcomes of carbon project aligned with high quality cattle management AgriProvenance - a failsafe system to prove the traceability Genomics - outcomes of the cattle (when the herd is at feed conversion) T4T, EOS, genomics = package to producers Genomically verify all the bulls - create auditable trails Prove the animals are the best ranking in a carbon sense Potentially use Gallagher / optiweigh and validate the measurements Collect the information and overlay into the program - herd/provenance Each animal verified through genomics, lifetime carbon project measured, kgs produced, kgs emitted, ongoing efficiencies - totalling a value MSA graded product vs reliability Whole of life information - green training wheels on the animal Breed outcome - market ready at a certain time Steer select - animals that will produce best on farm AgriProvenance , net emissions, credits, management strategy - making the farm very transparent Metrics - DOB Genomic testing $40 per head - data to make key decisions Give the data to make an assumption after birth (6 months) these are my highest ranking individuals - keep only the efficient animals on farm (carbon benefit based on efficiency) Improvement on feed efficiency and outcomes Making decisions based on long-term gains Is breeders are inefficient they enter the food supply Over the carbon project you have a high performing herd - go to for efficiencies AgriProvenance adds value to customer - health protocol, vaccine's, health status What AP has is soil - JC can provide the stable products Provenance also goes into the grains/timber, etc. Real tool is good outcomes Validation of bloodline, performance, and carbon story - QR to public page (T carbon produced, T carbon emitted, carbon story and ACCUs) Everything auditbale in a CP and passing audits Best practice and best management that is scalable Go and target Angus Australia

engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Justin, I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. As you will see in the attached document, your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note: This trend does not mean carbon has gone backwards, it shows the trend in vegetation greenness has been lower than your baseline average and therefore it is unlikely re sampling would be worthwhile at this time. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks and complete this phone check in? Talk soon. engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Mountain View/Page/Truss CPs
engagements.body: Dear Justin, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. discovery call with Justin: feedback for becoming a growth engine: We are busy - the life of the carbon project together - need to be able to bring forward the milestones of a carbon project. Key Pieces of Feedback: Transparency Transparency with the operational procedure - "were busy running our own businesses, put together a piece so farmers have an understanding of key times and what is required by the farmer - i.e. a piece of collateral that reflects the project lifecycle" Project Milestones Contact points Regular touch points either en masse or 1:1 AgriProve needs to come in to guide the project and where it needs to go. Goal oriented: Validate that carbon sequestration is possible Was "Mr Skeptical" and wanted to road-test it, so others could take these thing on. Big gap between Operations and the Producer We need guide Tech notes that come with it as well - when sharing technical information from other projects - we haven't done this very well. Provide the farmer with simple takeaways: So the producer is able to communicate, or guide people in a process where they can verbalise their soil mission - how many tonnes we are trying to sequester. Education is needed regularly - e.g. webinars, seminars, tutorials. attend 3-4 webinars a year - so they're engaged with what is happening reality on pay-offs, discussing the newest content. Value Propositions for Customer Success and Recruitment Linkage between production and carbon building: improvements to farm, lead to increase in production, the co-benefit is carbon. Tags for tonnes helps with this as the co-benefits: Compared the Customer success challenge with Ruminati program - they provide a very strong user experience around Baselining and understanding where they're at; Integrates for day to day farming with the carbon project What does it mean being in a carbon project? Similar thinking to superannuation; payback period is significantly further down the line, but the need to regularly check in on progress is important Vital piece is providing a producer with a really simple, value proposition for starting know that shade is super important, improving water, shade, pasture utilisation The more we can break down those barriers for customer success, if we can get that right, participants will be happier with the model, the model is a bit fractured as a result of not setting clear agendas/milestones/guidance - what is working and not working when it comes to carbon building and production benefit. "what were not doing enough of, investing in the production model, but not investing enough time into learning how this relates this back to carbon farming." Long term goal: asset growth and a carbon project Short term goal: animal production and outcomes from that Align short-term to long-term goals, but adding value and clear linkage between short term and long term goals. AgriProve needs to become a producer-oriented organisation: What would the farmer tell the consumer? I'm in an accredited carbon project and using data driven insights to improve my farm Stakeholders: Processors, get a green premium when speaking with processors on ESG programs Banks: Potentially beneficial interest rate when engaging with an ESG Program Teys - Grasslands - they pay a premium for productivity JBS - pay a premium for being a steward of their land Processors - they are talking about the ESG program, but not sure what that program looks like: what sort of value they can give people how do we attach benefits to the 240 farmers, will they get a better rate at the bank? What if they got 0.2% better rate because they're joined to an ESG program with AgriProve. Consumers: Reason other tech companies he's worked with have been successful: AgriWebb gives you a stewardship program, but AgriProve does not - need collateral, AgriProve Environmental Farming Program. Chat with Justin RE: Ruminati (8th May 24) Ruminati provide tangible accounting of farm management decisions Moving from what we think we know to something visual and easy to interact with What value prop can we give our customers - something like this is perfect for client interaction We need to have an active mechanism to give this sort of information Currently our emissions discussions are not a good visual representation of management decisions (spreadsheet based) Wen need to (through a tool like this) give them (our landholders and prospects) active scenarios with calcs of how their management changes would effect their carbon balance We need to go on a competitor watch and see the partners they are creating (highly influential) - would give us massive market penetration to partner with Ruminati What does this really give a farmer? - speeds up the process to get a quicker result on the validation piece to their management This is what we are lacking in our offering - pathways to get to net a quicker result - how do we make it easier to do a carbon audit Gives our landholders a triple A rating - auditing - great baseline tool that is farmer and supply chain accepted + government validated emissions sequestration AP should do a validation every 6 months - would be significantly easier and less time consuming with a product such as this AgriProve could provide EOFY Ruminati report AP shouldn't want to replicate the same product - partner and make a commercial agreement - and make the exponential progress Look at who they are ready integrated to - leverage their network We are a $150,000 (300 clients at $500 each) client for 25 years - that's a huge value add for them Want to have tools in the tool box - already have ceres tags and the soil testing internally - this could be a great add-on Rumninati cover the negative aspect - emissions - why wouldn't we look to just buy them out? And tell the whole story Bring on their existing clients and tell the other half of the story Gotta tell the positive - they will want to bring that in their suite of products - they don't do the positive aspects but they are tied in to a suite of partners As a farmer with their service you pay just to know you are a polluter - let us tell your positive aspect - fill their gap with landholders they already have on-board Create a licence agreement or partnership or a pathway for integrating into their clientele Potential for a commercial subscription? Once landholders are signed up create a baseline score for them and give them the option to play with management scenarios Works hand in hand with our products Helps grass fed producers get better market access - we need to look at end producer - grassfed programs Justin sees holes in his story - these are hard to explain - this plugs a massive hole - need to work on our enemy (emissions story tellers) Go to end user - Coles - pitch our product to tell whole picture - negative and positive - do you want to know more - show them Ready Graze with carbon accounting Justin wants $0.20 more per every kg produced due to validation - hard to make a profit right now because of the market - needs to show something different More market access for the positive management the more money landholders can put into the management of their carbon project

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Spoke to Justin about the certification and sustainability piece. Gave great responses, very interested

Responses to sustainability questionnaire: Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? - Yes - GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy - If no, then why not? - N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? - GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management - How can we make the testing attractive and simple - Very honourous - Teas - JBS - TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? - Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? - If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business - Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? - Not direct to consumers - Have looked at the big supply chains - Looked into Greenham’s - Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand - Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? - TBD - Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to - Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals

Hi Justin, I hope you are going well! Lovely to chat to you last week about our research project with RMIT University, about our sampling study, the Australian Soil Carbon Sampling Optimisation Study. As discussed, please see attached the sampling plan, for your approval. RMIT would like to sample only CEA 1, the highest performing CEA, and to resample T0, T1, and T2 points to understand change over time. They would also like to sample 2 extra points at each point 1m and 2m out, like the diagram below, to gain and understanding of spatial variability at a high resolution. Also please note in the plan attached, not all labels are showing due to them being too close together. Please note that this will have no impact on your compliant project sampling rounds and this data is not shared with the regulator. However, this sampling may be used to assist us to better stratify your project to reduce variability within strata. Please let me know if you are happy with this plan. We aim to sample next week, and the guys will be in touch direct to arrange a time. We have also sent you a consent form via panda docs, to say that you are happy for AgriProve to share this data with RMIT for the purposes of the study. Thanks again for being part of the project and please feel free to give me a call if you’d like to discuss. Melanie

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Chatted to JC about his ACCUs and sharing his profile. He has an idea around the data we are collecting and wanting to create a provenance story using combined AP data and genomics. Looking to put together a proposal to articulate his ideas. Notes from meeting below: Need to validate outcomes Outcomes of carbon project aligned with high quality cattle management AgriProvenance - a failsafe system to prove the traceability Genomics - outcomes of the cattle (when the herd is at feed conversion) T4T, EOS, genomics = package to producers Genomically verify all the bulls - create auditable trails Prove the animals are the best ranking in a carbon sense Potentially use Gallagher / optiweigh and validate the measurements Collect the information and overlay into the program - herd/provenance Each animal verified through genomics, lifetime carbon project measured, kgs produced, kgs emitted, ongoing efficiencies - totalling a value MSA graded product vs reliability Whole of life information - green training wheels on the animal Breed outcome - market ready at a certain time Steer select - animals that will produce best on farm AgriProvenance , net emissions, credits, management strategy - making the farm very transparent Metrics - DOB Genomic testing $40 per head - data to make key decisions Give the data to make an assumption after birth (6 months) these are my highest ranking individuals - keep only the efficient animals on farm (carbon benefit based on efficiency) Improvement on feed efficiency and outcomes Making decisions based on long-term gains Is breeders are inefficient they enter the food supply Over the carbon project you have a high performing herd - go to for efficiencies AgriProvenance adds value to customer - health protocol, vaccine's, health status What AP has is soil - JC can provide the stable products Provenance also goes into the grains/timber, etc. Real tool is good outcomes Validation of bloodline, performance, and carbon story - QR to public page (T carbon produced, T carbon emitted, carbon story and ACCUs) Everything auditbale in a CP and passing audits Best practice and best management that is scalable Go and target Angus Australia

engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Justin, I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. As you will see in the attached document, your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note: This trend does not mean carbon has gone backwards, it shows the trend in vegetation greenness has been lower than your baseline average and therefore it is unlikely re sampling would be worthwhile at this time. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks and complete this phone check in? Talk soon. engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Mountain View/Page/Truss CPs
engagements.body: Dear Justin, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. All you need to do is print out the statement page, sign, and re-send, and I will compile the complete document, and send to you for your records. As discussed, these records will from the basis of every crediting application going forward, but now that we've got all the baseline records sorted, for future, all we need is the updated changes as they occur. The threshold is simple for your project, in that the change in complete uncontrolled grazing, to a controlled grazing approach is an eligible activity which will be continually implemented in all reporting periods going forwards. The evidence for this, is as simple as a plan for goat/cattle movement, and that you've upgraded fencing (compared to the baseline); which is easy to prove. MS Mat Silver 18 May, 22 Dear Adam I have recently been appointed as AgriProves first Farmer Liaison Manager. The establishment of this role is part of an increased focus on project implementation support to all our clients. I am getting in touch with you to outline just a few of the practical things we are doing to increase support for you and your soil carbon project. 1. An annual review cycle We are moving to an annual project review cycle that will involve us assessing indicators of soil carbon change and determining whether soil sampling is likely to demonstrate an increase in your carbon stocks. As you are hopefully aware, once baselined all soil monitoring and sampling costs are now covered by AgriProve. Your AgriProve Project Manager will be in contact with you to discuss where your project is at in its annual cycle and if necessary to arrange soil sampling. 2. Technical webinar series with Q&A There is so much going on in agriculture at the moment and much of it relates to practices that can increase soil carbon and farm productivity. We are putting together a list of topics that we will engage speakers to provide a webinar followed by a session to answer all your questions on the topic. Some speakers will be technical specialists and academics, others will be fellow land managers sharing their experience with a particular practice. It would be good to have a chat at some point if you have a chance? Regards, Adam Gunthorpe Tarramba Brahmans Ph: 0402 630 907 [cid:e185bb1c-d2ad-4e8c-94ab-f73852244caa] ________________________________ From: Dylan Jones Sent: Thursday, 13 February 2025 6:55 AM To: adam@tarramba.com Subject: AgriProve - Howson Carbon Projects 1, 5 and 9 Resampling Results Hi Adam, I hope you’re well. The team wishes to thank you for your assistance with organising the resampling on three of your soil carbon projects in November last year. The results from the sampling indicated that the soil carbon levels have not increased enough to warrant progressing through to the reporting and crediting process. I have attached reports showing the individual core values from the samples taken on the projects. Also included in the reports are the additional analysis results from the SAR grant. * Howson Carbon Project 1 has seen an improvement compared to the previous sampling conducted in 2023, although still a decrease relative to the baseline. * Howson Carbon Project 5 has seen a further decrease in carbon levels since 2023 and baseline. * Howson Carbon Project 9 has seen a further decrease in carbon levels since 2023 and baseline. While this may be disappointing, it is important to point out that soil carbon projects are a long-term investment, with increases in SOC often taking a long time to be achieved. I will be in touch by phone soon to discuss your results further and see if you have any questions about the results or the projects moving forward. Please feel free to call me sooner too if you wish. This is a key time in a carbon project as there is a number of things that we need to tick off to meet your reporting requirements that are due before this date. This includes an audit in which you will need to supply your management records, we will need to re-sample if that has not been completed since baselining , and we need consent from everyone on your land titles to participate in your project including the bank if you have a mortgage. We are currently working through these steps and will contact you in the very near future with more detail as we work through this process behind the scenes. For Now, Your first steps are we need to get the Eligible interest holders consent process started as this is the part that can take the longest of all of these. To get this started we just need you to answer a couple of quick questions below so we can get the ball rolling on this. Please reply answering these questions: 1. Has anything on your land title changed since you started the project? eg. sold, bought out, new partners, solar panels or power line companies operating on your land. No 3. Who is on your land titles? What are their names? eg. is it just you or also your partner, siblings ect. land is in Adam Gunthorpe name only 3. Do you have a mortgage on your farm? Yes 4. If yes, which bank are you with? NAB , second mortgage from Wallace Gunthorpe and Kate Gunthorpe 5. What is the name, email, branch and phone number of your bank manager? This is assuming 3.5 ACCUs/ha/year. * In terms of next steps, we would like to work closely with you to make best endeavours to ensure any incoming owners retain the projects and we can novate the agreement for these projects only to incoming owners. We are more than happy to provide any documentation, or speak/meet with any parties as required, whether it be interested parties, banks, or solicitors. * It is worth noting that there are no costs at all associated with incoming owners taking this on, as all baselining has been paid. Regarding implementation while it would be excellent if incoming owners were to continuing implementation of the eligible activities (eg. your grazing management), it is not an obligation. engagements.body: CS - Project Review - Year 2 + 1. Has the landholder received the results of their annual review and have next steps and timelines been communicated? Notes: Yes via email 19/05/2025 2. If re-sampling was completed has the landholder received their results and next steps been communicated depending on the result? Notes: Yes 3. Has implementation of the selected eligible activities as outlined in the Project Proposal and Carbon Project Plan begun? Note any positive or negative changes that have been observed since implementation. Notes: All standard practice now, all projects implemented into the rotational grazing system. 5. For each of the eligible activities described above, please describe over what area these activities have been completed on a per project basis. For example: Project Name/Number: Eligible Activity: Implemented area %: Notes: 100% 6. What plans are there to continue implementation of these eligible activities over the next 6 months? Notes: Continue as planned 7. Have any of the restricted or prohibited activities been conducted since the last project review? Refer to the CPP or LMS for a description of these activities. Notes: None 8. If altering the stocking rate is chosen as an eligible activity: - What is the current average grazing duration per paddock? - What is the target rest period? - What is the average paddock size? Notes: All recorded in Maia Grazing. 9. How are records of the implementation of these activities being kept (farm management software, hand-written notes, spreadsheets)? Notes: All paddock treatments recorded in Maia grazing 10. Have there been any changes or unforeseen events that impact your carbon project areas since the start of your project (such as additional infrastructure, tree plantings, land sale, bushfire, flood)? Nothing happening at the moment.

engagements.subject: Tags for Tonnes Update and Webinar
engagements.body: Good afternoon Tony, Happy Beef Week! I hope you and the family are doing well. I thought I would provide you an update on AgriProve's Tags for Tonnes, and provide you some of the thoughts expressed from a early participant in the program. Here's our latest webinar where you can hear the insights gained already by one of our early participants, Justin Costello: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dO20F2IcxSo [cid:9b0f43b8-d8f1-443f-a265-ef701d8f8a65] Tags for Tonnes Webinar - Unlocking Your Farms Potential www.youtube.com AgriProve has been roaring along with the Tags for Tonnes program delivering actionable insights for landholders involved in carbon projects. The software is already providing the best in-class translation of the insights offered through Ceres Tags. We are now developing additional insights to complement those currently available. Watch this space for upcoming features: * Digitised hands-free and objective grazing diary (no data inputs required). * Pasture health monitoring - assistive satellite indices focussed on pasture health and rest and recovery, to assist your grazing rotations for optimal pasture to carbon conversion. * Additional IoT integrations. I hope everything is going well on farm and that you are happy, healthy and profitable. Have a great week!! engagements.subject: Tags for Tonnes Update and Webinar
engagements.body: Good afternoon Tony, Happy Beef Week! I hope you and the family are doing well. I thought I would provide you an update on AgriProve's Tags for Tonnes, and provide you some of the thoughts expressed from a early participant in the program. Here's our latest webinar where you can hear the insights gained already by one of our early participants, Justin Costello: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dO20F2IcxSo [cid:9b0f43b8-d8f1-443f-a265-ef701d8f8a65] Tags for Tonnes Webinar - Unlocking Your Farms Potential www.youtube.com AgriProve has been roaring along with the Tags for Tonnes program delivering actionable insights for landholders involved in carbon projects. The software is already providing the best in-class translation of the insights offered through Ceres Tags. We are now developing additional insights to complement those currently available. Watch this space for upcoming features: * Digitised hands-free and objective grazing diary (no data inputs required). * Pasture health monitoring - assistive satellite indices focussed on pasture health and rest and recovery, to assist your grazing rotations for optimal pasture to carbon conversion. * Additional IoT integrations. I hope everything is going well on farm and that you are happy, healthy and profitable. Have a great week!! engagements.subject: AgriProve - Lynch Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Hi Derek, Thank you for your patience with us completing your annual review. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The increase from the previous period to the current period has not met our threshold (shown in the attached report), we will not be resampling this year. Your project will be reviewed again next year. Note that we have a requirement under the method to sample your project a minimum of once every five years. I am working on the other items that we discussed on Friday regarding T0-T1 results and an overlay of your paddocks with the carbon project boundaries. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Morning Derek, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon project. We do these every 12 months using satellite imagery of the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) on your farm to get an idea of if the vegetation has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample at this time. As you will see in the attached document, your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it means that compared to baseline the average trend has not be positive comparatively - which is an indicator that carbon sequestration has been unlikely at this time. This result means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. We will review this again next year or when our HORIZON model is fully up and running to decide if resampling would be worthwhile then. if you have any questions or would like to touch base about your carbon project- feel free to call me anytime. From: Stephen Warnken Sent: Tuesday, 3 March 2026 12:14 PM To: 'Koolah Trust' Subject: RE: ACCU Distribution - Lynch Carbon Project Hi Derek, Thank you for your letter of 27 February 2026. We have reviewed your position carefully and write to respond formally in relation to the Additional Project Work and Services Fee for baseline soil sampling services under the Agreement. The Agreed Fee We respectfully disagree with the position set out in your letter. The terms of Schedule 3 of the Agreement are clear and unambiguous. The agreed Additional Project Work and Services Fee for Baseline Soil Sampling Services is stated as: “750 ACCUs @ $6.66” The fee is denominated in ACCUs. The figure of $6.66 per ACCU recorded in Schedule 3 reflects the prevailing risk-adjusted ACCU reference price at the time the Agreement was executed in November 2020. It was included to provide context as to the dollar-equivalent value of the fee at that time – consistent with how the Agreement records carbon pricing more broadly (as identified in Schedule 1). It does not, and was never intended to, convert the fee into a fixed dollar obligation or to cap AgriProve’s entitlement at a dollar value. There is no mechanism in the Agreement to convert an ACCU entitlement into a variable dollar amount based on prevailing spot prices at the time of issuance. Commitments Made in Reliance on the Agreement In discharging its responsibilities under the Agreement, and in good faith reliance on the terms of Schedule 3, AgriProve entered into downstream obligations and commitments that have already required the delivery of ACCUs from this project. Those commitments were made on the reasonable assumption that AgriProve would receive the ACCUs to which it is contractually entitled. To the extent those obligations have now been enforced, AgriProve has complied with them in full. AgriProve’s Position That said, we believe the most practical and sensible time to resolve the allocation of ACCUs under Schedule 3 is at the point of the next project issuance, when ACCUs are available for distribution. We propose that both parties defer this discussion until that time, at which point we can meet to agree the final allocation in light of ACCUs issued and the terms of the Agreement. Next Steps AgriProve will be in touch ahead of the next issuance to arrange a suitable time to discuss. In the meantime, if you have any questions or wish to raise anything further, please do not hesitate to contact me. engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Lynch CP
engagements.body: Dear Derek, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. Hi Adam, I hope you are going well. I will be joining the visit tomorrow, and am really looking forward to meeting you in person! We have received your results for the RMIT project soil sampling and have mapped them so you can see the spatial variability. Please see attached the results and maps of the various tests completed. This is the first time we have visualised results in this way. Please let me know of any feedback or changes that would make these more valuable for you. As mentioned previously, this dataset provides a sand pit for RMIT to do experiments and various sampling scenarios, the aim being to improve our physical sampling protocols. Happy to discuss further tomorrow if you have any questions. Thanks again for taking part in the project. Melanie

Hi Adam, I hope you are having a great week! Lovely to meet you in person a couple of weeks ago, thanks again for having us. Please see attached your updated results maps for the RMIT project sampling. The method used for the visualisation is called Inverse Distance Weighted, Manual Interval. This extrapolates the results over the whole project area. We have included the points so you can see how this method has extrapolated over the broader area. We also get a lot of questions on the moisture vs gravimetric water tests - The moisture % is reported on a dry basis = (wet weight – dry weight) / dry weight. Whilst the gravimetric water is the loss of mass in grams on drying at 105 degrees C. As they are reported on a different basis you cannot calculate the moisture % from the gravimetric water. Any questions please give me a bell. Mel

Had a meeting to review Crop monitoring functionality. Assessed differences in paddocks, veg indices and use cases. Also assessed respoinse to various grazes and rainfall - rest interval interactions. some insights were: Need an index that can assess chlorophyll across varying canopy heights (his stockpiles have huge biomass and chlorophyll content but scoring low) Need an indicator of biomass density 7.5 on RECI is probably his ideal grazing point his ideal grazing interval is 84 days - typically to hit high pasture quality He would love to have RECI integrated as a suggestion and let the landholder input their optimal point to graze + the capacity to input ideal rest interval Mentioned that farmers are trying to adapt to infrequent very high intensity rainfall events - he is using ripping as a technique to assist Has just performed subsoil ripping to assist soil infiltration down to 250mm deep and is seeding clover, chukery, and others. Has just put in some of the new tags on the mob yesterday

engagements.subject: CERES TAG data issue update
engagements.body: Good evening Adam, I’d like to provide an update on the data matter appearing since activation on your new batch of CERES RANCH Tags. We were the first to report an issue showing our diligence and care towards your projects. In summary, in March 2024, CERES TAG had firmware updated with a new design from CSIRO to improve battery life, accuracy, reliability and flexibility to update with additional algorithms. The Pasture Feed Intake (PFI) was not anticipated to operate differently from the previous firmware on this updated and improved model, however this was not the case. The team at CERES TAG and CSIRO are working to remedy the algorithm now to restore to performance equivalent to that pre-March. This week a patch fix was deployed to in-field testing. There is no issue with the GPS location data. Your animal location monitoring is unaffected. As we learn more about their progress towards a resolution, we will keep you informed. We thank you for your support, understanding and patience. If you have any questions, don’t hesitate to contact me. engagements.subject: Questions from todays sustainability convo
engagements.body: Evening Adam thank you for being so generous with your time today. Below are the answers, please feel free to add anything you may think of. Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? * No * Very, very limited amount * Someone else doing sustainability certification – biology outsomes and plant outcomes If no, then why not? * Not really Would you want to explore the criteria to have a sustainability certification applied to your produce? * Yep Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? engagements.body: Hi Adam, Hope things are travelling well in the Rabjohn's household at the moment. As one of our pioneering landholders you are often trying new things ahead of the crowd. These test and trials are often of great value to our other landholders and interesting for those considering a carbon project. To that end I wanted to formally check in on what you are, and most importantly aren't comfortable sharing. We have quite the repository of great imagery and maps of your property! I've attached a piece that I would like your consent to use in promotional material. The document is our new Carbon Ready Report (CRR). The reports assess the carbon sequestration potential of land, so that landholders have an idea of what they might be able to achieved with commitment to improved land management before starting a project. engagements.subject: Call with Adam Rabjohns
engagements.body: Spoke to Adam Rabjohns about the arrival of his Optiweigh unit. Optiweigh has arrived and in paddock. Main motivations being to remove guess work out of management - the data providing him with a guide to adaptive management and understanding if some of his mob are ready for AI. Couldn't be more stoked about the unit and the animals seem to love the protein supplement.

Reached out to Adam via Whatsapp to see if he was happy to chat to a prospect of Bill's who wants to speak to someone who has introduced dung beetles. Happy to chat with them and also shared a post from his FB about the topic. His FB is a great resource for management practice we would like to encourage. https://www.facebook.com/share/p/jL1bcbjYEox4LRgB/

Adam is redesigning his paddocks so he can intensify grazing and allow for automation (fence lifters) - to facilitate 3 moves + per day. Blue lines = permanent water lane - can walk back through areas grazed without having to access/overgraze other paddocks Green lines = permanent electric fencing (150m wide) Mob is 240 cows with 240 calves - get 3 chunks (paddock rotations) per day - 8am, 12pm, 6pm Rotations dependent on rain, grass and rest - currently paddocks they are grazing now are 100+ days rest (Some areas of them are even more) - recovery on some areas due to low spring rains are only just happening.

engagements.subject: Call with Adam Rabjohns
engagements.body: Notes stored.

Called Adam to let him know about the platform launch and his Ready Graze account being integrated. Feedback as follows: sign up to platform was quick and easy has been hearing about rewards for farmers ($20 / head) for adopting feed supplements (asparagopsis) and wanted to know who provides that and why (is it market driven or gvt) tags are not relevant to his situation - they are just another data source with little use, because he is physically seeing and moving them every day they have no real advantage - data is too descript with no0 real outcome context Optiweigh is incredibly useful for adaptive management and understanding how they are performing and where to improve dung beetles on farm are popping out everywhere and exploding in numbers

Had a recent chat with Adam notes as follows: He is no longer using the Optiweigh unit and is open to us gifting it to someone else The reason is he is grazing too intensively and can't keep up with the labour requirements to move that frequently @Claudia Bryant he is a great manager moving 3 times a day using a Total grazing approach (super high density, single mob (420 head over 1ha) he has just re-fenced his farm to facilitate strip grazing so he can utilise automatic fence lifters to facilitate the 3 moves per day

engagements.subject: Call with Adam Rabjohns
engagements.body: Spoke with Adam - notes recorded

Notes from Convo with AR today (were texting about Optiweigh usage): Animals trashing the non-ground covered areas - bogging it up Bought a drone a week ago - putting out clover seed and foliar nutrients - T50 DJI - 50kg of seed Fully automated and do some targeted foliar application Done sap analysis on the plant - John Kemp just released AI - put sap analysis into the AI which reads and tells what they need to do,- utilised with his soil analysis as well No urea, calcium, phosphorus … He does deficiency testing and provides a method of attack Ended up being $3.50/ha (would have been $40/ha) FieldLark AI - totally useful and gives info on how it is thinking (reasoning) Everything they are talking about (John Kempf and co.) is to increase the photosynthesis - to push the liquid carbon pathway Adam feels like they have the Total Grazing downpacked - can spend more time focussing the photosynthesis Total grazing - trying to make sure they are balancing the supplements and not smashing the grass too hard to balance the body condition and feed remaining So many farms around them with absolutely no grass - poor spring and autumn - they (the neighbours) are letting them out all over the place and the head are smashing anything that sprouts out Things are tight right now - really gotta make sure they are getting the timing of their graze right Animal condition is best they have seen it in a long time Right now - they have just started into the stock pile - just cleaned up anything in the growing season - never had less stockpile But as many animals as they have ever had Feed/ pasture is super dense in the places that aren't gravel country - feet are sinking 100mm into the ground - never felt soils so soft Stock pile is so much softer than they have ever experienced (On waiting for credits) All the indicators are pointing towards sequestration - he can see it - they are just waiting for the carbon to kick off - just need one reliable season Rain has been really good recently - not too intense (40mm in one night the other night) Optiweigh Found some utility - with the calves - incredibly helpful Hard to figure out if they are going ahead (before) - nice to have the data to see it With the cows it's less of an issue (figuring out if they are improving) and they are harder to measure as they venture all over the place - calves stick in a tight mob He is putting it near the water point Using a salt and lupens lick When it rains and gets wet the herd didn't wanna go near it Potential to integrate with FieldLark? + provides pathway to encourage extra analyte analysis Post about this here: Dylan Cronje: Feedback from Adam Rabjohns and an AI agronomy solution | AgriProve Product > Product General | Microsoft Teams

engagements.subject: CERES TAG data issue update
engagements.body: Good evening Adam, I’d like to provide an update on the data matter appearing since activation on your new batch of CERES RANCH Tags. We were the first to report an issue showing our diligence and care towards your projects. In summary, in March 2024, CERES TAG had firmware updated with a new design from CSIRO to improve battery life, accuracy, reliability and flexibility to update with additional algorithms. The Pasture Feed Intake (PFI) was not anticipated to operate differently from the previous firmware on this updated and improved model, however this was not the case. The team at CERES TAG and CSIRO are working to remedy the algorithm now to restore to performance equivalent to that pre-March. This week a patch fix was deployed to in-field testing. There is no issue with the GPS location data. Your animal location monitoring is unaffected. As we learn more about their progress towards a resolution, we will keep you informed. We thank you for your support, understanding and patience. If you have any questions, don’t hesitate to contact me. engagements.subject: Questions from todays sustainability convo
engagements.body: Evening Adam thank you for being so generous with your time today. Below are the answers, please feel free to add anything you may think of. Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? * No * Very, very limited amount * Someone else doing sustainability certification – biology outsomes and plant outcomes If no, then why not? * Wasn’t sure how to get value from it * Not direct selling so criteria you he needs to meet is more what the processors want – grass fed/ * Not a sustainability credential to give you more money through * Teys Wagga Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? * Not really Would you want to explore the criteria to have a sustainability certification applied to your produce? * Yep Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? * Yeah – need to be some kind of payback for it – need to see the return Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? engagements.subject: Consent request - use of Leeston farm maps in promotional material
engagements.body: Hi Adam, Hope things are travelling well in the Rabjohn's household at the moment. As one of our pioneering landholders you are often trying new things ahead of the crowd. These test and trials are often of great value to our other landholders and interesting for those considering a carbon project. To that end I wanted to formally check in on what you are, and most importantly aren't comfortable sharing. We have quite the repository of great imagery and maps of your property! I've attached a piece that I would like your consent to use in promotional material. The document is our new Carbon Ready Report (CRR). The reports assess the carbon sequestration potential of land, so that landholders have an idea of what they might be able to achieved with commitment to improved land management before starting a project. To promote the CRR we would like to have a dummy report that can be shared with prospects. In preparing the dummy I have used your farm maps. On the first page the map includes the name "Woodhouselee road" so makes it location-identifiable. This is my key concern and reason for checking in with you. Can you please confirm that you are happy for us to use this dummy report. It will not reference you or your property - it will just be the maps that are potentially identifiable. Happy to discuss this or any question you have on this. And as always thanks for your continued support!
