engagements.subject: Call with Adam Rabjohns
engagements.body: Spoke to Adam Rabjohns about the arrival of his Optiweigh unit. Optiweigh has arrived and in paddock. Main motivations being to remove guess work out of management - the data providing him with a guide to adaptive management and understanding if some of his mob are ready for AI. Couldn't be more stoked about the unit and the animals seem to love the protein supplement.

Reached out to Adam via Whatsapp to see if he was happy to chat to a prospect of Bill's who wants to speak to someone who has introduced dung beetles. Happy to chat with them and also shared a post from his FB about the topic. His FB is a great resource for management practice we would like to encourage. https://www.facebook.com/share/p/jL1bcbjYEox4LRgB/

Adam is redesigning his paddocks so he can intensify grazing and allow for automation (fence lifters) - to facilitate 3 moves + per day. Blue lines = permanent water lane - can walk back through areas grazed without having to access/overgraze other paddocks Green lines = permanent electric fencing (150m wide) Mob is 240 cows with 240 calves - get 3 chunks (paddock rotations) per day - 8am, 12pm, 6pm Rotations dependent on rain, grass and rest - currently paddocks they are grazing now are 100+ days rest (Some areas of them are even more) - recovery on some areas due to low spring rains are only just happening.

engagements.subject: Call with Adam Rabjohns
engagements.body: Notes stored.

Called Adam to let him know about the platform launch and his Ready Graze account being integrated. Feedback as follows: sign up to platform was quick and easy has been hearing about rewards for farmers ($20 / head) for adopting feed supplements (asparagopsis) and wanted to know who provides that and why (is it market driven or gvt) tags are not relevant to his situation - they are just another data source with little use, because he is physically seeing and moving them every day they have no real advantage - data is too descript with no0 real outcome context Optiweigh is incredibly useful for adaptive management and understanding how they are performing and where to improve dung beetles on farm are popping out everywhere and exploding in numbers

Had a recent chat with Adam notes as follows: He is no longer using the Optiweigh unit and is open to us gifting it to someone else The reason is he is grazing too intensively and can't keep up with the labour requirements to move that frequently @Claudia Bryant he is a great manager moving 3 times a day using a Total grazing approach (super high density, single mob (420 head over 1ha) he has just re-fenced his farm to facilitate strip grazing so he can utilise automatic fence lifters to facilitate the 3 moves per day

engagements.subject: Call with Adam Rabjohns
engagements.body: Spoke with Adam - notes recorded

Notes from Convo with AR today (were texting about Optiweigh usage): Animals trashing the non-ground covered areas - bogging it up Bought a drone a week ago - putting out clover seed and foliar nutrients - T50 DJI - 50kg of seed Fully automated and do some targeted foliar application Done sap analysis on the plant - John Kemp just released AI - put sap analysis into the AI which reads and tells what they need to do,- utilised with his soil analysis as well No urea, calcium, phosphorus … He does deficiency testing and provides a method of attack Ended up being $3.50/ha (would have been $40/ha) FieldLark AI - totally useful and gives info on how it is thinking (reasoning) Everything they are talking about (John Kempf and co.) is to increase the photosynthesis - to push the liquid carbon pathway Adam feels like they have the Total Grazing downpacked - can spend more time focussing the photosynthesis Total grazing - trying to make sure they are balancing the supplements and not smashing the grass too hard to balance the body condition and feed remaining So many farms around them with absolutely no grass - poor spring and autumn - they (the neighbours) are letting them out all over the place and the head are smashing anything that sprouts out Things are tight right now - really gotta make sure they are getting the timing of their graze right Animal condition is best they have seen it in a long time Right now - they have just started into the stock pile - just cleaned up anything in the growing season - never had less stockpile But as many animals as they have ever had Feed/ pasture is super dense in the places that aren't gravel country - feet are sinking 100mm into the ground - never felt soils so soft Stock pile is so much softer than they have ever experienced (On waiting for credits) All the indicators are pointing towards sequestration - he can see it - they are just waiting for the carbon to kick off - just need one reliable season Rain has been really good recently - not too intense (40mm in one night the other night) Optiweigh Found some utility - with the calves - incredibly helpful Hard to figure out if they are going ahead (before) - nice to have the data to see it With the cows it's less of an issue (figuring out if they are improving) and they are harder to measure as they venture all over the place - calves stick in a tight mob He is putting it near the water point Using a salt and lupens lick When it rains and gets wet the herd didn't wanna go near it Potential to integrate with FieldLark? + provides pathway to encourage extra analyte analysis Post about this here: Dylan Cronje: Feedback from Adam Rabjohns and an AI agronomy solution | AgriProve Product > Product General | Microsoft Teams

engagements.subject: Re: The Grove - Soil Carbon Analysis
engagements.body: Hi Laurence, Thanks for your time over the phone just now. 1. Consent to Register As mentioned, the Consent to Register Document is a non-obligatory option that allows us to register a project on behalf of the landholder. It allows us to perform deeper project scoping and register a project. Eligible Activity: Alter stocking rate, duration or intensity of grazing would accurately represent this clients intention to build soil carbon, given your comments below around employing a rotational grazing strategy to maximise the soil carbon potential. 1. Returns In terms of outlining the returns with a Soil Carbon Project, we see the following: * ACCU creation. I would suggest anywhere from 1-3 ACCUs / Ha / year based on client and internal assessment. Again, this is dependant on management and seasonality (rainfall) * Agronomic outcomes. Building soil cover will help improve ground cover, water retention and allow for higher stocking capacity. * Green premiums on commodities. 1. Baselining Sampling Fee Estimated at ~$20-25,000 based on a preliminary 500 Ha of eligible soil carbon project area (based on 25% EP and other exclusions) This payment can be deferred for 5 years interest free and paid back in ACCUs. Next steps, @Kieren Whittock 's team will supply preliminary maps (similar to those you've sent us) outlining the soil carbon opportunity. From there, we will be able to move forward with registering a project once the Consent documents are signed and returns. Any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me. engagements.subject: FW: Variation of ERF170337 Barwick Carbon Project 4 [SEC=OFFICIAL]

engagements.body: QTR Check - 19/11/2024 - OPS010 - Project Monitoring and Reporting 1. Eligible activities: · Applying nutrients · Retaining stubble 2. Has your selected management activities been actively implemented over the last 3 months? No nutrients put on in the last 3 months, season not good enough to put anything onto crops. Have put 4t CalciPrill over 80ha (50kg/ha) on to pasture paddocks on project 2. 3. What is your plan to implement these management activities for the next 3 months? Usually apply gypsum every march where beans are planted and lime every second year, around 150ha. Have sprayed out project 2 and transitioning to crop. 4. Has the implementation of these activities been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? Yes, new. 5. Over what proportion of your overall project area have these activities been implemented to date? 25% on project 2 only. 6. What is the Average Grazing duration per paddock target? (time, days) {*Grazing Projects only} 12-month period 7. How long is your rest period target? {*Grazing Projects only} 3 years, aiming for a 4-year rotation of crops and then grazed off. 8. What is the Average Size in Hectares per paddock? {*Grazing Projects only} 40ha 9. How are you keeping records of these management activities (farm management software, hand-written notes, spreadsheet)? AgWorld for all cropping, fert/chemical. No notes taken for the sheep. Just buy the sheep in and fatten them and sell them. 10. Have you observed any positive or negative changes in your operation since implementing these activities (for example increased productivity, improved soil health)? No noticeable changes in the last 6 months, although plants did look more robust, improved vigor with the VAM seed coating. Lack of rain lately. 11. Have you been impacted by any unforeseen circumstances related to your carbon project over the last 3 months (such as bushfire, flood, drought)? None. 12. Have there been any changes to your carbon project area over the last quarter (such as additional infrastructure, tree plantings)? None. 13. Is there anything further AgriProve can do to assist in the operation of your soil carbon project? Happy so far, Harry at LawrieCo has been keeping him up to date.

engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Barwick CPs
engagements.body: Dear Geoff and Donna, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. engagements.body: Hi Jackie and Morgan, Thank you very much for your patience while I came back to you with the additional information we require after our call last week. To assist with the project scoping process, I would like into introduce Ben Payne, Account Manager at AgriProve, who will be helping to bring all the information together for your final project proposal. At this stage could you please: Check that all property boundaries have been included in the below maps. If land titles have been missed, please identify them. Provided the AgriWebb paddock map KML. files for the properties. Confirm the total hectares that single super and lime were applied to for each year from 2020-2025. Confirm that the average stocking rate was 575 Breeders, 575 Calves, 10 Bulls for 2020-2025? Could you please provide either AgriWebb stock data or stock numbers based on the sale data for 2020-2025? (Why? Although the average numbers will be great for project registration. It will be important to have more exact numbers for later emissions accounting purposes.) Can you please provide the hectares of improve pasture each year from 2020-2025 and if applicable the number of hectares tillage each year and number of passes (direct drilling doesn't count as tillage but ploughing or scarifying for a oat pasture might be examples). If you have any questions, please feel free to ring as this can often save a lot of time and hassle for you. Once we have this information we look forward to commencing the mapping process. engagements.subject: National Carbon Farming Conference in Albury, 3–6 Nov
engagements.body: Hi Jacklyn, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is on in Albury from 3rd to 6th November. This conference is Australia’s leading event connecting farmers, science, and carbon markets - now with an even sharper focus on practical, profitable soil carbon solutions for your farm. It’s a great opportunity to hear from other producers and get practical updates on soil carbon and emissions reduction. AgriProve will be there this year. Our Chair, Matthew Warnken, will be helping MC some of the sessions, and we’re co-sponsoring Soil Carbon Day on the Tuesday. If you’re planning to head along, it would be great to catch up and talk about how a soil carbon project could work on your farm. AgriProve delivers issuance of 9,214 Australian Carbon Credit Units (ACCUs) in Tarramba QLD * Howson Carbon Projects 7 and 14 in Tarramba, QLD, have generated a combined total of 9,214 Australian Carbon Credit Units (ACCUs) under the ACCU Scheme. * The projects were registered with the ERF in March of 2022 and cover 550 hectares of a larger grazing enterprise with annual average rainfall of 620mm. * AgriProve has 59 projects with validated measured increases in soil carbon across its portfolio under the 2021 methodology. 7th June 2024: The Howson Carbon Project, part of the Gunthorpe Cattle Company/Tarramba Brahmans grazing enterprise, incorporates 15 individual soil carbon projects. The first two to show validated measured increases have generated a combined total of 9,214 ACCUs under the ACCU Scheme in a partnership with AgriProve, Australia’s leading carbon soiltech developer. Utilising AgriProve’s innovative, digitally enabled Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) model the projects benefited from the expedited soil sampling and carbon crediting process. The SOC model which combines satellite imagery with ground-truthed measurement more accurately predicts changes in SOC attributed to on-farm management practices. The result is AgriProve partnering landholders can be issued ACCUs in two years instead of five. Landholders Adam and Tracy Gunthorpe run 3,000 head of cattle with 900 breeding cows across 20,000 acres in central Queensland. From: Lucy Vincent Sent: Wednesday, July 3, 2024 12:15 PM To: Will Frecheville Subject: Re: EIH - Collings Query Thanks Will, Firstly some logistics: Can you confirm the date you received this advice from Luke please? I need to reference the date. Can I get a copy of the reference number for the project please? I need to include this as part of seeking a review of the decision. I will also need a copy of the full email or letter response from Luke rather than just a copy of an insert as I need to attach it to the application. As discussed I will provide you and Kieran a copy of the request before I submit it. However I have 28 days from the date of the advice from Luke to submit. We are currently able to offer a deferred payment option for the baseline sampling. This allows us to complete the sampling for no upfront cost to you, with the equivalent sampling cost taken from ACCUs once they are generated by the project. Please note that if sufficient ACCUs are not generated after 5 years to cover the baselining costs, this will need to be repaid in the dollar amount. Could you please respond to this email and confirm which payment option you would prefer: 1. Pay for the sampling upfront at a total cost of $7000 +GST 1.
